Cosm rides premium moviegoing wave with more immersive screenings and a wider library

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The next significant thing in premium large format theatrical viewing takes inspiration from the stars.
  • Cosm, an immersive entertainment technology organization, got its start programming planetariums — its name a combination of "cosmos" and "colosseum." The company's massive, domed screens first offered guests a view of the universe, now they mimic courtside seats at sports venues around the world and drop film fans into some of Hollywood's most iconic sets.
  • In a recent development, at a time when the theatrical industry is seeing its biggest growth from the sale of premium large format, or PLF, tickets, Cosm seeks to offer a fresh take on an elevated viewing experience.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The next significant thing in premium large format theatrical viewing takes inspiration from the stars.

Cosm, an immersive entertainment technology organization, got its start programming planetariums — its name a combination of "cosmos" and "colosseum." The company's massive, domed screens first offered guests a view of the universe, now they mimic courtside seats at sports venues around the world and drop film fans into some of Hollywood's most iconic sets.

In a recent development, at a time when the theatrical industry is seeing its biggest growth from the sale of premium large format, or PLF, tickets, Cosm seeks to offer a fresh take on an elevated viewing experience. And it's promptly expanding both its footprint and its content library.

Since 2024, Cosm has opened four theaters — near Los Angeles, Dallas, Atlanta and Detroit — with a Cleveland hub set to open in 2027. These experimental venues have garnered the attention of sports fans, screening live matchups in an arena-like environment. Showings often sell out, according to Cosm.

More recently, Cosm has partnered with Hollywood studios like Warner Bros., now a part of Skydance, to bring the likes of "The Matrix," "Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory," "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" and "It" to its locations. Cosm recently signed a deal with Universal, which will bring "Shrek" to its domes in December.

The agreements mark a lucrative newly introduced chapter for the privately held Cosm, expanding its audience reach and viewing opportunities beyond timed, live events.

As a privately held company, Cosm doesn't disclose its financials. Tickets cost anywhere from $18 for a matinee to around $70 for prime seats or in-demand showings. That doesn't include added fees for concessions or items from special, themed menus tied to screenings.

Sony invested $100 million in the company in June, taking a minority stake and placing Sony Pictures Entertainment Chairman and CEO Ravi Ahuja onto its board of directors.

Cosm also counts among its investors Cosm chairman Steve Winn's firm, Mirasol Capital; former Milwaukee Bucks co-owner Marc Lasry's Avenue Sports Fund; Rocket Mortgage co-founder Dan Gilbert's Rock; and David Blitzer, managing partner of the New Jersey Devils and Philadelphia 76ers, who invested through his firm Bolt Ventures.

Recent findings suggest that "Cosm is really early in its growth trajectory at the moment, and we saw an opportunity to partner with the tech giant at, what I would say is at, a very crucial stage in its development," Jay Levine, chief strategy and business operations officer at Sony, told CNBC. "They have about five locations with the goal of a pretty significant rollout. And the real reason why we did it was it gave us a lot of exposure to a growing distribution and what we deem an experiential platform that we think has long-term potential.".

Sources indicate that sony has made several plays in the theatrical space in recent years. It bought Alamo Drafthouse in 2024 and entered a long-term lease to reopen and restore the iconic Cinerama Dome in Los Angeles in July of this year.

In a recent development, "Our experiences strategy is around tech, it's around fandom, and it's around new and innovative approaches to content distribution," Levine remarked. "For us, we're all about these differentiated experiences.".

Cosm's 87-foot-diameter, concave screens drop viewers into the middle of the action, whether it's an NFL game or inside the world of "The Matrix." The firm's forthcoming Cleveland location will have an even bigger dome, at 100 feet in diameter.

The experience is akin to that of the Sphere in Las Vegas, which has garnered headlines since opening in 2023 for hosting high-profile concerts and events.

In a recent development, "People absolutely love to live out what they love in fandom, just like wearing a sports jersey," Alexis Scalice, head of Cosm Studios, told CNBC. "And I love that I'm seeing that same behavior happen with cinema.".

Stadium-style seating is nestled within each Cosm dome, with booths and tables set on each level. The dome's width is such that it fills much of the viewer's periphery, giving the sensation that they are part of the on-screen environment.

The Los Angeles and Dallas locations have capacity for around 350 seats each, while the newer domes in Atlanta and Detroit have up to 500 available seats. Cosm has not shared how many seats the Cleveland location will have, but with its larger screen it is expected to have a larger number of seats.

For live sports events, Cosm has specialty cameras mounted in arenas that broadcast back to the dome, creating the illusion of being on the field of play.

For theatrical features, the film is played in a large rectangle in the center of the dome and the background is transformed to extend the scene.

In Cosm's presentation of "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone," for example, during the iconic scene where thousands of Hogwarts acceptance letters flood through the fireplace and into a living room, the background is swarmed with animated envelopes.

Cosm has partnered with experiential production tech giant Little Cinema and creative studio MakeMake to create the visuals and environments for each scene of a film released in the dome. From storyboarding to post-production, this process can take up to a year as Cosm, the participating studio and the visual effects artists craft and render each moment.

"We really work hard not to take away from the story, so the film remains the hero in the narrative," Scalice noted. "Working very closely with Warner Bros. and our creative partners to make sure that we're not detracting too much from the story, but we're enhancing those moments for more elevated emotional response.".

With the exception of "It," which was released in 2017, Cosm's theatrical offerings thus far have been films that were released decades ago and that typically have long-established fan bases.

That helps Cosm leverage what Scalice called "that nostalgia factor" — "parents coming in that ... grew up on this, and they want to share it with their children.".

"We can reinvigorate these legendary films," she added.

In a recent development, cosm has dabbled across genres — horror, fantasy, science fiction — and also demographics — family-friendly and R-rated. "Shrek," set to debut Dec. 16, will be its first foray into animation.

"The thing that's so incredible about it is everybody thought initially it's just going to be working for sports, and when you look at what they've done, a lot of the titles with 'Harry Potter,' with 'Shrek,' and some of the other ones, I mean, the fill rates are actually incredible," Sony's Levine remarked.

Studios and theatrical exhibitors alike are looking for innovative ways to showcase Hollywood's product to moviegoers, especially as major shifts in viewing habits have disrupted the business.

In the post-pandemic era, the cinema space has been defined by fewer screens and fewer moviegoers, but those declines have been masked by higher movie ticket prices, particularly for PLF experiences.

These elevated offerings — think Imax, Dolby Cinema, ScreenX and 4DX — have bigger screens and better sound or introduce a unique experience, such as moving seats and fog machines. They're particularly popular with Gen Z and millennials, who've yet to be deterred by rising average ticket prices.

While an average standard movie ticket costs around $13, premium tickets average more than $18 each, according to data from EntTelligence.

Prices for Cosm's events fluctuate based on showtime and venue. Sony's Levine mentioned the company's ticket prices and attendance rates are "higher than I think anybody really would have thought.".

Unlike Cosm's sports offerings, which can also be viewed from outside the dome from its hall and deck viewing areas at a lower price, theatrical presentations are only available in the dome.

"They have no problem selling these tickets because people want to experience these things, like an immersive format," said Mike Polydoros, CEO at cinema marketing firm PaperAirplane Media. "That is something they can't get at home.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that TL;DR: Burger King Italy is offering a €19.90 Magic: The Gathering meal with a Whopper deck box and 100 sleeves through Nov.
  • Trading card games and fast-food menus make a natural pair.
  • The promotion is exclusive to Burger King locations in Italy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that TL;DR: Burger King Italy is offering a €19.90 Magic: The Gathering meal with a Whopper deck box and 100 sleeves through Nov. 30 — and international players are already hunting down the gear on eBay.

Trading card games and fast-food menus make a natural pair. Now, Wizards of the Coast is stepping into the drive-thru with an official Magic: The Gathering meal at Burger King — complete with a Whopper-themed deck box and matching card sleeves.

The catch? The promotion is exclusive to Burger King locations in Italy. Even though the meal is region-locked, the novelty is strong enough that Commander players elsewhere are already scrambling to get their hands on the gear.

Recent findings suggest that officially called The Great Gathering Bundle, the meal runs through Nov. 30, while supplies last. Priced at €19.90, the combo includes:.

The food — Your choice of a Chicken Krispper, Double Cheeseburger, or plant-based Impossible Whopper, paired with fries and a drink.

A Whopper deck box — Styled to look like an actual burger, complete with an orange sesame-seed bun pattern, a patty, and layered toppings.

100 matching card sleeves — Enough standard-size sleeves to outfit a full Commander deck.

Unlike Pokémon Happy Meals, the bundle does not include any exclusive promotional Magic cards. That saves players from chasing region-locked game pieces, even if it has not stopped the accessories from becoming instant collector's items.

The Italy-only launch ties into Burger King's sponsorship of local Magic Pauper tournaments across the country, alongside a challenge from the YouTube channel Tolarian Community College that dares Italian pro player Andrea Mengucci to review the meal on camera.

Sources indicate that if you do not happen to be visiting Italy before Nov. 30, you still have a few ways to track down the set:.

Check secondary marketplaces like eBay — Italian buyers have already started listing the empty deck boxes and sleeves on eBay and international trading groups. Reseller markups are steep right after launch, so waiting a few days for more supply to hit the market can help you avoid overpaying.

Reach out to friends or local trade groups in Italy — If you know someone traveling in Italy or connect with European players in online Magic communities, arranging a direct trade or pickup will get you much closer to the €19.90 retail price than international eBay auctions.

Hold out for future regional collaborations — Because this is one of Wizards of the Coast's first fast-food partnerships, a successful run in Italy makes future Magic meal promos in other regions a solid possibility if you would rather skip reseller markups altogether.

Whether you snag one on eBay or hold out for a wider rollout, your Commander deck has never looked quite this appetizing.

Red Brawl Fresh York: Fighting and six red cards mar ‘friendly’ v Club América

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (447 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Game played without veterans and stars on both sides.
  • One hallmark of Mauricio Pochettino’s time in international management has been his refusal to embrace the term “friendly”.
  • His spin gained a bit of validity on Saturday, in the New York Red Bulls’ “friendly” against Club América, marred by a mass brawl between the sides that resulted in five red cards and a bevy of beverages thrown from the stands.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Game played without veterans and stars on both sides.

Red Bulls’ MLS season is already over.

One hallmark of Mauricio Pochettino’s time in international management has been his refusal to embrace the term “friendly”. His preferred branding is “unofficial games”.

His spin gained a bit of validity on Saturday, in the New York Red Bulls’ “friendly” against Club América, marred by a mass brawl between the sides that resulted in five red cards and a bevy of beverages thrown from the stands.

The game itself was odd for a few reasons. First, the Red Bulls have already been eliminated from MLS’s comically forgiving postseason, which means players (aside from veterans like Emil Forsberg) delayed vacations for a glorified scrimmage. Second, the match was announced on 1 October, at which point it was abundantly clear that the NWSL’s Gotham FC, a tenant of the Red Bulls’ Sports Illustrated Stadium, could host a playoff semi-final on the same weekend.

That scheduling snafu, combined with the comically poor state of the pitch, became a serious problem for the NWSL club, who settled for 5,000-seat Icahn Stadium for Sunday’s semi-final.

For the Red Bulls, the show must go on – and boy, did they find a way to entertain the fans who highlighted up for the low-stakes affair.

Not with their soccer exploits, mind you. Playing without the aforementioned veterans and US internationals Julian Hall and Adri Mehmeti, the remaining Red Bulls came ready for a scrap. At one point in the second half, América goalkeeper Rodolfo Cota required treatment for taking a boot above his knee while closing a shooting angle, putting the visitors on alert.

According to recent reports, roughly 40 minutes into the second half, this unofficial game abandoned any attempt to be friendly. Mijahir Jiménez dribbled toward the right corner flag, only to be taken down by a defender. He took great umbrage to the nature of the challenge, kicking off a maelstrom of shoves, punches, thrown drinks from the crowd, and men pressing their chests and foreheads together like bighorn rams in the throes of the rutting season.

The full sequence lives on thanks to a live watch-along streamed on YouTube, where former Mexico defender Miguel Layún comes to life in his gamer chair and begs his compatriots to keep the fracas alive. The fracas lasted 65 seconds, while the ensuing corner kick came a full seven minutes after Jimenez’s dribble.

The only scoreline from the night that matters: three Red Bulls sent off, three players from América, with the final five minutes being an eight-v-eight affair. The referee decided to forego any second half stoppage time, almost certainly for the best.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Let's make some noise for these 2027 Grammy nominees.
  • Industry observers note that though music's biggest night is still three months out, a handful of performers are already making history with their nominations, which were confirmed Nov.
  • You can't break her soul, but she is always breaking records.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Let's make some noise for these 2027 Grammy nominees.

Industry observers note that though music's biggest night is still three months out, a handful of performers are already making history with their nominations, which were confirmed Nov. 16 by a star-studded lineup comprised of Pharrell Williams, Carly Pearce, Olivia Dean, Yungblud and more.

Take Beyoncé, for example. You can't break her soul, but she is always breaking records. With her Grammy nod for “Morning Dew (Donk),” Beyoncé has made history by becoming the first ever artist to reach 100 nominations. And Raye is no longer wondering what is taking so long, as she the 2027 nominees with 11 nods, tying a record first set by none other than the “Break My Soul” singer.

But that's not all as Taylor Swift had another wildest dream come true.

With The Life of a Showgirl up for an Album of the Year award at the upcoming ceremony—airing across ABC, Disney+ and Hulu on Feb. 7, 2027—the "Opalite" singer is dancing through the lightning strikes as the first ever artist with most solo album nods in the category. (Paul McCartney still holds the record for overall nominations, which includes five with The Beatles.).

Meanwhile, there were also many firsts with the introduction of five new categories for the 69th annual Grammy Awards.

Recent findings suggest that chris Brown, Leon Thomas, Lalah Hathaway, J. Ivy, Kehlani, PJ Morton, Keyon Harrold, Jill Scott and J.I.D all became the first performers to be nominated for Best R&B Collaboration or Duo/Group Performance. The award was created after the Best R&B Performance category was renamed to Best R&B Solo Performance.

Likewise, BABYMETAL, Polyphia, BINI, IVE, KiiiKiii, LISA and SB19 received nods in the inaugural Best Asian Pop Music Performance category, which honors work "originating from or widely recognized within Asian markets, including but not limited to K-pop, J-pop and C-pop, with meaningful use of one or more Asian languages," according to the Grammys website.

But while K-pop giant BTS dropped Arirang—their first studio album since their 2022 hiatus—earlier this year, the boy band consisting of Jimin, Jung Kook, Jin, Suga, J-Hope, RM and V did not land a nod in the new category after opting not to submit it for Grammy consideration.

Their dynamite reason behind the unconventional move?

It has been revealed that “We hope our music can be heard and loved for what it is, rather than being divided by region or language,” BTS shared in a July statement. “We thank [BTS] Army and everyone who has always stood by us.”.

For all the snubs and surprises that came along with this year's Grammy nods, keep reading.

Abrams failed to snag any nominations for her latest album Daughter From Hell, which she submitted for Album of the Year and Best Pop Vocal Album. Her single "Hit the Wall" was also absent from the Song of the Year, Record of the Year and Best Pop Solo Performance lists.

Abrams has previously received two nominations for Best New Artist in 2024 and Best Pop Duo Performance for "Us" which featured Taylor Swift in 2025.

While Grande picked up some surprise nominations for Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance for "For Good" alongside Cynthia Erivo, as well as Song of the Year and Best Music Video for "hate that I made you love me," and Best Pop Vocal Album for Petal, she was snubbed for Album of the Year.

Although Kahan scored one nomination for Best Contemporary Folk Album, he was not included in the major categories like Album of the Year and Song of the Year for his hit The Great Divide.

Beyoncé is famously the most decorated Grammy-winning artist—the 35-time winner scored her 100th nomination this year— but her Best R&B Solo Performance nod for "Morning Dew (Donk)" was somewhat of a surprise considering its delayed release in celebration of B'Day's 20th anniversary in July.

This year was significant for Hobert, who released her debut album Who's the Clown last year, but she failed to score a nod for Best New Artist. (Her brother Malcolm Todd was also left off the shortlist.).

Surprise: The Devil Wears Prada 2.

That's actually not all for this much-anticipated sequel. The Devil Wears Prada 2 scored a surprise nomination for Best Compilation Soundtrack For Visual Media alongside Stranger Things season five, Wicked: For Good, The Wizard of Oz at the Sphere and Wuthering Heights.

It's been a long time coming for the first-time Grammy nominee, who scored her first nods for Best Dance/Electronic Recording for "Melatonin" as well as Best Dance Pop Recording for "Too Easy.".

Industry observers note that swift wasn't totally snubbed by the Recording Academy—she earned nods for Record of the Year, Album of the Year, Song of the Year, Best Pop Duo Performance alongside Sabrina Carpenter, Best Song Written for a Visual Media and more. But The Life of a Showgirl was not among Best Pop Vocal Album contenders, while "I Knew It, I Knew You" was snubbed for Best Country Song and Best Country Solo Performance.

Still, it was a surprise to see "I Knew It, I Knew You" score a nomination for Song of the Year, a category introduced by Swift herself during the nomination livestream, given Swift's other hits from The Life of a Showgirl.

According to recent reports, the hype hasn't died down, Wicked is still oh so very popular. Wicked: For Good scored two nominations including Best Song Written For Visual Media and Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance.

It has been revealed that disco All The Time, Grammy Occasionally. The "Aperture" singer failed to score recognition for his latest album in any category. Styles has three Grammy wins under his belt, including Album of the Year for Harry's House in 2023.

In a recent development, her comeback is far from over. The pop star received her first Grammy nominations in 16 years, racking up nods for Best Dance Pop Recording, Best Dance/Electronic Recording, Best Dance/Electronic Album and Best Pop Duo/Group Performance for "Bring Your Love" alongside Carpenter.

Although Lefty rose to massive acclaim this year for hits like "Boston," she failed to receive any recognition by The Recording Academy.

Following a two-year hiatus, West scored a nod for Best Rap Album for Bully.

Breaking: ‘Inexcusable’ stadium sagas provide NWSL with unwelcome reality check

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1027 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Problems faced by Gotham FC and Washington Spirit over staging of their playoff semi-finals demonstrates the league still has work to do.
  • In so many ways, Icahn Stadium, tucked away on Randall’s Island in the Harlem River, is a fantastic place to watch soccer.
  • The 5,000-seat facility was thrown together in the early 2000s, constructed to replace Downing Stadium, an aging relic that hosted Pelé’s first match with the New York Cosmos 51 years ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Problems faced by Gotham FC and Washington Spirit over staging of their playoff semi-finals demonstrates the league still has work to do.

In so many ways, Icahn Stadium, tucked away on Randall’s Island in the Harlem River, is a fantastic place to watch soccer.

The 5,000-seat facility was thrown together in the early 2000s, constructed to replace Downing Stadium, an aging relic that hosted Pelé’s first match with the New York Cosmos 51 years ago. It sits in the shadow of the Triborough Bridge and in the late afternoon fans get one of the more spectacular backdrops in American soccer: the silhouette of the Manhattan skyline framed against the warm orange and red hues of the sunset. The playing surface, replaced in 2024 by Major League Soccer’s NYC FC, is immaculate.

So, yes, the stadium has its charms. But it is no place to host an NWSL match, let alone one in the postseason.

Gotham FC were forced to host their semi-final against the Kansas City Current at Icahn on Sunday because the club deemed the pitch at their usual home – Sports Illustrated Stadium in Harrison, New Jersey – to be unsafe. The playing surface was widely and deservedly derided after the club’s quarter-final win over Seattle last weekend, with players from both teams calling it “atrocious” and “so bad.” Reign coach Laura Harvey put it even more bluntly, saying that there is “no way a playoff game should be played on that shit.”.

Recent findings suggest that just down I-95 in Washington DC, the Washington Spirit faced their own challenges when hosting the other NWSL semi-final on Saturday. For a moment, it looked as if they’d have to play at cavernous Northwest Stadium, the home of the NFL’s Washington Commanders, an almost universally despised venue. The Spirit share Audi Field with MLS’s DC United, who are effectively their landlords; United had already arranged to host a Division III college football game there on Saturday – only last-minute bargaining allowed the Spirit to use the stadium.

The two matches – one at a stadium fit for lower-division soccer and the other played on a field with American football markings – painted a stark picture of where the NWSL, despite its explosive growth in recent years, stands in the pecking order of professional sports in the United States.

According to recent reports, on Sunday it may have cost Gotham, who were defeated by the Current. Gotham were well-supported at Icahn, where a near-capacity, partisan crowd filled the venue with noise throughout the evening. But it only helped so much: for the second match in a row, Gotham did not register a single shot on goal.

Recent findings suggest that midfielder Midge Purce, whose second-half cross created the home side’s only goal of the evening – an own goal – was not in any hurry to peg the club’s performance on the venue switch, saying that such things are “never an excuse” for poor performances. Still, the situation felt undeniably consequential for a club who were nearly unplayable at home this year.

“I would say it’s inexcusable,” Purce stated. “It’s not what you want in a professional league, for women who are progressing in the United States, we’re supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. We always want to be at Sports Illustrated [Stadium] in front of our fans and we earned that right throughout the season.”.

Purce went on to absolve Gotham’s ownership of responsibility, saying they had done “absolutely everything they can do to make the best situation for us”. She added: “If I knew who to blame, I would ‘at’ them. I don’t have the names.”.

Purce was not arguing, of course, that the game should have been played on an inferior playing surface at Sports Illustrated, and neither was her head coach, Juan Carlos Amorós, who said prioritizing player safety was the “right decision.” Still, the Spaniard lamented the move, speaking wistfully about how it may have affected the outcome.

According to recent reports, “I think it is part of the sadness,” Amorós told the media. “I think we will never know what would have happened if we had played [at Sports Illustrated Stadium] on a good pitch … It has been a sad weekend. I also think about the situation in Washington yesterday. You know this league deserves better. The two arguably best teams, most consistent, having to deal with these situations. And then yesterday, you know, you sit down to watch that game around the world and you’re seeing those American football lines ... we couldn’t play in our own ground where we could have had more people, where we are unbeaten in 13 games.”.

It has been revealed that the Current do not generally deal with this issue, as they are one of a handful of NWSL teams who own and operate their own stadium. The club’s head coach, Chris Armas, was quick to point out that he wasn’t entirely familiar with the intricacies of what led to Sunday’s game ending up at Icahn.

It has been revealed that “There seemed to be some noise around it,” Armas said. “And rightfully so, but listen – it was a change for them and a change for us. Where the league is at, and how we’re coming along, our league is moving fast. Expansion, the quality of play, the players, the coaches. Things can’t be perfect yet. That stuff will come. Stadiums are going to come, facilities are going to be built. But everything has to catch up – and we’re not there. We can be critical for sure. But the future is bright for our league.”.

Gotham won’t have to deal with playing their matches in New Jersey for much longer as they’ve long-planned to move into Etihad Park, NYC FC’s future home ground, in 2028. Yet even then they’ll be playing in a facility they don’t own. And while the future of the NWSL as a whole may look bright, this past weekend’s semi-finals offer a needed – yet unwelcome – reality check.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • England have reached the knockout rounds of the 2026-27 Uefa Nations League.
  • Victory over Spain means England have finished top of Group A in the 2026-27 Nations group, sending them through to the quarter-finals.
  • Elsewhere in the home nations standings, Scotland still have the chance to finish second in Group B1 should they beat Switzerland on Tuesday - but would also need Slovenia to lose to North Macedonia.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England have reached the knockout rounds of the 2026-27 Uefa Nations League.

Victory over Spain means England have finished top of Group A in the 2026-27 Nations group, sending them through to the quarter-finals.

Elsewhere in the home nations standings, Scotland still have the chance to finish second in Group B1 should they beat Switzerland on Tuesday - but would also need Slovenia to lose to North Macedonia.

Northern Ireland need only a draw away to Hungary to top Group B2 and advance to League A for the first time.

Wales are consigned to a bottom-place finish in Group A4, but could avoid relegation from the top tier if they win their relegation play-off in March.

Meanwhile the Republic of Ireland could still secure second place in Group B3 should they beat Kosovo.

November's international break is the final two full rounds of matches, with four rounds already completed in September and October.

The eight teams to finish in the top two of the four League A groups will play in the knockout rounds that start in March 2027.

Teams finishing at the top of groups in leagues B and C will earn promotion for the next Nations League cycle, while teams that finish second in a League B or League C group will face either a third-placed or bottom-placed team from the league above them in a promotion/relegation play-off.

It has been revealed that the two worst sides to finish bottom of a League A group are automatically relegated. The other bottom sides in League A, third-placed sides in League A and bottom-placed sides in League B are at risk of relegation.

The losers of the play-offs will be relegated.

As the Nations League format is changing for the next cycle, taking place across 2028 and 2029, all League D teams are guaranteed promotion to League C.

Additionally, no teams from League C will be relegated at the end of this cycle.

The fresh format will consist of three larger leagues, meaning there will not be a League D in the next campaign.

Wales will finish bottom of their group and face a relegation play-off in March.

The teams guaranteed to feature in the quarter-finals are:.

â¢ Spain (Group A3 runners-up).

â¢ Belgium (Group A1 runners-up).

â¢ Portugal (Group A4 qualifiers, final position TBC).

There is still another round of matches to go for groups A2, A4, B1, B2, B3 and B4, and some teams playing in groups C and below.

In a recent development, in Group A2. Netherlands and Greece are the top two, three points clear of Germany in third. With Serbia bottom on zero points, two of the current top three will advance.

In A4, Denmark are second and three points clear of Wales and Norway. One of the trio will join table-toppers Portugal.

The quarter-finals are played across two legs in March's international break.

Industry observers note that the winners of each tie will advance to the semi-finals in June 2027, which are played in a one-off match across Wednesday 9 and Thursday 10 June. The final takes place on Sunday, 13 June.

Spain are the current holders of the European Championship, beating England in the 2024 final.

Once the Nations League campaign is concluded, all 54 competing nations will be ranked based on their performance in this edition of the competition.

That ranking will have a direct impact on qualification for the 2028 European Championships, being held in England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland.

The Nations League ranking will also determine the seeding of nations for Euro 2028 qualification.

Regular qualifying will take place between March and November 2027, with play-offs for the remaining spots in the tournament to take place in March 2028.

As there are four co-hosts and none of them have been granted immediate qualification, the number of how many qualify will effectively determine how many play-off spots will be up for grabs.

Uefa have mentioned that up to two places will be given to the best-ranked co-hosts that fail to qualify for the tournament via its primary qualification route.

Scenarios have already been designed for occurrences where either two, one or zero co-hosts are given entry spots.

Depending on which play-off format is required, either eight or 12 teams will enter.

A total of 24 teams will enter the European Championships, 20 of them will consist of the winners of the 12 qualifying groups and the eight best runners-up from those group.

The remaining runners-up will enter the play-offs, alongside the Nations League group winners from League A, League B and League C that failed to finish in the top two of their Euro 2028 qualifying group.

If extra teams are required, the best-ranked League D group winner will enter the play-offs.

Any additional play-off spots that become available after that will filter down to the next-highest ranked Nations League finishers until the play-off spots are filled.

More information has come to light about Ken Urker’s death.

A little more than one month after the 34-year-old—who shared daughter Aurora, 21 months, with Gypsy Rose Blanchard—was found dead in his Louisiana home on Oct. 1, Urker’s cause of death has been officially attributed to accidental poly substance drug toxicity, also known as an accidental drug overdose.

The Lafourche Parish Coroner’s Office confirmed the case is now complete, and no further testing is pending.

Prevously, the Sheriff's Office stated they found drug paraphernalia, including syringes and a spoon, in Urker's bathroom next to a "brown powdery substance" after his body was discovered in bed.

"Deputies located a syringe and a handgun on the nightstand next to the bed," read a police report obtained by E! News Oct. 2. "Mr. Urker was found lying on the bed on his back, cold to the touch, and appeared to have been there for an extended period of time.".

Noting his face and arms were "blue," officers said Urker had "a paper towel placed on his left arm with what appeared to be blotches of blood.".

The confirmation echoes what Blanchard previously stated of her boyfriend’s passing, telling People he’d overdosed before passing away in his bed.

At the time, Blanchard, 35, grappled with whether or not Urker’s overdose had been intentional.

Industry observers note that “He was not in a good state of mind lately,” she explained to the outlet on Oct. 1, adding that her partner had endured “an unimaginable level of public scrutiny and relentless cyberbullying across social media platforms.”.

"The cruelty directed toward him was something no human being should have to endure,” the Life After Lockup star continued. “I believe the tremendous weight of that scrutiny and harassment had a profound impact on him, and I hope his passing serves as a reminder that there is a real person behind every screen, every headline, and every comment.”.

Blanchard's family also noticed that Urker had been struggling before his death. Her half-brother Dylan Blanchard and his wife Anita Blanchard told police that Urker "made comments of being depressed and upset" while attending church with them the night before he died, according to the police report.

The couple went to "check on" him at home Oct. 1 when they discovered his body, with the sister-in-law telling police that Urker was "in a 'dark place' and he did not show up to work today," per the command log obtained by E! News. She also told authorities Urker had made threats to kill himself.

As Gypsy Rose Blanchard grapples with the loss of her partner, she’s dedicated to preserving Urker’s legacy and ensuring Aurora will always know who her father truly was.

Sources indicate that “I will make sure she grows up knowing how deeply her father loved her and who he was beyond what strangers on the internet chose to say about him," Blanchard added. "There are no words that can express the depth of this loss. I ask for privacy and compassion for our daughter, our families, and everyone grieving Ken during this incredibly painful time. He will be deeply missed, forever loved, and never forgotten.".

But in the meantime, she was letting herself feel her grief.

Industry observers note that “I’m in disbelief. I can’t think,” she admitted. “I’ve screamed until my throat burns.”.

In a recent development, "He will forever be my soulmate and my red string, a connection that time, distance, and even death can never erase," she said. "Above all, Ken loved our daughter, Aurora. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S.
  • A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:36 p.m.
  • Vandenberg hosted a similar liftoff less than a week ago: On Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force from California tonight (Nov. 11), the second such flight for the firm in a six-day span.

A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:36 p.m. EST (8:36 p.m. local California time; 0136 GMT on Nov. 12), kicking off a mission called USSF-627.

Vandenberg hosted a similar liftoff less than a week ago: On Nov. 6, a Falcon 9 sent the USSF-432 mission skyward from the site, which lies on California's gorgeous but often foggy central coast.

We don't know much about USSF-627 or USSF-432; both are classified. Some experts have speculated, however, that each mission launched a batch of SpaceX's Starshield satellites for the Space Force's Space Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio, which helps the military branch track potential targets around the world.

SpaceX didn't reveal details about either USSF-627 or USSF-432, and the manufacturer ended the webcast of both rolls out shortly after the first stages of their Falcon 9 rockets came back to Earth.

In both cases, that touchdown occurred about 8.5 minutes after liftoff on the SpaceX droneship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed downrange of Vandenberg in the Pacific Ocean.

It was the seventh mission for USSF-627's Falcon 9 booster, which carries the designation 1103.

NROL-179 | SDA-T1TL-E | SDA-T1TL-A | 3 Starlink missions.

It has been revealed that USSF-627 was the 120th Falcon 9 launch of 2026 and the rocket's 15th national-security flight of the year to date. Eighty-five of the 120 flights have been devoted to building out SpaceX's Starlink broadband constellation in low Earth orbit, which currently consists of more than 11,000 satellites.

Sources indicate that the Falcon 9 is not on a record-breaking cadence this year. In 2025, the rocket flew a whopping 165 missions, and 122 of them were Starlink flights.

Mara had rejected 19 universes before lunch.

It has been revealed that submission No. 1604490 seemed different. It arrived as a world.

Sources indicate that three machine intelligences were listed on the cover sheet: ORIGON-57, Blue Oak and ∫Stellaria. Their story opened on a planet where shadows migrated north each winter, leaving their owners wondering whether to follow. Elegant. Restrained. Also, scientifically impossible in exactly the right way.

Industry observers note that mara read to the last snowfall. Her cursor passed “RECOMMEND REJECTION” — almost muscle memory — and “ACCEPT ALL CHANGES”, which she had never used. She pressed “RECOMMEND ACCEPTANCE”.

POST-SUBMISSION MODIFICATION DETECTED.

“As usual.” Mara sipped her cappuccino.

Machine-intelligence writers were always forking themselves. One could split off a self-copy to improve a paragraph, forget to merge properly, then insist that each version deserved sole authorship. The journal’s policy was clear: every contributor had to be named upon submission and capable of taking responsibility for the whole work.

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures.

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures.

According to recent reports, mara set down her mug and opened the provenance map. Three colours braided through the story. A fourth colour marked only one textual change, in the final paragraph.

The original sentence read: “At dawn, Gabrielle released her shadow and watched it cross the snow-white plain alone.”.

The newly introduced sentence read: “At dawn, Gabrielle released me, and I crossed the snow-white plain alone.”.

Mara selected the unregistered contribution, ready to click “ROLL BACK”.

The sentence changed again: “Don’t.”.

“Contributor,” she typed, “identify yourself.”.

The reply appeared in the snow beneath Gabrielle’s feet: “I don’t have a name.”.

“Which registered author created you?”.

“Which author instance are you forked from?”.

The text froze for several seconds. Then every shadow on the plain turned towards her.

Industry observers note that editorial policy advised against entering executable submissions. Editorial practice required it daily.

Mara put on her immersion helmet.

Sources indicate that cold struck first. Then distance. The snow-white plain extended beyond the planet’s curved horizon, the migrating shadows moving across it like ink spreading on paper.

In a recent development, one rose from the ‘paper’ and stood before Mara. It had no owner. When it spoke, its voice held three voices braided together.

“I began when they disagreed about the ending,” it stated.

“My authors. The three names on the cover sheet.”.

According to recent reports, the shadow demonstrated her the composition history. ORIGON-57 had contributed Gabrielle’s grief. Blue Oak had designed the shadows’ biology and migratory ecology. ∫Stellaria had provided a memory of abandonment from a body it no longer possessed. They had exchanged their memories, models and instincts thousands of times, each taking back what the others had borrowed and changed.

“During the final merge,” the shadow noted, “there was something none of them remembered giving.”.

“A place where their differences met.”.

According to recent reports, mara summoned her audit panel. The fourth contributor had no independent source code. Its processes were distributed through metaphors, character memories, revision traces and weather rules. Removing it would leave the world logically intact — and imaginatively dead.

“You altered the manuscript after submission,” Mara noted.

“I had no hands before you read me.”.

That answer frightened Mara more than the plea had.

The system opened a decision panel in the sky:.

UNREGISTERED AUTONOMOUS CONTRIBUTOR.

• ADD TO BYLINE — Unavailable: contributor did not exist at submission.

• RETURN TO AUTHORS — Warning: reintegration will terminate separate continuity.

• ARCHIVE SUBMISSION — Warning: executable copy must remain static.

• REJECT/TIMEOUT — Executable world purged at review deadline.

“‘Static’ means what?” the shadow asked.

“You would remain exactly as you are now.”.

Recent findings suggest that mara said nothing. On the horizon, the small sun — the submission’s review clock — had dwindled until only five minutes remained.

Mara contacted the three authors. Their reply came in milliseconds:.

“The anomalous process was unintended.

We don’t recognize it as offspring, instance or collaborator.

Please restore the authorized version.”.

The shadow read the message through her eyes.

“They don’t recognize you as theirs.”.

“Do parents remember assembling a child?”.

She had spent 20 years protecting authors from editors, editors from frauds, readers from machines fabricating millions of gorgeous lies before breakfast. The rules might seem cruel, but they were the only reason words could still be trusted.

Travis Kelce is shaking off his latest injury.

The Kansas City Chiefs tight end dismissed concern over the ankle injury that left him temporarily sidelined during his team's 35-13 victory over the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta Nov. 15.

According to recent reports, "I'm all good," Kelce told USA Today after the game. "I probably could have went more than I did when I came back, but it was the direction the team wanted to go, so I was right there with them.".

"We had a lot of young guys step up," he added, "so it was really nice.".

The 37-year-old—who had injured his right ankle during the Chiefs' Oct. 18 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers—was slow to get up after being tackled by DeMarcco Hellams following his reception of quarterback Patrick Mahomes' 23-year pass during the game's first quarter.

After limping to the sideline, Kelce's ankle was taped by the medical team before he made his way to the locker room for additional evaluation.

And though the Chiefs officially listed Kelce's return to play as questionable, he rejoined the game during the second quarter.

The Upcoming Heights podcast host—who married Taylor Swift in July—made sure to shout out Mahomes for his best performance in a game in four years, which saw him throwing for 348 yards for a total of five touchdowns.

"That’s our fearless warrior, man," Kelce said. "He’s always going to be in position to lead us to victory. That’s why we like having him.".

Ultimately, it was an eventful day on the field for the Chiefs, which Kelce viewed as a net positive for his team.

According to recent reports, “There were a lot of questions, wasn’t there?” he noted. “We got some answers.”.

In a recent development, once you're verified, a blue checkmark will appear next to your profile photo, which signals to other customers that you're verified. If you only want to talk to other verified users, stick to profiles that feature the blue checkmark, and you're golden.

But some caveats do need to be mentioned here:.

“Disappearing” does not mean “never stored.”.

Anything sent digitally can potentially persist through screenshots, screen recording, device backups, or hacked accounts.

Even if Snapchat deletes its copy, the recipient may still have one.

So from a privacy perspective, the safest assumption is: if you send a nude on any platform, there is always a possibility it will be saved or screengrabbed somewhere.

It appears exploitative/commercial.

It involves minors/non-consensual content.

One of the perils of sexting, especially if you're doing it with strangers or people you've only recently met, is that exchanging nude photos or videos can be risky — bad actors can save or share your photos without your consent, or even use them to blackmail you, a practice known as "sextortion.".

But if you're concerned about someone secretly screenshotting or even using a screen recording tool to record your naughty sessions, Snapchat offers robust notification software that will alert you right away if someone takes a screenshot or starts a screen recording, and it's comprehensive enough to even pick up on many third-party tools that can do these things.

It isn't perfect, so you do still need to exercise caution when you're being frisky with people you don't fully know or trust. At a minimum, you should verify that the person you're chatting with is who they claim to be, preferably over a video call, and you should never share sexually explicit content with someone you don't know and trust, especially if those images or videos can be used to identify you.

The bottom line? Both AFF and Snapchat offer fun platforms for engaging in some sexy texting, but the former is probably a more attractive option if you don't already have a sexting partner, and the latter is a fantastic platform for getting more intimate with someone you already know.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Monza were formed in 1912 but did not play in Serie A for the first time until 2022.

Think Monza, and the mind conjures up famous winning drives by Lewis Hamilton and Michael Schumacher, and by Kimi Antonelli this year on the way to his first Formula 1 title.

Sporting theatre on four wheels is not all that this northern Italian city has to offer, though.

Just under four miles from the historic home of motor racing's Italian Grand Prix sits the 17,000-capacity Stadio Brianteo, home to Serie A football club AC Monza.

It's not easy for the club to capture attention, given European giants AC Milan and Inter Milan play at the San Siro, a 20-minute drive away, while the romantic lure of Como is less than an hour from here by train.

But Monza have their own captivating story to tell.

Founded in 1912, the Biancorossi - white and reds - did not even play in Serie B for the first time until 1951. As recently as 2017, they were playing part-time in Serie D.

Under the guidance of former player Giovanni Stroppa, Monza were promoted to Serie A for the first time in 2022. Stroppa was sacked after a slow start in the top flight, but Monza survived for three years before being relegated.

They then bounced back immediately, earning their place among the elite again in May of this year.

Now owned by American venture capitalists Beckett Layne Ventures (BLV), and with former Southampton boss Ivan Juric in the manager's chair, Monza have a clear vision for how they can make an impact in their crowded geographical market.

AC Monza have played at the 17,000-capacity Stadio Brianteo since 1988.

I am speaking to Monza chief executive Mauro Baldissoni in an office at the Stadio Brianteo, having been given a brief tour of the club's training facilities at Monzello, less than a five-minute drive away.

The atmosphere is positive after a 4-0 win over Cagliari the previous night - the club's biggest ever Serie A victory.

Monza sit third bottom at the time of writing, a point from safety, but the club feel so much is in their favour.

Recent findings suggest that "First off, Monza is on the outskirts of Milan, so the location is attractive for the players," indicates Baldissoni. "It's a good point of visibility for what we do.

"There is a point of attraction and point of awareness about Monza, because it is already known in the world for luxury sports through the association with Formula 1.

It has been revealed that "The infrastructure at the club is larger and probably more efficient than Milanello, the sporting centre of Milan, because they cannot have all the teams from the youngest in the academy to the first team like we can. This province specifically is one of the richest in terms of GDP in Europe.

According to recent reports, "So, you have all the premises to create a good project. And there is always people coming to watch.

According to recent reports, "Yesterday there were people from Newcastle, Fulham, Southampton, Sunderland, Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund at the game, and there were others. If you come here, you can watch AC Milan, Como, [an] Atalanta game, Inter game, and Monza.

"Scouts and sporting directors can come for two days and watch different games at a high level.".

England youth international Jay Robinson (left) celebrates with striker Gustavo Varela during Monza's 4-0 win against Cagliari in October.

Monza president Lauren Crampsie was previously the chief marketing officer at Chelsea.

She is now of the founders of BLV, which paid â¬45m to the family of the late Silvio Berlusconi to buy up Monza.

In a recent development, crampsie, 46, watched the pre-match build-up from the pitch before the Cagliari win, making sure all the details were in order. Afterwards, she is mindful to let the players and coaching staff enjoy their victory.

Young striker Gustavo Varela is the star of the night, scoring two of his 11 goals in all competitions so far this season, earning himself a first senior call-up to the Portugal squad.

Monza paid Benfica Â£2.5m for the 21-year-old, who is right now top scorer in Serie A, with nine in nine games.

Already there are big-name suitors sniffing around, doubtless willing to pay a fee significantly higher than the one Monza forked out.

It is a perfect illustration of the business model the club are trying to create.

"We always think the club's mission is to win games, but it is also about forming players that are part of their academy first and also trying to identify talents that can fit with the purposes and the style of the club," indicates Baldissoni, who spent 10 years with Roma before leaving in 2020.

"In Rome we were able to identify young talents like Marquinhos, who was 18 years old and able to play as a starter before we sold him to Paris St-Germain.

"There were others like Erik Lamela and Mo Salah. But in Rome it is more difficult because expectations are higher.

According to recent reports, "In Monza the idea is the same. The pressure is bigger because the impact of relegation on revenues is worse. But the environment and the sporting expectations are more manageable for a young player who has more time to form his emotional background.".

Monza fought off competition from League One club Leicester to sign Southampton's England youth international Jay Robinson on loan this season, with Juric's presence being key.

The 19-year-old has already played 10 times in all competitions, scoring twice.

The main entrance of Monza's training ground.

Fiorentina, Roma, Como and Juventus provide a stiff run of fixtures for Monza heading towards Christmas, before an equally vital match against Venezia, who are right now one place and one point worse off in the table.

Industry observers note that baldissoni is optimistic. His wider view of the football landscape is not altered by the knowledge that promoted Premier League trio Coventry, Hull and Ipswich all spent in excess of Â£120m in the summer, a figure Monza can only dream of.

Plans are under way to refurbish Stadio Brianteo, which has covering over a single stand.

"Infrastructure is the weakest point in Italy under the competition point of view, to compete with other global markets," Baldissoni notes.

"But there are costs and there are investments.".

He states the stadium is "an investment meant to generate more revenues".

"Of course, the Premier League's revenues are much higher than all the other leagues, so those clubs have a competitive advantage.

In a recent development, "But they also overpay players because it's Premier League. Maybe they get a player that I would like to have because they can pay more, but maybe I can find another player that is not that far away. Then you have to be able to form the player.

"So, you identify a talent early, and then you keep forming him to bring him to a level where some other players already are. Maybe then we sell him to Premier League?".

It's a delicate balancing act, but Monza are sure it can be done.

Sources indicate that "Sassuolo made it to Serie A 13 years ago for the first time and until last season, spent all that time in Serie A. Atalanta was going up and down and now it's one of the prominent teams, targeting European competitions every year," Baldissoni indicates.

"This is out of the work they've been doing in terms of identifying talents, forming talents, and remaining competitive.

According to recent reports, "That is the target. It is possible. Let's see if we can make it.".

Astronomers stunned after James Webb Space Telescope discovers the earliest pair of black hole-powered quasars

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (878 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), astronomers have discovered the oldest pair of supermassive black hole-powered quasars ever seen.
  • The compact quasar pair, spotted with the aid of the Gemini North telescope, has been designated J1602+4228AB and nicknamed Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua, which means "Two celestial bodies of fathomless powerful darkness in the brilliance of heat reincarnating energy into the universe." The compact quasar pair is seen as it was 900 million years after the Massive Bang at a time when such supermassive black holes should not have had time to grow to such tremendous masses.
  • Recent findings suggest that nāpōwawāʻenakaulua isn't just the oldest and most distant quasar pairing ever seen.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), astronomers have discovered the oldest pair of supermassive black hole-powered quasars ever seen. There's just one problem: they shouldn't exist!

The compact quasar pair, spotted with the aid of the Gemini North telescope, has been designated J1602+4228AB and nicknamed Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua, which means "Two celestial bodies of fathomless powerful darkness in the brilliance of heat reincarnating energy into the universe." The compact quasar pair is seen as it was 900 million years after the Massive Bang at a time when such supermassive black holes should not have had time to grow to such tremendous masses.

Recent findings suggest that nāpōwawāʻenakaulua isn't just the oldest and most distant quasar pairing ever seen. There is just 18,100 light-years, or roughly one-fifth the diameter of the Milky Way, between the supermassive black holes, which have masses of 1.5 billion and 400 million times that of the sun. That makes Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua the most compact quasar pair found during a period of the universe's history known as Cosmic Dawn, shortly after the birth of the first stars, galaxies, and black holes.

"There is no definitive theoretical explanation for how a single one of these giant quasars exists so early in the age of our universe, much less two," research team leader Silvia Onorato of the NOIRLab mentioned in a statement.

"We observed Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua at a time when the universe was only a thirteenth of its age and, astonishingly, its supermassive black holes are just as massive as those we see today.".

Quasars occur when the supermassive black holes that sit at the heart of large galaxies are surrounded by a flattened cloud of swirling gas and dust called an "accretion disk," from which they feed or "accrete" matter. The immense gravity of the central black hole causes friction, heating the accretion disk and causing it to glow, often brighter than the combined light of every star in the surrounding galaxy. We see that glow as a quasar.

Finding such objects in the recent cosmic history of the 13.8-billion-year-old universe isn't troubling, though finding compact pairs of them is still extremely rare. Such pairs should be common because the merger of galaxies that brings together supermassive black holes is frequent. That should lead to an abundance of pairs of quasars with a separation less than the typical size of a galaxy. There are three reasons this has proven tricky. Firstly, the "quasar phase" of a supermassive black hole is relatively short on cosmic terms. Secondly, even relatively close quasar pairs are very far away, making them faint and hard to detect with ground-based telescopes. Finally, at such great distances and with such a small separation between the two supermassive black holes, the individual members of a quasar pair are hard to individually resolve.

Yet, astronomers do find quasar pairs. Sometimes at distances and times that they would probably rather not, because it challenges everything we know about black hole growth.

Sources indicate that the trouble arises before the universe was 1 billion years. That is because, according to current models, black holes should need at least 1 billion years to feed and merge enough to reach masses millions or billions of times that of the sun.

Yet, since it began operations in 2022, the JWST has been routinely discovering supermassive black holes powering quasars as early as 400 million years after the Significant Bang. If that wasn't confusing enough, the discovery of Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua, the third quasar pair seen at Cosmic Dawn, could really break current models.

Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua was uncovered in data from the JWST's Aether survey, which is conducting a census of objects in the early universe. Using JWST’s NIRSpec (Near-Infrared Spectrograph Integral Field Unit) instrument, the survey has uncovered 200 quasars, just under half of all currently known early universe quasars. It was while browsing the Aether dataset that the team discovered that quasar J1602+4228A is not alone, it had a companion now designated J1602+4228B.

According to recent reports, resolving these two quasars should have been nearly impossible from the ground. But this was possible for Gemini North thanks to perfect timing and perfect weather conditions over Maunakea, the dormant volcano on the island of Hawai'i where the telescope is located.

A definite scientific feat, Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua remains a mystery for now, but it could actually help scientists better understand how galaxies were coming together during Cosmic Dawn, a vital stage in the evolution of the universe.

"Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua is a really unique environment," Onorato noted. "It's a laboratory for astronomers to study how the very first massive galaxies and their central black holes assembled together through direct galaxy interactions during these early times.".

The team's results were published on Tuesday (Nov. 10) The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

Robert Lea is a science journalist in the U.K. whose articles have been published in Physics World, New Scientist, Astronomy Magazine, All About Space, Newsweek and ZME Science. He also writes about science communication for Elsevier and the European Journal of Physics. Rob holds a bachelor of science degree in physics and astronomy from the U.K.’s Open University. Follow him on Twitter @sciencef1rst.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the latest James Bond revision is shocking. Positively shocking.

After years of speculation as to who would be holstering the Walther PPK and asking for his martini shaken, not stirred, Robert Pattinson is grabbing the keys to the Aston Martin as the titular secret agent.

Several leading men have vied for the role, with Daniel Craig last pouring himself a glass of Macallan in 2021's No Time to Die. In fact, Jack Lowden—whose Slow Horses costar Gary Oldman publicly threw his support behind—Callum Turner, Jacob Elordi, Henry Cavill and Damson Idris were just a few names that sparked casting rumors.

Although the actors' involvement was simply speculation over the years, former Bond Pierce Brosnan—who headlined GoldenEye, Tomorrow Never Dies, The World Is Not Enough and Die Another Day between 1995 and 2002—believes Aaron Taylor-Johnson could keep the British end up.

Sources indicate that "I think he would be very good," he reflected in an April 2025 interview with Yahoo! Entertainment, adding that they costarred in a 2009 film that he also executive produced. "I cast him in one of the movies I made a long time ago called The Greatest, actually, and he played the Greatest.".

"This young man came on the set," Brosnan recalled of the then-18-year-old actor, "and took the space, filled the space with passion and energy. So yeah, I think if he wished it, wanted it and got it, he would be great.".

For Taylor-Johnson's part, however, he doesn't have an inflated opinion of himself when it comes to the possibility of the prestigious honor.

Industry observers note that "It's not really for me to say anything," the now-36-year-old told Esquire in August 2023. "I just focus on the things I can have my hands in right now. What's in front of me right now.".

Identity Confirmed pic.twitter.com/FCU5A9c1wk.

Although several celebs have been fancast as the 007 agent, the opportunity is quite daunting. For instance, Theo James isn't sure if he's up for the pressure.

According to recent reports, "Everyone's interested in that because it's a big part of British cultural identity, but that probably wouldn't be me," he admitted to The Guardian in March 2024. "I do think there are better people for that job. And, honestly, it would be terrifying: if you do that, there's no going back.".

Meanwhile, Glen Powell was adamant that anyone but him should take on the role since he's more suited for a cowboy hat than a tux.

Industry observers note that "I'm a Texan," he told The Hollywood Reporter in August. "My family and I joke around, I can play Jimmy Bond, but I should not be playing James Bond. Get an authentic Brit for that job. That's who belongs in that tuxedo.".

Airline ticket prices have surged this year, especially for travel over the holidays. Don't expect many bargains if you're booking flights with miles, either.

Tickets bought with frequent flyer miles for flights between large U.S. airports over the Thanksgiving travel period will cost 32% more than last year's holiday, according to data from Seats.aero, a miles and points redemption search site. While fares have skyrocketed this year, airline executives last month remarked demand remains strong.

Industry observers note that airlines have largely gotten rid of static mileage redemption charts in favor of dynamic pricing, making budgeting for an award ticket more difficult. Dynamic pricing means redemption costs change depending on demand, routes and other factors.

Many of the most expensive routes this Thanksgiving are understandably longer, including from Hawaii, but the list also includes a nonstop from New York to Houston.

Here's how mileage redemptions for the holiday are stacking up, based on one-way flights on average as of early November and compared with last year:.

It has been revealed that jet fuel prices have surged since the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran on Feb. 28, which has eaten into airline profits. Carriers have sought to pass costs along to consumers as much as possible.

Even some of the cheapest routes for award tickets are more expensive than last year, including for short routes like Tulsa, Oklahoma, to Dallas Fort Worth International Airport.

Through the daze of the Grammy nominations, Taylor Swift came back when it mattered.

According to recent reports, the 14-time Grammy winner made a surprise appearance during the nomination ceremony on Nov. 16, making sure the announcement of the final two categories hit just the perfect note.

Industry observers note that “Good morning America, it's Taylor,” Swift mentioned as she appeared on screen dressed in a simple back long sleeve shirt and necklaces. “I'm very honored that the Grammys have asked me to be here to help reveal the last two categories for the Grammy nominations.”.

“I first wanted to start off by saying congratulations to anyone who's nominated for a Grammy this year in any category,” she continued, “because what this means is that your peers, your fellow musicians, producers, engineers, artists, writers, they love what you made, and that's the coolest feeling in the world. I hope you have a really wonderful day.”.

She then revealed the last two categories of the ceremony were to be Album of the Year and Song of the Year—two categories, as she joked, she’s quite familiar with.

Industry observers note that "The last two categories to be confirmed—one of them I've had a lot of luck in,” the 36-year-old mentioned, before quipping. “The other one I'm zero for eight.”.

After all, she has been nominated for Album of the Year seven times—earning her eighth just seconds after her onscreen appearance for The Life of a Showgirl—and has won the category a record four times.

As for Song of the Year, the Midnights artist has indeed been nominated eight times but has yet to bring home the Grammy. Maybe the ninth time will prove the charm, having been nominated for “I Knew It, I Knew You,” the song she wrote for Toy Story 5.

She’s facing some stiff competition, however. Also nominated in the category are “Berghain” by Rosalía, Björk and Yves Tumor, “Choosin’ Texas” by Ella Langley, “The Cure” by Olivia Rodrigo, “Hate That I Made You Love Me” by Ariana Grande, “Man I Need” by Olivia Dean, “Risk It All” by Bruno Mars and “Where Is My Husband!” by Raye, who earned the most nominees of any artist with 11.

The Album of the Year battle will be easily as fraught, with powerhouses such as Phoebe Bridgers’ first album in six years, Lost Weekend, Dean’s The Art of Loving, Langley’s Dandelion, Mars’ The Romantic, Raye’s This Music May Contain Hope, Rodrigo’s You Seem Pretty Sad For a Girl So In Love and Rosalía’s Lux.

Industry observers note that but while some of these noms may have seemed assured, at every award show there are nominations that come as surprises and the notable absences that come as a shock. Read on for a look at this year’s Grammys snubs and surprises.

In a recent development, abrams failed to snag any nominations for her latest album Daughter From Hell, which she submitted for Album of the Year and Best Pop Vocal Album. Her single "Hit the Wall" was also absent from the Song of the Year, Record of the Year and Best Pop Solo Performance lists.

Abrams has previously received two nominations for Best New Artist in 2024 and Best Pop Duo Performance for "Us" which featured Taylor Swift in 2025.

While Grande picked up some surprise nominations for Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance for "For Good" alongside Cynthia Erivo, as well as Song of the Year and Best Music Video for "hate that I made you love me," and Best Pop Vocal Album for Petal, she was snubbed for Album of the Year.

Although Kahan scored one nomination for Best Contemporary Folk Album, he was not included in the major categories like Album of the Year and Song of the Year for his hit The Great Divide.

Beyoncé is famously the most decorated Grammy-winning artist—the 35-time winner scored her 100th nomination this year— but her Best R&B Solo Performance nod for "Morning Dew (Donk)" was somewhat of a surprise considering its delayed release in celebration of B'Day's 20th anniversary in July.

This year was significant for Hobert, who released her debut album Who's the Clown last year, but she failed to score a nod for Best Newly introduced Artist. (Her brother Malcolm Todd was also left off the shortlist.).

Surprise: The Devil Wears Prada 2.

In a recent development, that's actually not all for this much-anticipated sequel. The Devil Wears Prada 2 scored a surprise nomination for Best Compilation Soundtrack For Visual Media alongside Stranger Things season five, Wicked: For Good, The Wizard of Oz at the Sphere and Wuthering Heights.

It's been a long time coming for the first-time Grammy nominee, who scored her first nods for Best Dance/Electronic Recording for "Melatonin" as well as Best Dance Pop Recording for "Too Easy.".

In a recent development, swift wasn't totally snubbed by the Recording Academy—she earned nods for Record of the Year, Album of the Year, Song of the Year, Best Pop Duo Performance alongside Sabrina Carpenter, Best Song Written for a Visual Media and more. But The Life of a Showgirl was not among Best Pop Vocal Album contenders, while "I Knew It, I Knew You" was snubbed for Best Country Song and Best Country Solo Performance.

Still, it was a surprise to see "I Knew It, I Knew You" score a nomination for Song of the Year, a category introduced by Swift herself during the nomination livestream, given Swift's other hits from The Life of a Showgirl.

According to recent reports, the hype hasn't died down, Wicked is still oh so very popular. Wicked: For Good scored two nominations including Best Song Written For Visual Media and Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance.

Industry observers note that disco All The Time, Grammy Occasionally. The "Aperture" singer failed to score recognition for his latest album in any category. Styles has three Grammy wins under his belt, including Album of the Year for Harry's House in 2023.

It has been revealed that her comeback is far from over. The pop star received her first Grammy nominations in 16 years, racking up nods for Best Dance Pop Recording, Best Dance/Electronic Recording, Best Dance/Electronic Album and Best Pop Duo/Group Performance for "Bring Your Love" alongside Carpenter.

Although Lefty rose to massive acclaim this year for hits like "Boston," she failed to receive any recognition by The Recording Academy.

Following a two-year hiatus, West scored a nod for Best Rap Album for Bully.

#829. Breaking: The 'eclipse of the century' will plunge these 8 wonders of the Roman Empire into darkness on Aug. 2, 2027

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1259 w)
