Homophobia on the rise in football - what is your club doing about it?

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1753 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rainbow laces were a common sight for several years across football and other sports.
  • Homophobia and transphobia are on the rise in English football, with latest data revealing record numbers of discrimination reports in the game - so what is the Premier League doing about it?
  • Last season, with little fanfare, the league introduced a fresh LGBTQ+ celebratory activation in February, Premier League With Pride.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rainbow laces were a common sight for several years across football and other sports.

Warning: this article contains offensive language.

Homophobia and transphobia are on the rise in English football, with latest data revealing record numbers of discrimination reports in the game - so what is the Premier League doing about it?

Last season, with little fanfare, the league introduced a fresh LGBTQ+ celebratory activation in February, Premier League With Pride.

The lowkey launch contrasts with the landscape of a few years ago, when England internationals like Jordan Henderson and Conor Coady were proudly proclaiming their allyship.

"The one thing it [Premier League With Pride last season] was lacking was engagement from players," remarked Jon Holmes, founder and lead of news organisation and campaign group Sports Media LGBT+.

In a recent development, "Not only would you have the rainbow armbands, but clearer allyship from players - that was more around the late 2010s. That has been in decline.".

Recent findings suggest that A report last month from anti-discrimination charity Kick It Out says they received a fresh high of 1,744 discrimination reports during the 2025-26 season, a 25% increase on the previous campaign. In this, reports of homophobia rose 46% to 203.

Kick It Out noted it had received 142 reports of discriminatory mass chanting during the season, a 41% increase on 2024-25 and the highest number recorded. These reports included increases in homophobic and transphobic chants.

In a recent development, A prime example is the 'rent boy' chant predominantly aimed at Chelsea players and fans, for which incidents had dropped since it was criminalised in 2022. However, the combined 24 reports of homophobic chanting in 2025-26 season were the most in three years.

According to Kick It Out,, external many of the incidents over the past few seasons can be linked to domestic and world events, such as the Supreme Court ruling on gender leading to the FA's ban on transgender women in the women's game, which it states led to a spike in transphobic abuse.

What are the Premier League doing about rising homophobia in English football?

BBC Sport asked all 20 Premier League clubs what diversity policies they have regarding the LGBTQ+ community, and how much of their budget is dedicated to such schemes.

Nine clubs responded to the BBC request. None stated how much money they invest in these areas.

A Nottingham Forest spokesperson told BBC Sport: "The club commits significant funding to this key area, and has an Equality, Diversity and Inclusion lead whose role is dedicated to ensuring inclusion is at the heart of everything we do.".

Recent findings suggest that some clubs do visibly engage with their local LGBTQ+ community. Leeds United have been a sponsor of the city's Pride celebrations since 2018. Luke Ayling, then Leeds captain, marched in the Pride parade in 2022.

Liverpool and Brighton are annually represented in their city's extensive Pride events, as are the Manchester clubs.

Manchester City host an annual Progress flag-raising ceremony, while Manchester United stated staff marched in the city centre parade. They also ran a flag competition with LGBTQ+ supporters' club Rainbow Devils, with the winning design displayed at Old Trafford for all matchdays.

Tottenham said that at the start of 2024, Spurs in the Community helped launch a weekly football session for members of the LGBTQ+ community.

And for the first time this season, all 20 current Premier League clubs have dedicated fan groups for LGBTQ+ supporters.

In a recent development, "It feels like there is a renaissance in the LGBT fan movement," said Holmes. "There is a rise in homophobia, but it does seem like the authorities are sitting up and taking notice. We can feel a degree of optimism.".

But it is difficult for Premier League teams to encourage LGBTQ+ allyship and diversity, when representation within clubs is a mixed bag at best.

According to Kick It Out, which gathered data on the senior management teams from 17 out of the 20 current Premier League clubs, just 0.3% of people in those roles openly identify as LGBTQ+ - well below the UK population average according to latest national census data, with 4% of the British population identifying as LGBTQ+.

At a senior coaching level, from 11 clubs which responded there is no-one from the LGBTQ+ community.

Kick It Out says, comparing the dataset to relevant census data, that if football's workforce was truly representative of local communities, over 100 more people from the LGBTQ+ community would have to be employed at Premier League clubs.

The first Premier League With Pride event included rainbow branding at grounds - but nothing involving players.

The Premier League previously had a high profile association with LGBTQ+ charity Stonewall's Rainbow Laces campaign - but this was ended before the 2025-26 season.

It has been revealed that rainbow Laces started in 2014-15 as a collaboration between Stonewall, Paddy Power and the Premier League. For two game weeks, usually around the end of November, players would wear rainbow-coloured laces or armbands, and the colourful branding would be seen in grounds and on broadcast idents.

Holmes said by the end it was doing more harm than good.

"I think the novelty of Rainbow Laces wore off," he told BBC Sport. "It also became more newsworthy to talk about the controversies; it became more difficult for players to engage without difficult questions.

"Also, club media departments are more risk averse, given growing toxicity on social media.

"It has been misconstrued that players were forced to engage, I think it was because Rainbow Laces became de rigueur, and it was perceived that captains would need to lead with the armband and allyship.".

Rainbow armbands were introduced in 2017 for captains, having first been worn by MLS club Orlando City following the mass shooting at Pulse, an LGBTQ+ nightclub, in the city in 2016.

But the Premier League held its final Rainbow Laces campaign from 29 November to 5 December, 2024, and it was surrounded by controversy.

Marc Guehi, then Crystal Palace captain, wrote 'I Love Jesus' on his armband in what was widely viewed as a protest against wearing the armband (which was not mandatory).

Ipswich captain Sam Morsy refused to wear the armband, while Manchester United scrapped aims for a Rainbow Laces-themed jacket during the pre-match ceremonies following an objection by Noussair Mazraoui.

Simon Blake, CEO of Stonewall, admitted to BBC Sport that by the end of its 12-year lifespan in the Premier League, Rainbow Laces in that form had run its course.

It has been revealed that "When it started, getting a few people to wear the laces was success," he noted. "When it ended, when a few people didn't wear them there was criticism.

"If a campaign no longer has a positive vibe, perhaps it is time to do something different.

"Everything must evolve and change, but visibility still matters, it is vital not to throw the baby out with the bathwater.".

Sources indicate that stonewall held its first ever Rainbow Laces Day on 8 October this year, to encourage LGBTQ+ people to engage with sport. It had no connection with the Premier League.

Marc Guehi and Crystal Palace did not face any action after he wrote on his rainbow armband.

It is notable that the players most ardently against Rainbow Laces were also vocal in their religious beliefs.

Guehi has spoken of the importance in his life of his faith and was one of several devout Christian players in the Crystal Palace dressing room. Both Morsy and Mazraoui are practicing Muslims.

Both Holmes and Blake acknowledge that this may have had an impact on Rainbow Laces.

"The influence of religion is clearly quite significant, but I think more understanding is coming in too," remarked Holmes.

It has been revealed that "We have seen many parts of life less willing to engage with Pride, and football reflects that. The nature of LGBT campaigns is peaks and troughs, and we are in a trough.".

"We don't have any specific data about what people's beliefs and views are, but we are in a world where people have different views, even within religions themselves," added Blake.

"The notable thing is about behaviours, and we must learn to live with people who have these different beliefs and respect them.

"I don't want to speculate, as it would be too easy to assume people of faith would not be inclusive, I know from my work across 30 years that is not true; I have worked with many religious people who are LGBTQ+ supportive. Freedom of belief is important.".

The current picture is a difficult one for gay and trans people in football at all levels.

According to recent reports, the grassroots game is where the bulk of the increase in abuse has occurred, says Kick It Out, which claims it received 140% more reports last year than in the 2024-25 season. Three quarters of these reports are from senior grassroots games, where the players are over 18.

It has been revealed that away from football, research by Stonewall published in October found 11% of LGBTQ+ people in the UK avoid the gym, exercise classes or sports groups for fear of discrimination. Among trans people, the figure rises to 29%.

It mentioned 15% of LGBTQ+ people who had been to a live sporting event, or watched sport in a bar, in the past year had experienced discrimination there. This rose to 26% for trans people.

"What we know is that there is a lot of work going on around equality and diversity; we also know homophobia and transphobia continue to be rife," Blake noted.

Industry observers note that "We are in a world, whether at Premier League or grassroots football, where views that may have been perceived to be unacceptable are now being expressed freely. That influences peoples' relationship with sport.".

Premier League With Pride will return in 2026-27.

"The matchday activations take place in February in line with LGBTQ+ History Month, when the league and clubs will showcase their commitment to LGBTQ+ inclusion," a Premier League spokesperson told BBC Sport.

"There will be two match rounds dedicated to Premier League With Pride. This means all 20 clubs have a home game during that period, providing an opportunity to highlight and celebrate the LGBTQ+ community in football and showcase the work undertaken to make the game more inclusive.

"There is no centralised activation lined up for November.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Diallo confirmed by Uefa as its chosen candidate.

He accused Infantino of seriously damaging football.

The French Football Federation president, Philippe Diallo, has been confirmed as Uefa’s surprise late choice to run for the Fifa presidency. The search for a Uefa-backed candidate to challenge Gianni Infantino was taken to the wire, with Wednesday the deadline for those planning to contest the Fifa election in March.

“At a meeting held today and chaired by Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin, the national associations represented on the Uefa executive committee and the Fifa council invited Philippe Diallo, president of the French Football Federation (FFF), to stand as a candidate in the Fifa presidential election in March 2027 and unanimously pledged their full support,” a statement remarked.

Diallo emerged as the favourite after plans to enlist a decorated former player or manager did not reach fruition. Uefa said the 63-year-old had accepted the invitation and that his candidacy was due to be ratified by the FFF on Tuesday.

Diallo strongly criticised Infantino in September, saying he had “seriously damaged the image and unity of football”. He continued: “His initiatives during and after the World Cup have seriously damaged the image and the unity of football. As a result, we believe that trust has been broken.”.

In a recent development, it is unclear whether the move to back Diallo will spell the end of the campaign begun by Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japanese Football Association, to challenge Infantino. Tashima, a Fifa council member, has influential backers within Uefa but its hierarchy appears to feel Diallo has a greater chance of wooing voters in other areas of the world.

In the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.

If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.

If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from the iOS App Store on iPhone or the Google Play store on Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.

Diallo is expected to win the backing of the vast majority of Uefa’s member associations and there are hopes he could pick up votes from Francophone members of the Confederation of African Football, which has been steadfast in its support for Infantino.

There are concerns that having multiple challengers to Infantino will strengthen his position and play into the hands of a campaign that will present the incumbent as the unity candidate after months of in-fighting.

Concacaf, the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation, has been reluctant to endorse an alternative candidate, despite opposing Infantino, with some federations arguing that a boycott of the election would send the strongest message regarding the need for governance reform.

Diallo getting Uefa’s backing represents a marked departure from its original approach, in which it sought to coalesce behind a more high-profile figure who had made their name on the pitch or in the dugout. There had been late hope that Arsène Wenger, Fifa’s chief of global development, would throw put himself forward, but it would have required a major change of heart from him. Former players such as Mikaël Silvestre and, belatedly, Didier Drogba are understood to have expressed interest that never came to anything.

Diallo is a career administrator who has worked in French football since 1992, chairing the clubs’ lobby group Union des Clubs Professionnels de Football (UCPF) for almost 30 years before joining the FFF in 2021. He was elected president two years later in what was regarded in France as a shock victory, having initially stepped up in an interim capacity. Diallo joined Uefa’s executive committee in the same year.

Germany’s head coach, Jürgen Klopp, has said he would welcome a newly introduced president. “The general consensus is that a change might make sense. But what would interest me even more in this context, from a football perspective, is that we never thought things could get any worse after Sepp Blatter, and yet someone actually managed to make it worse.

“Right now, we’re thinking that if Mr Infantino were to leave, it would be cool if the next person could just do a better job. Because I believe it should be possible to do better.”.

Jen Affleck's new secret weapon is putting herself first.

As the Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star navigates her divorce from Zac Affleck while pregnant with their fourth baby, she decided to treat herself to some R&R under the Hawaiian sun.

“Finally made it to Maui,” Jen captioned a Nov. 16 Instagram Story. “Taking this time to slow down and soak in every little moment.".

“I'm not doing the best right now,” she stated to E! News in an exclusive interview earlier in November. “I'm just taking one day at a time, and really just focusing on my kids. And obviously, the timing sucks, especially with me being pregnant.".

In fact, she feels more herself than ever—and her time filming the spinoff series was just the start of that.

"I feel like for the past seven, eight years of my life, I've tried to mold myself into who I think people want to see, whether it be for my marriage or for TV or for the world,” the 27-year-old said. According to recent reports, as for Zac, he previously shared insight into his and Jen’s split in the wake of her Nov. 3 divorce filing.

Noting that he learned about the filing from TMZ, Zac confessed the split was "something we've been talking about for a long time.".

He also admitted, "I still love Jen," identifying her "light" and "good heart" as the reasons he fell in love in the first place.

As such, the decision to go their separate ways romantically has weighed on Zac, especially as he feels disappointed for their four children.

"The thing that's eating me alive the most is I feel like I've just I feel like I failed my kids," he continued. "I'm worried that I'm going to cause them damage, and I just hope that we can still give them a normal childhood.".

He ultimately attributed their fallout to the result of when "life happened" but also mentioned that in his eyes, the Hulu series had become "a show that's really hurt a lot of people's lives.".

Read on for where the rest of the SLOMW couples stand.

Taylor Frankie Paul & Dakota Mortensen: Broken Up.

While Taylor Frankie Paul's romance with Dakota Mortensen—they welcomed son Ever in 2024—bloomed on The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, they called it quits due to Dakota's infidelity.

"Right after Ever was born, Dakota and I were living together and in bliss with our newly introduced baby, and I was even considering engagement," Taylor—who began dating the real estate agent in July 2022—revealed during the season two premiere of the Hulu series. "And then I learned that he was lying this entire time.".

Taylor was told by a woman named Jenna that she and Dakota had been intimate and he had "spent the night more than once." (He has denied the claims, writing in a September 2024 TikTok that he "never cheated.").

On the series, Taylor remarked that Dakota accused Jenna of instigating their affair.

"No, it was him," she emphasized in the confessional. "He said he had just kissed her on the couch. No, he went on the couch, they hooked up on the couch, and then they went to the room and they hooked up.".

Since ending her romance with the Basin Tiling founder, the mom of three (she shares two kids with ex-husband Tate Paul) was set to find love once again on season 22 of The Bachelorette, but things got a bit thorny when news broke in March 2026 of an alleged confrontation between the exes weeks earlier.

A spokesperson for the Draper City Police Department confirmed to People that there was an open "domestic assault investigation," telling the outlet "allegations have been made in both directions.”.

Days later, a video of a previous 2023 physical altercation between Taylor and Dakota surfaced online, prompting ABC to cancel the MomToker's season of the dating franchise.

As for Dakota, he has kicked off a romance with show guest star Shinia Powell, though he previously apologized to Taylor for hooking up with her during a season four episode.

Whitney Leavitt & Connor Leavitt: Married.

Whitney Leavitt found the perfect dance partner in Connor Leavitt, whom she wed in 2016. But it wasn't always smooth sailing for the couple—who share kids Sedona, Liam and Billy—as they navigated life in the spotlight.

For instance, the Dancing With the Stars alum, who announced during her Broadway run in May 2026 that she'd be leaving Mormon Wives, had to shut down rumors about her husband's sexuality.

"Do I need to put out a sex tape, or something? Like, trust me," she noted on the Off the Vine podcast in October 2024. "We're good. Everything's fine.".

Sources indicate that "I think it's because when we were going through our personal stuff—and I know you haven't seen it—but he struggled through a porn addiction," she explained. "There's a scene where one of my friends states something along the lines of how they could see how he was confused sexually.".

Through the ups and downs, the reality star emphasized that she and Connor—who were 23 and 22, respectively, when they got married—are stronger than ever. In fact, they even renewed their vows in February 2026 for their 10th wedding anniversary.

Recent findings suggest that "We got married really young," Conner told Brides after their ceremony. "It felt like our wedding day, as much as it was for us, it really felt like it was for our families. So we really want to do something to make it ours, and this felt like a really fun way to do it.".

Jen Affleck & Zac Affleck: Divorcing.

Married in 2019, Jen Affleck and Zac Affleck—no relation to Ben Affleck, despite jokes to the contrary—have been at the center of breakup rumors since SLOMW's debut.

In fact, their fight after Jen attended a Chippendales striptease show in Las Vegas became a focal point of the first season. The couple—who share kids Nora, Penelope and Lucas—made up, however, and the Dancing With the Stars contestant later defended their relationship.

Industry observers note that "It can be tiring and draining, just because it gets old having to hear the same things," Jen told E! News of the speculations in November 2025. "For me, I'm like, 'People will always talk and people will always have their opinions.' I think it is frustrating for him when people don't see what's happening behind closed doors and how much work and effort he's putting in.".

It has been revealed that but while Jen announced in June 2026 that she'd be adding to their dance troupe with baby No. 4, the MomToker filed for divorce that November after seven years of marriage.

Jessi Draper & Jordan Ngatikaura: Divorced.

Bumps in Jessi Draper and Jordan Ngatikaura's five-year marriage emerged after the hairstylist admitted to having an emotional affair with Vanderpump Villa's Marciano Brunette, though initially it appeared they were working towards smoother roads.

According to recent reports, "We are back together," Jessi—who shares kids Jagger and Jovi with Jordan—told E! News in November 2025. "We're trying to work on it. Relationships are not perfect. I think a situation like ours—it's going to take time. It's not going to something that's just amazing overnight.".

Sadly, the reconciliation appeared to be short-lived, with Jordan also dad to daughter Peyton from a previous relationship, filing for divorce in March 2026 after five years of marriage.

However, days later, Jessi remarked she was “blindsided” by his filing and accused him of rushing to submit the paperwork because “he wanted the headline first.”.

In a recent development, admitting that her “heart sunk” seeing the news, she explained, “because we agreed to tell our children together before filing and we haven’t done that.” (E! reached out to attorneys for Jordan for comment but haven’t heard back.).

Though Jessi told E! News that she was "just casually dating and living life," when she brought Marciano as her date to the 2026 American Music Awards in May 2026, he revealed a tattoo dedicated to her that August.

Jessi and Jordan finalized their divorce in September 2026.

Mayci Neeley & Jacob Neeley: Married.

Mayci didn't expect to find love with Jacob Neeley. In fact, after the unexpected death of her boyfriend Arik Mack in 2015, when she was just 14 weeks pregnant with their son Hudson, she was prepared to be a single mom.

But it all changed when she met Jacob in 2016 at age 21, whom she would marry two years later.

"After everything I'd been through, I was very guarded, but Jacob was kind and we got on really well," Mayci stated in her memoir Told You So. "For a long time, we remained just friends and because we weren't really dating, I was OK with him meeting my son.".

It has been revealed that "Jacob was amazing with him, which made him appear even more attractive," she continued. "I was terrified of getting hurt again but, after four months, I couldn't deny my feelings any longer. He was kind and funny and made me feel safe.".

Mayci and Jacob went on to welcome daughters Harlow in 2021 and Charli in 2025.

Demi Engemann & Bret Engemann: Married.

Demi Engemann and her husband Bret Engemann tied the knot in 2021, one year after she and Blake Corbin divorced. As the couple's relationship played out on the reality show, their sexual explorations became a major plot point after Whitney gifted Demi a box of Fruity Pebbles.

The truth behind the joke gift wasn't revealed until Jessi shared on Instagram in November 2025 that "grandpa Bret likes to drink her piss like it's dirty soda and he gulps it down like water.".

But Demi and Bret aren't crying over spilled secrets—or pee. In fact, she told Entertainment Tonight that December that she and Bret "have nothing else left to do other than own it and have fun with it.".

Sources indicate that although their sex life raised eyebrows, the couple has been embracing life with their blended family. While Demi shares daughter Maude with her ex, Bret is dad to his and The Real Housewives of Salt Lake City alum Angie Harrington's sons Rome and Cole.

"I've never seen a dad so involved or love their kids harder, the most devoted step-dad to Maude, and future father to our own children one day," Demi wrote on Instagram in June 2024. "Your ability to remain consistently loyal to your role as father/step-father while navigating all that life throws your way, will never cease to amaze me!".

Mikayla Matthews & Jace Terry: Married.

Mikayla Matthews and Jace Terry have been through it all together. While The reality star first met Jace in 2015 when she was 15 and they welcomed their first son Beckham two years later. Since then, the couple—who tied the knot in 2018—welcomed kids Haven, Tommie and Lottie.

While Mikayla and Jace have been loving life with their four kids, Mikayla admitted that she hopes to grow their family even further.

"When people ask me how many kids I want, I'm like, 'I've always wanted three or four, but I could see myself having six,'" she told People in February 2025. "I'm excited to hopefully move into a fresh house. I want a big lot for my herd of kids.".

However, Mikayla confirmed in the ninth episode of the show's fourth season that she and Jace were taking time apart amid ongoing intimacy struggles.

As Mikayla began unpacking her trauma surrounding years of sexual abuse as a teen, as well as her chronic illness—which causes flare-ups due to heightened stress—their marriage had been deeply affected.

But the tides have officially turned on their connection as the reality star shared during the show's fifth season that she and Jace are back on track.

"I feel like I got a lot more clarity," she said in a confessional on the show, "and so I was able to express more what I needed to Jace.".

And, as she added, “He’s been very supportive.”.

Layla Taylor & Clayton Wessel: Divorced.

After Layla Taylor and Clayton Wessel—who are parents to sons Oliver and Maxwell—divorced in 2023, the reality star teased her new romance with Mason McWhorter in July 2025.

Their relationship was a bit complicated on paper. Hang with us: Mason's brother is Chase McWhorter, the ex-husband of Layla's costar Miranda McWhorter. But the pair had been willing to put their romance to the test.

"Right now, I'm kind of scared of marriage but I just want to get to know somebody very well before I even consider that," Layla told Us in November 2025. "I'm just happy and content where me and Mason are. And if somehow that ever were to come up, then we would see.".

Unfortunately, the mom of two confirmed that she and Mason had split in February 2026.

In a recent development, "I think we were just on two different paths right now, and he felt in order for him to grow, he had to be on his own," Layla shared. "I respect his decision, and I truly hope that he gets what he wants in life.".

As for Layla, who came out as bisexual in June 2026, she soft-rolled out her romance with a mystery woman a month later in an Instagram video. She later seemed to confirm her relationship with Colorado-based content creator Kelsie Chesser.

Miranda McWhorter & Chase McWhorter: Divorced.

Although Miranda is a newer addition to The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, joining in season two, she played a major role in the infamous MomTok "soft swinging scandal." Despite the situation with Taylor, Miranda revealed that drama wasn't the reason for her 2024 breakup from Chase.

Industry observers note that "The reasons why we decided to split were things that were concerns far before that,” she explained on the Weekly Trash podcast in August 2024. "That might not have helped, for sure, but it definitely did not play a part in the decision process.".

Nonetheless, she and Chase have been committed to parenting their kids Brooks and Cohen.

Recent findings suggest that "With co-parenting, you're always having to work on it," she reflected. “The thing is that if we got along perfectly all the time and it was just rainbows and butterflies, we probably wouldn't have gotten divorced.".

"The thing with him and I," she continued, "we've always had a pretty good foundation of a friendship prior to even having a romantic relationship. I feel like that's something that set us up for some level of success when it comes to co-parenting.".

Though Miranda and Chase broke up in 2024, the former filed for divorce in 2026.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Liverpool full-back Neco Williams has 67 Wales caps, scoring five goals.

Wales will be without right-back Neco Williams for their final Nations League group match against reigning champions Portugal on Tuesday (19:45 GMT), while goalkeeper Karl Darlow is a doubt.

Nottingham Forest's Williams has been ruled out after he was injured during Saturday's 3-1 defeat in Norway, while Manchester United's Darlow missed training on Monday and will be assessed further.

Midfielder Ethan Ampadu will also miss out at Cardiff City Stadium because of suspension, but centre-back Ben Cabango and winger Sorba Thomas are available after serving one-match bans.

Wales will finish bottom of Group A4 whatever happens against leaders Portugal, and Craig Bellamy's side will have a relegation play-off in March against one of the League B runners-up for a place in the top tier.

According to recent reports, "One or two players had to come off through injury [in Norway]. One or two have come through; one or two haven't," said Bellamy.

Industry observers note that "Neco's going to be out. Darlow, we'll wait and see later, and everyone else is fully fit.".

What Wales need to stay in Nations League top tier.

With less riding on this fixture than there might have been, Bellamy could be tempted to make further changes to his side from the loss in Oslo.

Cardiff City attacking midfielder Rubin Colwill shone as a substitute, while Bournemouth's David Brooks came off the bench to score an excellent goal.

Colwill's performance was a particularly popular talking point among fans, many of whom have long been calling for the 24-year-old playmaker to feature more regularly for Wales.

Recent findings suggest that "Rubin's been pushing [to start] for a while," noted Bellamy. "Once you get this kid in the final third, then he's a player. We've just got to get him in those areas.

"But he's also got to offer us without the ball as well. If you're not good without the ball, you cannot be a top player.

"If you want a lesson tomorrow without the ball, watch Vitinha [Portugal's Paris St-Germain midfielder] if he plays.

"Rubin has moved [up a level] and long may that continue, because if it does Wales have got a brilliant player.

"I'm more harsh on Rubin because I've known him since he was so young, but credit to him and his manager at Cardiff [Brian Barry-Murphy].

"He's helping develop a real player for us that's going to hopefully have a huge impact for the next five to 10 years.".

Highlights: Norway beat Wales in Oslo.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We've had no shortage of great Warhammer 40K games lately, but most aren't exactly aimed at the casual crowd. Warhammer Survivors changes that, finally providing curious gamers with an easy entry point into the grim darkness of the 41st millennium.

Sources indicate that developed by Auroch Digital (in collaboration with Vampire Survivors' Poncle), this new spin on the survivors-like roguelite subgenre mixes the sci-fi 40,000 setting with the pure fantasy Age of Sigmar universe. This means heroes and enemies from all over the Warhammer mythos meet together in a bite-sized game that anyone can figure out and enjoy in less than five minutes.

When you look at the alternatives, that's a remarkable achievement for a franchise that's notoriously hard (and often expensive) to get into.

Sources indicate that warhammer Survivors isn't bogged down by dense lore, involved mechanics, or massive campaign playthroughs. It's more of an "inspired by" effort that gives casuals a small taste of the series' iconic characters — including Boltgun's Malum Caedo — and factions like the terrifying Tyranids, the raucous Orks, and the foul forces of Chaos.

All of 40K's (and Age of Sigmar's) recognizable elements are on display, but they serve more as flavoring sprinkled on top of Vampire Survivors' successful formula.

It has been revealed that if you're new to the Survivors-like subgenre, it's a unique gaming experience. You battle an endless onslaught of enemies that slowly march towards you, with your character passively attacking automatically. You only need to move them around sprawling arenas and select level-up upgrades and items after collecting enough gems (skulls in this case).

The moment-to-moment gameplay is as simple as it can get outside of walking sims and interactive "experiences," but there's a deceiving depth to item synergies and how to correctly "build" characters to endure all the carnage.

According to recent reports, unlike Poncle's original game, Warhammer Survivors struggles a bit to get going. The early hours are sluggish until you unlock certain meta upgrades, but its still got that Vampire Survivors magic at its core.

As far as "podcast/gym games" go, this is a perfect fit. There's just enough going on to keep one's brain engaged, but minimal inputs and a tight overarching design lead to a rhythm that's easy to get into without using much brainpower. It's oddly satisfying to weave through enemies and level up your firepower, watching a single Astra Militarum grunt grow into a full Lasgun-spamming, chainsword-wielding wrecking ball.

Sources indicate that achievement and unlock hunters will find enough to bite into here, too. It's unclear if the devs will continue to add more Warhammer 40K and Age of Sigmar deep cuts to this game via DLCs and free updates, but those universes have daunting depths to explore. This really could become a gateway game for future 40K fans: by the time they realize they're hooked, they'll already have 2000 pts of space marines painted and ready to play.

It has been revealed that as massive sci-fi and fantasy properties try to aggressively expand and absorb more and more fans, it's easy to pander to already-converted diehards too much. And sure, we can't wait for strategy heavyweights like Dawn of War 4 and Total War: WH40K either, but they're hardly good recommendations for folks who don't even know what a Space Marine is or why the robotic Necrons are so grumpy.

Warhammer Survivors won't answer those questions beyond the surface-level iconography, but it's fun enough to push those curious to dig deeper and embrace the same material in more mature video game genres... and maybe even pick up a few miniatures.

Warhammer Survivors is now available on PC (Steam & GOG), PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch 1/2, and mobile (iOS & Android). It's also playable on Game Pass.

Tech Report: Tuchel and England must learn lessons of history, Seville and Southgateism | Barney Ronay

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1637 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Another 3-2 win in Spain brings the lure of a golden latest hyper-future – but it did not pan out that way last time.
  • I may have the body of a weak and feeble German, but I have the heart and stomach of a manager of England.
  • The words, there, of Thomas Tuchel, England’s Faerie King, speaking to TalkSport shortly after the glorious 3-2 defeat of the Spanish possession armada at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Another 3-2 win in Spain brings the lure of a golden latest hyper-future – but it did not pan out that way last time.

I may have the body of a weak and feeble German, but I have the heart and stomach of a manager of England. And I think it foul scorn that Spain should dare to invade the borders of my realm. Or, for that matter, any one of 24 qualified teams for Euro 2028, because at the end of the day there are no easy games at this level, I’ve always mentioned that.

The words, there, of Thomas Tuchel, England’s Faerie King, speaking to TalkSport shortly after the glorious 3-2 defeat of the Spanish possession armada at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid.

Recent findings suggest that OK, Tuchel didn’t technically say any of this. He was instead wry and spiky. He made a joke about people moaning about his team on the radio, which just goes to show he’s a good lad and one of us (disclaimer: when he wins). But this is England. And beating Spain can do some strange things to you.

Not just because Spain are the defining team of the past 20 years, six-time international trophy winners and current world and European champions. But because Spanish football culture is the global template for tone, texture and tactics, the ultimate source of the Football Association’s slightly dog‑eared footballing blueprint.

Beating Spain is like beating your super-smart but slightly controlling younger brother. It’s getting one over on that other way of playing, punitive high technique, death by possession, patience over urgency. Even better, Tuchel’s team did so in Madrid with a performance based around the hard‑running physicality that English football sees as part of its deep sporting soul.

As such it will be tempting to see this Nations League victory as a springboard, a Rubicon crossed, a shattering of the Iberian ceiling. With some justification; England have the talent to win a home European Championship two years from now. But it feels just a little bit easier to visualise now.

In a recent development, there was something upcoming in seeing Spain not just outmuscled but outplayed in the first half, reduced to whinging about fouls, unable to take the ball away. Not only because England’s pressing was smart and relentless but because of the players’ ability to keep possession in tight spaces.

It is also true that a quick glance back at recent history tells us exactly how much of a golden dawn a win such as this can be. Which is: zero, zilch, nothing. No golden dawn at all.

In reality there are no Rubicon moments, no decisive levellings-up, only staging posts and warning signs, even in victory. This is the most crucial point about a night such as this. It won’t tell you where you’ll end up. But it may tell you how to keep heading the right way, if you’re ready to learn from recent history.

It has been revealed that as it happens, recent history is in the room with us right now, clearing its throat, rattling its chains, trying to shift the Ouija-board dial. Here is an interesting fact. Spain have only twice conceded three goals at home in a competitive men’s international. The second time was on Sunday night, when England won 3-2 in Madrid after going 3-0 up. And the first time was 15 October 2018 when England beat Spain 3-2 in Seville after going 3-0 up.

The parallels between those games are numerically improbable. At the time of win No 1 Gareth Southgate had been in permanent charge for 684 days and one narrow World Cup semi-final defeat. Spain was his 29th game. At the time of win No 2 Tuchel had been in charge for 683 days and another narrow World Cup semi-final defeat. Spain was Tuchel’s 28th game.

That Southgate moment was greeted with understandable optimism. You know the kind of language used because it’s out here now, too. New dawns. Statement victories. Rise of a Golden Generation. Not just a benchmark but a springboard as well, an astonishing feat of carpentry if true.

So was it that? Answer: no. In fact Seville 2018 was arguably the moment Southgate-ism reached a stylistic ceiling. England played a fast-paced game of counterattack that night. The team was an attacking mix, a midfield of Winks‑Barkley‑Dier, with Sterling‑Kane‑Rashford in front. England scored 27 goals in six games the following autumn, starting most with a back four and a double pivot, ending 2019 with a 6-0, a 7-0 and a 4-0. This felt like something new.

The Covid break pretty much killed that mini-era. Or rather, it was allowed to kill it, because coaches have choices too. England went 42 weeks without a game. By November 2020 they were losing 2-0 in Belgium with a back five and a deep defensive midfield.

Sources indicate that the Euros had already been postponed for a year. In the summer of 2021 England started the final against Italy with another back five plus Declan Rice and Kalvin Phillips, and congealed into a kind of footballing rice pudding as the game reached its crisis point.

Industry observers note that here is an unprovable counterfactual. If football had rolled on, if England had not had an empty year to look down and get scared, they might have retained enough momentum to go harder against Italy in that final and win it.

But then, the Southgate era was gruelling for many of those players. There is a separate study to be made of the way so many key early Garethistas disappeared or entered a slow decline. That October 2018 team turned out to be a pop‑up thing of shifting parts, evidence of the complex, zigzagging nature of team building.

Industry observers note that the would-be golden generation included Ben Chilwell, Eric Dier, Joe Gomez, Ross Barkley, Harry Winks and Marcus Rashford. Nathaniel Chalobah made his only appearance as a sub in added time, and still has the second shortest England career, after Martin Kelly.

Recent findings suggest that rather than a golden dawn of ultimate glory, England entered a more talent-appropriate era of losing late-stage games against good opponents. If anything the Spain victory added to the ambient pressure around those tournaments, helping to create the sense it is now unthinkable for England to lose, because we have an image of them as winners, and English winning is the best winning, the only real winning.

In a recent development, the lesson remains the same now, the need to avoid both portents of doom and the lure of a golden new hyper-future. In this sense Tuchel is encouragingly restless both in defeat and victory. Even his new-season touchline look – tailored, sombre, all black – has an agreeably priestly, hair‑shirt energy; less Elizabeth I, author of the introductory quote above, more Martin Luther on his way to a business meeting in an out‑of‑town spa hotel.

Tuchel’s best quality is his obsession with analysis and objectivity. On Sunday night he was already talking about the need to improve. This can be an obstacle at times (see: process-based Argentina substitutes). But it is also a rejection of complacency, ornament, frippery. This England are better than their 2018 equivalent. That team had seven players from Leicester and Arsenal. This one has key parts from Real Madrid, Barcelona and Bayern Munich, including the current Ballon d’Or winner and a £300m midfield tripod.

According to recent reports, the balance of the attack in Madrid was good, not just the most seductively talented players but the best parts for the initiative. Anthony Gordon is an interesting figure in this respect, an intelligent, culturally adaptable, tactically aware footballer, whose game is nonetheless basically running up and down. Elite teams seem to have a place for this role now. Flank-scurry energy node. Right-sided gallop unit. Lewis Hall was also very good again. Any team looks better with a genuine left‑footed full-back, like hanging a picture straight on the wall.

Mainly what Tuchel did in Spain was to select a team with no indulgences, full commitment to a tailored gameplan, no celebrity passengers. And that style is not fixed. See also: Trent Alexander-Arnold against Croatia, and some excellent passes against a deep block even on a middling night. Stick that behind your ear as well, Thomas.

It has been revealed that teams are hugely complex things. Tuchel had to get to know his players. The idea you can simply bolt on an elite manager and expect instant progress was always a bit silly. No dips or lulls, no adaptation. This might work if you come from the same cultural system. But plonking on a brain from someone else’s body is still a way of looking for shortcuts, the managerial equivalent of sticking it in the mixer and hoping for the best. There you go. Give us a final fix on 75 years of inherited domestic culture.

Tuchel is now a little further along with all this. He even did the backs-to-the-wall thing better, waiting to the last moment to press the defensive emergency button, the sight of Dan Burn rumbling out a signal to both teams that this really is the end of the night, like turning on all the lights and getting the DJ to play Don’t Look Back in Anger.

Sunday night was a wonderful game. It was England’s most complete performance under Tuchel. But the lesson hasn’t changed. Trust the process, not the results. Keep doing the ruthless, adaptive things that got you there. England will at some point have to beat the best. And the Nations League is a very useful tool. Win it next summer and taking that final step starts to look a whole lot less of an Arthurian fever dream.

#766. How did England cling on against Spain and what did Tuchel do differently?

How did England cling on against Spain and what did Tuchel do differently?

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1057 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • James Trafford (right) kept Spain out in the latter stages.
  • England held on to beat Spain 3-2 with a backs-to-the-wall finale in the Nations League to finish top of their group.
  • But many observers would have been feeling a sense of deja vu from the World Cup semi-final when England sat back and were beaten by Argentina.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

James Trafford (right) kept Spain out in the latter stages.

England held on to beat Spain 3-2 with a backs-to-the-wall finale in the Nations League to finish top of their group.

But many observers would have been feeling a sense of deja vu from the World Cup semi-final when England sat back and were beaten by Argentina.

So what was different this time? BBC Sport has a look.

First of all the context of the two games was entirely different.

England were 1-0 up against Argentina in the 55th minute on neutral territory in Atlanta - and still had all their players.

Anthony Gordon had put them ahead but Lionel Messi set up Enzo Fernandez and then Lautaro Martinez late on.

But against Spain the best performance of Thomas Tuchel's reign had them 3-0 up through goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

Elliot Anderson then fouled Lamine Yamal for a penalty, which Mikel Oyarzabal scored - and that began the siege at a partisan Riyadh Air Metropolitano.

Nico Williams made it 3-2 but Spain could not find an equaliser, thanks in part to England keeper James Trafford.

Recent findings suggest that "Half an hour feels like two hours against a team like this [with 10 men]," Tuchel told ITV afterwards. "That's the way it is. Without the red card we were clear winners.".

60 minutes of perfection, 30 minutes of chaos - an England win for the ages.

England cling on to stun world champions Spain in thriller.

Making defensive subs is fine when it works - but when it does not, boy will a manager hear about it.

In the World Cup last 16, England had been 2-1 up against Mexico in the Azteca when Jarell Quansah was sent off.

Tuchel brought on three defenders for a defender, a midfielder and a forward.

But England won 3-2 and Dan Burn's cameo was the stuff of legend.

However, nine days later with England 1-0 up against Argentina, Tuchel did the same again - three defenders on for a defender, midfielder and forward.

The first of those subs, with Konsa replacing Anthony Gordon, was in the 72nd minute.

And England just sat back until Argentina broke their resistance.

However, against Spain this time, despite England being down to 10 men and facing incessant pressure, Tuchel was not so quick with defensive subs.

Myles Lewis-Skelly, replacing Harry Kane, was the first on after 78 minutes - 15 minutes after Anderson's sending off. And then five minutes later he brought on two more players - but one of them was a striker in Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

Burn replaced fellow defender White in the 89th minute.

"Harry played 78 minutes, Jude [Bellingham] 83 minutes and then just defending and defending, it's tiring," explained Tuchel.

Industry observers note that "So we needed fresh energy. I was asked yesterday what happens if there needs to be a critical or crucial substitution. And I stated, I feel free enough to take any substitution if I think it is necessary to help the team and to influence the game.

According to recent reports, "I feel free enough to do that and I think there was a lot of defending needed. So we just went for some fresh legs.".

Win over world champions Spain is a 'statement' - Tuchel.

England actually faced more of a siege this time than against the Argentines, the stats confirm.

In the final 30 minutes they faced 19 shots from Spain, with seven on target and an expected goals (xG) total of 2.53.

Argentina, in that time, had 10 shots, with four on target and an xG of 1.41.

In terms of passes from England the numbers were similar with 65 against Argentina and 61 against Spain - both times with an accuracy rate of about 64%.

In Thursday's 2-1 win against Croatia, as a comparison, they tried 557 passes with accuracy of 89%.

"For half an hour it was Mexico reloaded and it felt like we were back in the Azteca. We had to overcome 30 minutes which, against Spain, felt like three hours," Tuchel told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"We defended in a 4-4-1," he continued.

Sources indicate that "The difficult thing is it's not only a red card, it's a red card, and a goal so that makes a completely new game. Thirty minutes against the world champion feels like three hours. I mentioned it before in the stadium and wave after wave after wave.".

England were criticised for blowing a 2-1 half-time lead at Wembley in their first Nations League game with Spain.

But on that day their final 30-minute figurers were much better - with only five shots faced and 176 attempted passes with a 90% accuracy.

So what was different this time? Perhaps the team highlighted more resilience and unity?

After Spain had pulled one back England's players had a huddle.

"I love the fact the team went into a huddle and if anything the manager's stepped back because he wants to see the player reaction," said ex-England defender Matt Upson on BBC Radio 5 Live.

"I almost think that the trauma from that sending off of Elliot Anderson has almost been a positive thing for England because it's given the team a chance to get together and cope in what is an incredibly difficult situation and come through the other side.

"There was so much going on in this game. England had to suffer and came through the other side.".

Defender and goalscorer White was asked about the huddle after the game.

"Just stay calm, when you're one down it becomes more difficult and things change so it was all about managing that," he noted.

Another factor was the performance of England keeper James Trafford, who made six saves - with four of them coming in the final 12 minutes of the game with the score at 3-2.

He made an incredible double save to deny Fermin Lopez and Lamine Yamal in injury time.

Upson remarked: "I think that double save was the moment for Spain and Trafford had the answers.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that whether you're planning a mega holiday movie marathon, yearning for an old classic, or trying to mix up your family movie night with something different this year, there's plenty to choose from.
  • Yes, we can all agree that Die Hard is the GOAT Christmas action movie, but don't you dare sleep on The Long Kiss Goodnight.
  • Recent findings suggest that in Renny Harlin's action thriller, Geena Davis' Samantha is a wholesome small-town school teacher and mother who, eight years ago, woke up pregnant on a beach with no memory of who she was.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that whether you're planning a mega holiday movie marathon, yearning for an old classic, or trying to mix up your family movie night with something different this year, there's plenty to choose from. We've curated the very best Christmas movies you can stream or rent, from sentimental classics with a twist and cozy romantic comedies to emotional indie dramas and high-speed action thrillers.

Yes, we can all agree that Die Hard is the GOAT Christmas action movie, but don't you dare sleep on The Long Kiss Goodnight.

Recent findings suggest that in Renny Harlin's action thriller, Geena Davis' Samantha is a wholesome small-town school teacher and mother who, eight years ago, woke up pregnant on a beach with no memory of who she was. In the present day, Samantha gets into a car accident that changes everything — she begins remembering things and discovers she has elite knife skills. Was she a chef, perhaps? That seems unlikely when a strange man who recognized her at a Christmas parade reveals up at her house to attack her. She kills him with ease as if it's her day job. Turns out, it sure as heck was.

It has been revealed that davis' PTA mom soon transforms back into her old badass self, a platinum blonde CIA assassin. This time, she has Samuel L. Jackson's private eye as her sidekick. With explosions and car chases galore, The Long Kiss Goodnight is everything you'd want from a delightfully bonkers holiday action movie. — Oliver Whitney, Freelance Contributor.

How to watch: The Long Kiss Goodnight is available for rent or purchase on Apple TV, Prime Video, and Fandango at Home.

It has been revealed that watching Macaulay Culkin's Kevin McCallister line his house with booby traps in Home Alone never gets old. It's also a great lesson for young kids left at home by their chaotic families in how to prepare for pesky burglars. Anything can be a weapon! Those old paint cans, your brother's pet tarantula, even a blow torch to burn the top off of a strange man's head can keep you safe. Home Alone has all the perfect ingredients to make a great, rewatchable Christmas movie with its wacky and playful plot, its charismatic cast, a sentimental message about the importance of family during the holidays, and some of the most quotable lines. Go eat some junk and watch some rubbish this Christmas. — O.W.

How to watch: Home Alone is now streaming on Disney+, and is available for rent or purchase on Apple TV, Prime Video, and Fandango at Home.

A cozy Christmas movie starring Whitney Houston and Denzel Washington — what could be better? In director Penny Marshall's The Preacher's Wife, a remake of 1947's The Bishop's Wife, Washington plays a charming angel sent down to Earth to help save a marriage in shambles. Houston's Julia is growing impatient with her pastor husband Henry (Courtney B. Vance), who's distracted by his dwindling church membership. Washington's jovial Dudley is just the spark that the family needs. His wit and doting attention remind Julia of what things used to be like with her and Henry, and the pastor grows jealous. But no worries; Dudley is just here to revitalize the pastor's faith and remind him of the key things he's let slip as Christmas approaches. The Preacher's Wife is warm and full of heart, and also features one of the silliest Denzel Washington performances that simply must be seen. — O.W.

How to watch: The Preacher's Wife is available for rent or purchase on Apple TV, Prime Video, and Fandango at Home.

Industry observers note that nothing indicates a Christmas classic like a Judy Garland song. In Meet Me in St. Louis, we get several memorable Garland numbers, from the classic “Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas” to the buoyant "Trolley Song.".

Industry observers note that the 1944 Vincente Minnelli musical tells the story of the wealthy Smith family living in St. Louis, Missouri, one year before the 1904 World's Fair. All is well for them until the devastating news arrives that the family must relocate to Fresh York City immediately after Christmas for their father's new job. The two eldest Smith daughters, Esther (Garland) and Rose (Lucille Bremer) are distraught, since they're both in love with local boys and have their futures planned near home. Even the youngest, Tootie (Margaret O'Brien), is so upset that she destroys a bunch of snowmen in a fit of rage. But maybe, just maybe, the spirit of Christmas will turn things around for them. — O.W.

According to recent reports, how to watch: Meet Me in St. Louis is now streaming on Tubi, and is available for rent or purchase on Apple TV, Prime Video, and Fandango at Home.

It has been revealed that the majority of family-friendly Christmas movies often tell the same types of holiday stories about Santa. But Sergio Pablos' Klaus proposes a newly introduced origin story for Old Saint Nick. In the animated adventure, it all begins with a Norwegian postman named Jasper (voiced by Jason Schwartzman) who's sent away to an icy northern town called Smeerensburg to carry out his mail delivery duties. There he happens to stumble upon a reclusive bearded toymaker named Klaus (J.K. Simmons). When Jasper helps Klaus donate one of his creations to a local kid, soon every kid in town is desperate to send the toymaker a letter to get a gift in return. And so, Santa is born. Pablos' animated film is a welcome addition to the Christmas movie canon, not only for its originality but also for its gorgeous animation that's glowing with light and Christmasy warmth. — O.W.

How to watch: Klaus is now streaming on Netflix.

We all need a sad gay romance to weep over during the holidays, and there isn't one better than Carol. Todd Haynes' 1950s-set love story follows Cate Blanchett as the eye-catching Carol Aird, a glamorous mother recently separated from her irate, homophobic husband (Kyle Chandler), and Rooney Mara's budding young photographer, Therese Belivet. The two women begin to fall in love over a shared lunch of martinis and a trip to Carol's Connecticut home. But remember, this is the '50s, and Carol's queer relationship is soon used against her in her divorce.

In a recent development, set over the holidays in New York City, Carol beautifully captures the Christmastime atmosphere of the East Coast in winter. There's a snowy trip to a tree lot, the frazzled energy of a department store amid the holiday shopping bustle, long winter coats and scarves, and the cozy relief of escaping the icy streets for a warm holiday party where eyes meet over cocktails. — O.W.

How to watch: Carol is now streaming on Prime Video, and is available for rent or purchase on Apple TV and Fandango at Home.

It has been revealed that it's Christmas Eve in Hollywood and Sin-Dee (Kitana Kiki Rodriguez), a Black trans woman and sex worker, has just gotten out of jail. She meets up with her best friend Alexandra (Mya Taylor) and soon finds out that her pimp/boyfriend Chester (James Ransone) has been cheating on her — and not with just anyone, but with a white cis woman. Now it's time for revenge.

It has been revealed that tangerine follows the two friends over the course of the night as they walk across Hollywood searching for Chester. A simple story blossoms into a profound and emotional journey that sheds light on the real-life experiences many Black trans sex workers encounter on the daily. When Sean Baker's film first came out, it was praised for its low-budget indie style, and for being shot entirely on iPhones. But it's really the story, rich with intimate human moments and bursts of comedy, along with Rodriguez and Taylor's raw performances, that makes Tangerine such a moving film, and one about the power of chosen family. — O.W.

How to watch: Tangerine is now streaming on Tubi and Fandango at Home, and is available for rent or purchase on Apple TV and Prime Video.

Forget cozy holiday dinners and family trips to the tree lot. This Christmas, why not go to a rave? That's how the kids in the '90s cult classic Go decide to celebrate the holiday season.

It's the night of a massive Santa-themed rave in Los Angeles, and two guys are looking to score some ecstasy. Sarah Polley's supermarket clerk Ronna is faced with being evicted, so she decides to become a dealer for the night. Yet things go incredibly wrong, incredibly fast. There's undercover cops, a pissed-off Las Vegas bouncer, car chases, a guy who took way too many pills, and lots and lots of anxiety.

According to recent reports, watching Go is the exact opposite experience of watching a traditional Christmas movie; instead, it feels a lot like being on a bad trip at a rave. Sounds awful, I know, but I swear it's a blast! If you're itching for some adrenaline, a great '90s cast, and a taste of L.A. rave culture, look no further. — O.W.

How to watch: Go is available for rent or purchase on Apple TV, Prime Video, and Fandango at Home.

Sometimes you're so depressed and heartbroken after a breakup that the best solution is to get the heck out of town and spontaneously travel to a stranger's home in another country. Maybe you'll find your deepest self there, or maybe you'll meet a charming, kind man for once. In Nancy Meyers' pre-AirBnB romcom The Holiday, that's just what Cameron Diaz's Amanda and Kate Winslet's Iris do. Iris swaps her cozy English cottage to spend Christmas in the Hollywood Hills, while Amanda takes a break from her movie trailer-editing job in L.A. to soak in some English countryside solitude. A sweet holiday rom-com with all the signature Nancy Meyers' touches (sappy romance, picturesque homes, cozy cream sweaters, etc.), The Holiday checks all the boxes. — O.W.

How to watch: The Holiday is available for rent or purchase on Apple TV, Prime Video, and Fandango at Home.

Sources indicate that in this endlessly rewatchable Christmas staple, Jimmy Stewart is the most generous man in town who puts his dreams aside to help save his neighbors during a financial crisis. Stewart's George Bailey skips his honeymoon, uses his savings to help his community, and even turns down a cushy high-paying job to put others first. But when things go terribly wrong on Christmas Eve, Bailey reaches a breaking point and steps onto a bridge, preparing to jump. That's when his guardian angel, Clarence (Henry Travers), arrives to show him just how different his town and family's life would be without him.

Frank Capra's It's a Wonderful Life is an enduring Christmas classic because it's a reminder of just how precious life is and the impact we have on those around us, even when we can't see it ourselves. It's the type of Christmas film you put on to get into the holiday mood, then suddenly find yourself sobbing, even if you've seen it a dozen times. — O.W.

How to watch: It's A Wonderful Life is now streaming on Prime Video, and is available for rent or purchase on Apple TV and Fandango at Home.

Industry observers note that it's simply not Christmas without Will Ferrell, or a bowl of spaghetti and candy for breakfast. In Elf, Ferrell's Buddy spent his entire life growing up in the North Pole believing he was one of Santa's helpers, despite being enormously tall compared to all the others. Once he finally learns that he's an orphan, Buddy sets out to New York City to find his real father and embark on a series of silly misadventures. James Caan plays Buddy's father, Walter Hobbs, a hardened business exec who publishes children's books. The two are a perfect if chaotic pair — a goofy child-in-a-man's-body, and a grouchy, workaholic dad. For a playful family Christmas comedy that's got romance, humor, and substantial Manhattan-at-Christmas energy, you can't go wrong with Elf. — O.W.

How to watch: Elf is now streaming on HBO Max, and is available for rent or purchase on Apple TV, Prime Video, and Fandango at Home.

If you're tapped out on sentimental Christmas movies, why not put on a seasonal period romance that's enjoyably cynical and even a bit kinky? Set in the 1950s, Paul Thomas Anderson's Phantom Thread is all about relationship power dynamics. A perfectionist London dressmaker named Reynolds Woodcock (Daniel Day-Lewis) falls for a waitress, Alma (an excellent Vicky Krieps). However, he soon discovers his new muse isn't as submissive as the usual women he casually dates and discards. After Reynolds experiences a bout of sickness, the couple's dynamic takes a fascinating turn. And while the holiday season is technically only present as a backdrop for a handful of scenes — notably some of the most emotionally charged of their romance — Phantom Thread has a wintry, even ghostly, Christmas atmosphere throughout. — O.W.

How to watch: Phantom Thread is now streaming on Netflix, and is available for rent or purchase on Apple TV, Prime Video, and Fandango at Home.

Imagine being a grumpy Scrooge when you're surrounded by a town full of silly Muppets. Michael Caine is as cantankerous as ever as Ebenezer Scrooge in The Muppet Christmas Carol. In the Jim Henson musical take on Dickens' classic, Caine humbugs around London as the townsfolk sing about his coldheartedness. Gonzo and Rizzo narrate the musical film, injecting it with humor and shenanigans throughout. Kermit plays Scrooge's benevolent employee Bob Cratchit, with Miss Piggy as Mrs. Cratchit and Robin the Frog as the adorable Tiny Tim. The whole Muppet gang appears throughout, and while the film follows the same beats of A Christmas Carol, the familiar cast of characters and added music make it an extra joyous watch. — O.W.

How to watch: The Muppet Christmas Carol is now streaming on Disney+, and is available for rent or purchase on Apple TV, Prime Video, and Fandango at Home.

Some people watch A Christmas Story every December, while others put on Moonstruck. The romantic comedy may not be about Christmas, but in almost every scene it gives off massive Christmas energy. There's Cher's Loretta walking through the snowy streets of Latest York City in a long black trench coat and sipping wine by a fireplace. There's the Lincoln Center tree lit up behind Loretta and Nic Cage's Ronny as they attend the opera. There's the twinkling of string lights and Christmas decor along the streets and shops in the backdrop. The energy of Christmas is all around in this movie as Loretta falls in love with the ill-tempered Ronny while his brother (her fiancé) is away in Sicily. While Moonstruck is a perfect movie to watch any day of the year, it's especially fitting to snuggle up with it during the holiday season. — O.W.

How to watch: Moonstruck is now streaming on Tubi and Pluto TV, and is available for rent or purchase on Prime Video, Apple TV, and Fandango at Home.

When you imagine a picturesque Santa Claus, jolly, endearing, and kind, no one fits the bill better than Richard Attenborough in Miracle on 34th Street. The beloved actor just looks the part, with his rosy cheeks, warm smile, and inviting demeanor. Sadly, no one in Manhattan except a 6-year-old girl named Susan actually believes he's Santa.

Sources indicate that in the wholesome 1994 remake of the classic film from 1947, Attenborough plays a sweet old man named Kris Kringle who gets hired to play Santa at a Manhattan department store. Kris keeps insisting that he's actually the famous guy from the North Pole, but everyone in New York seems to have lost the spirit of Christmas so much that a plot is formed to institutionalize the poor guy. It's up to Susan (Mara Wilson) and a lawyer (Dylan McDermott) to defend Kris Kringle in court and prove that he's not just wearing a red and white suit for a seasonal gig. — O.W.

How to watch: Miracle on 34th Street is now streaming on Prime Video and Disney+, and is available for rent or purchase on Apple TV and Fandango at Home.

Leave it to filmmaker Robert Zemeckis to bring the wonder of a children’s book to vivid life on screen. The Polar Express expands Chris Van Allsburg’s beloved Christmas story into a film about a young boy who boards a magical train on its way to the North Pole. Tom Hanks plays and voices a handful of roles, including the train's conductor, a Scrooge puppet, and Santa Claus himself. What’s most notable about The Polar Express is the visual world it creates, converting the quiet classicism and awe of the book’s illustrations into a CG world. Back in 2004, it was the first feature-length film to be shot entirely using motion-capture, and the first big studio IMAX 3D movie to ever hit screens. While those visuals have certainly not aged well with time, The Polar Express still manages to capture the magical spirit of Christmas viewed through the eyes of a child.* — O.W.

How to watch: The Polar Express is now streaming on HBO Max, and is available for rent or purchase on Prime Video, Apple TV, and Fandango at Home.

In this charming sequel to the smash hit Home Alone, Kevin McCallister (Macaulay Culkin) winds up in the Major Apple without his family. But fret not, this clever kid is quick to make friends with an unhoused pigeon lover and a kindly toy store owner. He makes enemies too, including Tim Curry as a dastardly hotel concierge. And of course, the Wet Bandits (Joe Pesci and Daniel Stern) are back and up to criminal shenanigans once more!

According to recent reports, for my money, this sequel is even better than its predecessor. Kevin has more foes to outwit, more outlandish traps to set, and there's no beating Newly introduced York in winter. It's a beautiful and moving movie that's terrific fun for the whole family. — Kristy Puchko, Entertainment Editor.

How to watch: Home Alone 2: Lost in New York is now streaming on Disney+, and is available for rent or purchase on Apple TV, Prime Video, and Fandango at Home.

Sources indicate that director Ron Howard dared to imagine how Dr. Seuss' iconic holiday humbug might look in live-action. And who better to take on the role of such an iconically comical character than rubber-faced movie star Jim Carrey? While down in Whoville, cheery citizens plan for gift-giving, celebrations, and feasts, high above them in his cave the green-furred and self-loathing Grinch plots a plan to ruin Christmas. Among the more bizarre elements of this adaptation was a schmaltzy backstory that explained the Grinch's hatred of Christmas and facial prosthetics that turned the likes of Christine Baranski, Molly Shannon, and Jeffrey Tambor into Whos. Yet over the decades, these quirks have been embraced by a generation that sees Carrey's capering as the ultimate Grinch. — K.P.

Sources indicate that how to watch: Dr. Seuss' How the Grinch Stole Christmas is now streaming on Peacock, and is available for rent or purchase on Apple TV, Prime Video, and Fandango at Home.

Perhaps the most polarizing movie of the holiday season, Love Actually is a collection of interlocking vignettes all about — well — love. There's the story of the timid prime minister (Hugh Grant) who falls for a sassy staff member (Martine McCutcheon), the story of the widower (Liam Neeson) guiding his stepson through puppy love, the shy American (Laura Linney) with a crush on her office mate (Rodrigo Santoro), and Alan Rickman playing his most villainous holiday role as the heartbreaker of Emma Thompson. (I too have seen Die Hard. I said what I said.).

Industry observers note that written and directed by Richard Curtis, Love Actually is both wildly popular and widely derided for some of its quirks. But the awesome star power and unapologetically joyful love stories keep us coming back year after year. — K.P.

How to watch: Love Actually is now streaming on Netflix and Peacock, and is available for rent or purchase on Apple TV, Prime Video, and Fandango at Home.

Ah yes, the classic '90s movie where Tim Allen accidentally kills Santa. In The Santa Clause, the first of what would soon become a trilogy, Allen’s Scott is a divorced marketing exec who doesn’t believe in Santa. After Scott spooks the old guy mid-present delivery, Santa tumbles off the roof to his death. Dark! When Scott puts on the magical suit to please his young son Charlie (Eric Lloyd), he becomes bound by the holy North Pole contract stipulating that he now must carry the mantle as the new Saint Nick. He isn’t exactly up for the job and ends up being a pretty grouchy Santa, not to mention a lactose-intolerant one, much to the disappointment of one little girl expecting him to drink his customary glass of milk. Despite some icky fatphobic jokes over Scott’s Santa weight gain, The Santa Clause is a delightfully strange and charming family movie with a clever story and some signature sardonic Tim Allen humor.* — O.W.

How to watch: The Santa Clause is now streaming on Disney+, and is available for rent or purchase on Apple TV, Prime Video, and Fandango at Home.

It’s Dec. 24, 1988, and NYPD detective John McClane (Willis) has just arrived at the Nakatomi Corporation Christmas party to reconnect with his estranged wife (Bonnie Bedelia) — ya know, to come out to the coast and have a few laughs. Unfortunately (or rather, fortunately for our viewing pleasure) Alan Rickman’s Hans Gruber has decided to crash the party with his long-haired German henchmen to steal some bearer bonds. “It’s Christmas, Theo,” Hans tells his safecracker. “A time for miracles!” Too bad for him this Christmas miracle arrives in a bloody tank top and sporting a cranky disposition; McClane won’t let these thieves get away easily.* — O.W.

How to watch: Die Hard is now streaming on Disney+ and Prime Video, and is available for rent or purchase on Apple TV and Fandango at Home.

Leave it up to Tim Burton to inject a brooding darkness into the holiday season. After Edward Scissorhands but before The Nightmare Before Christmas, Burton gave us Batman Returns. And yes, it is indeed a Christmas movie.

Recent findings suggest that first of all, it's a Batman film where Gotham City actually looks and feels festive and colorful for the first time. Burton's extravagant sets are filled with towering Christmas trees blanketed in string lights and ornaments; there's the tree-lighting ceremony where the Red Triangle Circus Gang jump out of a massive gift box; there's the penguin army strapped with candy cane-striped rockets; and, of course, there's the fact that mistletoe plays an key role in the plot.* — O.W.

How to watch: Batman Returns is now streaming on HBO Max, and is available for rent or purchase on Apple TV and Prime Video.

Industry observers note that every kid remembers that one toy they desperately wanted more than anything else for Christmas. It dominates every moment of your young life as you plead for it and shake presents to guess at what's inside. For 9-year-old Ralphie (Peter Billingsley), that Christmas gift fixation is a BB gun. Unfortunately, everyone from his mom to the local department store's grumpy Santa rejects his wish by looking out for his safety. “You'll shoot your eye out!” they shout.

A Christmas Story is in many ways the perfect movie to watch on Christmas Day. It's warm and nostalgic, wacky and playful, and accurately captures a child's view of Christmas. Plus, it's one of a kind — no other holiday movie features a leg lamp, tongues stuck on a frozen pole, and elves shoving screaming children down a giant slide.* — O.W.

How to watch: A Christmas Story is streaming on HBO Max, and is available for rent or purchase on Apple TV, Prime Video, and Fandango at Home.

The third installment in the National Lampoon’s Vacation series opens with the only Griswold family vacation in the film: a trip to a forest where Clark (Chevy Chase) gleefully drags his family out into the snow to cut down their own Christmas tree. From there, many classic Griswold hijinks ensue as Clark goes out of his way to plan the most over-the-top Christmas of all time. That includes decking out his roof in hundreds of string lights to the point of knocking out the entire city’s power grid, the unexpected arrival of his wife’s cousin and her cigar-smoking husband (Randy Quaid), an indoor squirrel attack, a cat wrapped inside a gift box, a very pissed-off Julia Louis-Dreyfus as his snooty neighbor, a SWAT team storming the house, and so much more. It's total Christmas chaos, Griswold style.* — O.W.

How to watch: National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation is streaming on HBO Max, and is available for rent or purchase on Apple TV, Prime Video, and Fandango at Home.

Tim Burton and director Henry Selick’s stop-motion masterwork isn’t a Halloween or a Christmas movie: It’s a spectacular fusion of both in the best of ways. The Nightmare Before Christmas is the perfect film for those who prefer their yuletide delights to come with a side dish of spookiness — and songs. Sick of movies where kids greedily open presents? Great, please enjoy a giant black and orange snake gobbling up gifts whole, along with the entire dang Christmas tree. Family comedies where a jolly old Santa rides his magical sleigh — yawn! How about one where Santa gets kidnapped and a kid gets a shrunken head for a gift? That’s exactly what happens when Jack Skellington, the Pumpkin King of Halloween Town, loses his, well, joie de mort. Wandering sadly through the woods, Jack stumbles into a series of parallel worlds, each dedicated to a different holiday. When he lands in Christmas Town, his bony little mind is blown, and he dedicates himself to learning everything he can about this warm and magical place, and its strange leader named Sandy Claws. There's mischief and romance, a mad scientist and a singing boogeyman, not to mention a voice cast that includes Chris Sarandon, Catherine O'Hara, and the late, great Paul Reubens.

Brilliant in everything from its stunning animation and clever story to its detailed world-building and endlessly catchy music, there’s nothing quite like the haunting magic and whimsy of The Nightmare Before Christmas.* — O.W.

Industry observers note that how to watch: The Nightmare Before Christmas is streaming on Disney+, and is available for rent or purchase on Apple TV, Prime Video, and Fandango at Home.
