#764. SpaceX's Starship megarocket will launch to orbit on Nov. 13. Will you be able to spot it in the night sky?

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (909 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Space ↗ Open Full Page

SpaceX's Starship megarocket will launch to orbit on Nov. 13. Will you be able to spot it in the night sky?

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (909 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that spaceX's Starship megarocket is slated to launch on its ambitious 15th flight test as soon as this Friday (Nov.
  • Recent findings suggest that flight 15's 75-minute launch window opens at 5:45 p.m.
  • According to recent reports, "As it releases towards the southeast, and it will be daylight, then the prospects for viewing from the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that spaceX's Starship megarocket is slated to launch on its ambitious 15th flight test as soon as this Friday (Nov. 13). Will you be able to spot its leviathan upper stage, known as Ship, or its Starlink satellite passengers as they circle Earth during the historic orbital jaunt?

Recent findings suggest that flight 15's 75-minute launch window opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT) on Nov. 13. Starship will fly from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas, where it will be 4:45 p.m. at the opening of the window — about an hour before sunset. The launch could therefore be especially dramatic for folks in the area.

According to recent reports, "As it releases towards the southeast, and it will be daylight, then the prospects for viewing from the U.S. are going to be in Texas and the states along the Gulf of Mexico," Robert Massey, deputy executive director at the Royal Astronomical Society, told Space.com. "They could see the exhaust plume (the 'jellyfish') with the sky darker for observers further east.".

If all goes to initiative, Starship's Super Heavy booster will propel the Ship upper stage through the densest part of Earth's atmosphere before returning to Starbase for a powered landing and capture via the "chopstick" arms of the "Mechazilla" tower system. Ship, meanwhile, will go on to orbit Earth approximately 14 times over the following 22 hours, during which time it will deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites before returning to Starbase for its own ambitious catch attempt.

Satellite visibility in the night sky depends on a cocktail of factors, from the size of the spacecraft to its reflectivity, orbital inclination and position relative to the Earth and sun.

Ship is big — about 171 feet (52 meters) tall — so it will be a viable target for skywatchers, experts say.

"It certainly will be visible in twilight hours. It should be very bright, considerably brighter than the Starlink satellites due to its size," professor James Osborn of Durham University told Space.com. "Where and when is a bit more tricky.".

In a recent development, ship and its Starlink satellites may be seen in the 90 minutes directly after sunset on Nov. 13 and before sunrise on Nov. 14, as the probes catch the sunlight on either side of Earth's colossal shadow as they drift through the twilight sky.

Industry observers note that the spacecraft will initially appear as a string of bright, evenly spaced lights, with Ship most likely appearing significantly brighter than the Starlink satellites. However, Osborn noted that the lack of publicly available data makes it challenging to forecast exactly when the spacecraft will appear.

In a recent development, "During its 14 orbits over 22 hours, the spacecraft is between inclinations of 30.5 [degrees] N and S of the equator," explained Massey. "So it will be best viewed between those latitudes, and then lower in the sky up to latitudes of 40 N and 40 S. That's pretty much the whole of the contiguous U.S.".

Space.com skywatching columnist and veteran meteorologist Joe Rao shared further details on what stargazers may see with the naked eye as Ship drifts silently through the autumn sky.

"When it passes overhead, it will look like a bright, fast-moving star crossing the sky — similar to the International Space Station, but potentially even brighter depending on its orientation," explained Rao. "The Starlink V3 satellites are much smaller, so not as bright, perhaps ranging anywhere from 2nd to 4th magnitude, depending on the angle of illumination with reflected light from the sun.".

Sources indicate that magnitude is the scale used by astronomers to measure the brightness of objects in the night sky. The lower the magnitude, the brighter the object! The unaided eye can make out objects with a magnitude of around +6.5 under ideal dark sky conditions, while the planet Venus at the moment shines at magnitude -4.41.

The Starlink train will likely fall further behind Starship as the 22-hour mission progresses, while the train itself will become more elongated, according to Rao. "For locations where it will make a high arc across the sky, the Starship should be visible for at least a few minutes, although because it is orbiting at a lower altitude (170 miles/275 km) compared to the ISS, it probably will appear to move somewhat faster. ".

According to recent reports, there are multiple handy resources that should allow you to track Ship and the newly deployed batch of V3 Starlink satellites following their scheduled launch on Nov. 13, including the websites Heavens-Above, Star Dash, Orbital Radar and Find Starlink.

Be sure to keep an eye on our Starship Flight 15 live blog for all the latest news along with our launch timings article containing details on how to watch SpaceX's potentially historic orbital launch attempt.

Editor's Note: If you capture a photo of Starship and want to share it with Space.com's readers, then please send your photo(s), comments, and your name and location to spacephotos@space.com.

Anthony Wood joined Space.com in April 2025 after contributing articles to outlets including IGN, Latest Atlas and Gizmodo. He has a passion for the night sky, science, Hideo Kojima, and human space exploration, and can’t wait for the day when astronauts once again set foot on the moon.

Industry News: Mauricio Pochettino sends coaches to Manchester to help prepare for United job

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (304 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Assistant Jesús Pérez and two others depart US early.
  • Pochettino to begin as United head coach on Wednesday.
  • Mauricio Pochettino has sent key members of his coaching staff to England in an early move to prepare for his role as Manchester United’s newly introduced head coach while he gets set to lead the US men’s national team for a final time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Assistant Jesús Pérez and two others depart US early.

Pochettino to begin as United head coach on Wednesday.

Mauricio Pochettino has sent key members of his coaching staff to England in an early move to prepare for his role as Manchester United’s newly introduced head coach while he gets set to lead the US men’s national team for a final time.

Pochettino’s assistant Jesús Pérez, goalkeeping coach Toni Jiménez and athletic coach Sebastiano Pochettino travelled to Manchester soon after the US’s 6-0 victory over Haiti in Miami and in the run-up to United’s Premier League visit to Liverpool on Sunday, when Pochettino will take charge of a fourth English team for a first time. Before then, he will take charge of the US in the second leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final with Haiti in Cincinnati on Tuesday.

Pochettino will have little time before his first game with United, with whom he has a signed a two-and-a-half year contract. He officially joins United on Wednesday.

Sources indicate that “For me, it’s not difficult. I think we are well prepared to switch quick - ‌like a player, from the national team to the clubs,” Pochettino noted on Monday. “From one game that you don’t play well to another that you need to be ready again. From one action to the next action.

“The business today is to be focusing here in ‌Cincinnati for the game against Haiti tomorrow. But for sure, in the moment that [we] finish that game, we are going to start ​to be 100% focused on our next project.”.

Brandi Glanville's health woes continue.

Although the Real Housewives of Beverly Hills alum is "still figuring out" her health as she continues to get to the bottom of her facial disfigurement, she revealed doctors recently removed a "black mass" from her face.

In a recent development, "He stated there were several of them," she added. "He only took one out.".

“I feel like I’m so sad about my dad and Mark," she shared, "that I don’t notice physical pain.".

And her health has only complicated her grief journey. Glanville added that she feels "some guilt" after missing Hasche's funeral because she has "so much fluid" in her head.

Sources indicate that "I keep on thinking and talking myself into this crazy thing like, ‘Oh my God, people hate me. Mark’s family hates me,’” she said. "It just wasn’t possible. I couldn’t fly. I couldn’t drive.".

However, the Special Forces star—who has long suspected a parasite is to blame for her health problems—believes a breakthrough could be imminent. Detailing how she’s now "on antibiotics almost 24 hours a day" Glanville is "excited" after "seeing a difference" with a new medication she's been taking.

The revision comes after she shared that her doctor was going to investigate what was under the skin on her face, noting it could be "fungal balls or something alive.".

"Dr. Carlo Henrado is taking my face off on Friday," she told fans on the Oct. 22 episode of her podcast, "and going to do an exploratory surgery to kind of do a power wash under my skin.".

"I think it’s alive, personally," the reality star added, "because it moves when it wants.".

  • In a media theatre at the Metropolitano in Madrid, head coach Tuchel's sixth sense led him to go public with what he was convinced England would produce against the world champions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Harry Kane scored for a record-equalling seventh England away game.

Thomas Tuchel went with bold words when reminded about the caution that sabotaged England's World Cup hopes and left them with so much to prove against Spain in the Nations League on Sunday.

In a media theatre at the Metropolitano in Madrid, head coach Tuchel's sixth sense led him to go public with what he was convinced England would produce against the world champions.

Tuchel looked his inquisitors in the eyes and declared: "We are up for something spectacular.".

To say Tuchel and England kept their word was a masterpiece of understatement after the finest night of the head coach's reign resulted in a 3-2 victory that was large parts magnificent, some parts madness - and all parts spectacular.

It also ended Spain's 43-game unbeaten run - setting aside their penalty shootout defeat by Portugal in the 2025 Nations League final.

If England and Tuchel could be accused of being cowed by pressure when they led Argentina in the ill-fated World Cup semi-final, they were thrillingly positive in this unforgiving Madrid environment.

The question being asked when England held a one-goal advantage through Harry Kane's penalty at half-time was 'what would theirs and Tuchel's reaction be?' Stick or twist?

Industry observers note that would Tuchel tell England to press their foot on the pedal for acceleration? Or would he take the approach of going into reverse gear, as he did to ill-fated effect against Argentina?

How did England cling on against Spain and what did Tuchel do differently?

Industry observers note that who swaggered around like he owned the place? Spain v England ratings.

England hold on to stun world champions Spain in thriller.

The answer was delivered when they added goals from Arsenal duo Ezri Konsa and Ben White in the first 12 minutes of the second half.

This being England, they then created a mess for themselves when Elliot Anderson was sent off for fouling Lamine Yamal in the area after 65 minutes, although the main culprit was Jarell Quansah for initially conceding possession.

Mikel Oyarzabal scored from the spot and, when Yamal set up Nico Williams for Spain's second with 15 minutes left, it looked like more than an hour of faultless England football might be wasted.

But not a bit of it, as goalkeeper James Trafford produced heroics and England defended with every fibre to close out this landmark win.

Was this the statement victory that was almost demanded of Tuchel as recompense for the World Cup disappointment, a performance to convince the doubters?

Sources indicate that "We're fully aware what we put out there," said Tuchel afterwards. "What a performance we put out for 65 minutes to be deservedly 3-0 up.

"Of course, the red card and the penalty changed the momentum and the characteristics of the game... but we know, and the players know very, very well, what they put out there. That is the statement - and that is the significance of this victory.".

Simple details of the game barely touch the sides of a night filled with quality and glorious chaos, vindication for Tuchel and England's positive approach.

Spain opened with an ostentatious parade of the World Cup in front of England's players as the teams lined up, perhaps a psychological reminder of the superiority that has seen them dominate international football.

What followed, at times literally, reduced Spain's supporters to stunned silence and their players to a shell-shocked shambles chasing the shadows that were overpowering them.

England's white shirts were everywhere but Spain could not get near them. The tormentors had become the tormented.

It was alien territory for a Spain side that has carried all before them, while England's fans tucked away high in a corner of this vast arena were equally unbelieving as a dream unfolded in front of them.

In a recent development, england, for 65 minutes, were in a different class to Spain. And, yes, you have read that right.

From the first whistle, employing a suffocatingly high press, England ran all over Spain.

When White crowned a superb move with the third goal four minutes after Konsa's second, it looked, remarkably, to be a case of how substantial England's victory margin would be.

In the end, the margin was narrow but the stature and significance of England's victory was huge.

Tuchel labelled this meeting with Spain as "proof of concept at the highest level".

There was no doubt the German manager and England were under fierce scrutiny after the manner of the collapse, mentally and tactically, against Argentina at the World Cup.

Here they delivered the proof they can match the best then beat them.

Win over world champions Spain is a 'statement' - Tuchel.

If the vital signs were being forensically examined for evidence Tuchel has learned lessons from a chastening World Cup, that England have improved after that harrowing experience, this game delivered these conclusions.

Of course, England must do it again. Do it when the pressure and expectation in at its highest.

The Nations League is competitive but cannot be compared to a World Cup and European Championship, both titles right now in the possession of the team they beat here.

But England's world-class players delivered - Kane inevitably with his 93rd international goal, but Jude Bellingham was on a level of his own, the outstanding performer on both sides with an individual display simply confirming he is the player with everything.

Industry observers note that and Tuchel got his big calls right, especially selecting Trafford, who responded superbly in a frantic closing phase. White, making a strong claim for the right-back berth, not only scored a goal but produced crucial challenges in the face of relentless, albeit belated, Spain pressure.

"This was the highest level in terms of belief, team spirit, togetherness," stated Tuchel. "It was on the highest level football wise in all aspects of the game. We did everything that needs to be done together.

It has been revealed that "The deep build-up. The high press. The counter-attack. The tracking. The defensive phases. This was an excellent performance and of course a wonderful feeling for us in the dressing room.

It has been revealed that "We overcame some difficult moments in the end. That's how it is. But we are very well aware which steps we took now through after the World Cup.".

England's win means they top their Nations League group, but the importance spreads much wider than simply a league table.

Industry observers note that the first 65 minutes were simply breathtaking. Spain wilting under attack after attack. Spain rattled until they shook as England refused to allow them meaningful possession.

After Anderson's dismissal, bad memories were revisited as England were forced into a rearguard action, but any other result than the one that was eventually delivered would have been a huge injustice.

England survived 29 nervous minutes, including added time, to make a powerful statement about their current status, which is much healthier than when recriminations about Tuchel's approach provided the post-World Cup narrative.

Recent findings suggest that "I'm very impressed with the steps that we took after the World Cup", said Tuchel. "We wanted to get better, better in a deep build-up, get better in defending in a low block and, on top of it, we wanted always to impose our identity and the way we want to play against every opponent.

In a recent development, "I think this was clearly visible throughout the whole group phase. The results followed with an excellent group phase.".

Was this the finest performance of Tuchel's time in charge? Most observers felt so, but the head coach was best placed to answer.

According to recent reports, "Yes, given the circumstances," he said, "and the pressure, the quality, where we played in this building against the reigning world champions, unbeaten in 43 matches. Putting a performance out there in Madrid, and in this environment, was a very complete performance.".

Tuchel will, of course, need repeat performances - but the outstanding ability and character England displayed here to beat the World Cup holders will deliver a huge injection of confidence and self-belief.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • International students earn almost 40% of science and engineering PhDs awarded in the United States.Credit: Bill Pugliano/Getty.
  • The number of international students arriving in the United States in August for the start of the academic year has fallen by 28% since 2024, reaching the lowest level since the depths reached in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic.
  • According to recent reports, data from the federal National Travel and Tourism Office show that the number of incoming student-visa holders fell from 387,000 in August 2024 to 277,000 in August 2026 (see ‘Students stay away’).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

International students earn almost 40% of science and engineering PhDs awarded in the United States.Credit: Bill Pugliano/Getty.

The number of international students arriving in the United States in August for the start of the academic year has fallen by 28% since 2024, reaching the lowest level since the depths reached in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic.

According to recent reports, data from the federal National Travel and Tourism Office show that the number of incoming student-visa holders fell from 387,000 in August 2024 to 277,000 in August 2026 (see ‘Students stay away’). The trend has been driven by a decline in the numbers of students from India and China, which dropped by about 50,000 and 23,000, respectively, from 2024 to 2026.

Source: National Travel and Tourism Office (NTTO); Nature analysis.

The number of applications from international students to US PhD programmes has also declined over the past year, falling by 21% from 2025 to 2026, according to a survey of 55 members of the Association of American Universities (AAU), a coalition of research-intensive schools.

These decreases are squeezing already strained university budgets, and researchers worry about the impact on US science. “I can’t imagine a more effective way for the US to cede its dominance in critical scientific fields to China and Europe than by reducing international students,” claims Nigel Goldenfeld, a physicist at the University of California, San Diego. In 2024, international students earned 38% of the science and engineering PhDs awarded in the United States.

The great university shake-up: four charts show how global higher education is changing.

The great university shake-up: four charts show how global higher education is changing.

The administration of US President Donald Trump has introduced several restrictions on visas and international travel since Trump took office in early 2025. Last month, the administration also attempted to place a US$100,000 levy on science and engineering students enrolling in extended Optional Practical Training (OPT), a work programme used by hundreds of thousands of recent graduates and the largest pipeline of scientific talent into the United States. The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which issued the proposal, stated that it is meant to “combat fraud, strengthen the integrity of the immigration system, and protect U.S. workers”.

Federal judges have suspended the OPT charge and other efforts that the administration made to curb immigration. But higher-education specialists link these attempts to the large decrease in latest overseas students, who, they say, can no longer count a US education as a stable investment. “Uncertainty has become policy, and that has registered in the hearts and minds of students,” claims Chris Glass, a higher-education researcher at Boston College in Massachusetts.

In a recent development, the United Kingdom, Canada and Australia have also seen drops in enrolment of international students after placing upcoming limits on these populations. But the US policies are especially restrictive, Glass claims.

A spokesperson for the White House did not respond to Nature’s request for comment.

On this day in space! Nov. 12, 2014: European Philae probe lands on Comet 67P, bounced twice and then got lost for nearly 2 years

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (637 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • 12, 2014, a European spacecraft named Philae landed on Comet 67P.
  • The European Space Agency's Philae lander separated from an orbiter called Rosetta ahead of its historic landing in 2014.
  • Recent findings suggest that when it touched down, it immediately bounced back up into space.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that on Nov. 12, 2014, a European spacecraft named Philae landed on Comet 67P. To say it was a bumpy landing would be an understatement.

The European Space Agency's Philae lander separated from an orbiter called Rosetta ahead of its historic landing in 2014. It was supposed to use harpoons to secure itself on to the surface of Comet 67P, but the harpoons never fired.

Recent findings suggest that when it touched down, it immediately bounced back up into space. The first bounce brought Philae half a mile above the comet's surface before gravity brought it back down.

Philae was missing for almost two years before scientists found it. Images from Rosetta highlighted Philae stuck in a dark crevice on top of the rubber duck-shaped comet.

The European Space Agency's Rosetta and Philae expedition was a first-of-its-kind mission, an endeavour to not just rendezvous with a comet and watch it change over time as it approached the sun (that was Rosetta's job), but also to soft-land a probe on its icy and rocky surface to see what a comet is truly made of.

In a recent development, the Rosetta and Philae mission succeeded on both counts, but Philae's historic landing was marred by its turbulent touchdown. Philae actually landed three different times on Comet 67/P, all because the harpoons designed to secure it in place didn't fire as planned.

After the first landing, Philae bounced up and drifted around the comet for two hours, making another bounce before Rosetta's cameras lost track of it. Scientists figured it was stuck in a shady spot where sunlight couldn't reach its solar panels. Because it was solar-powered, Philae needed to be facing the sun properly to generate enough power for sustained operation on the comet's surface.

In a recent development, still, Philae did have some power stored in batteries, which lasted for more than two days on the surface. That allowed Philae to perform some science with its 10 instruments in the time it had on Comet 67/P. Most notably, Philae found organic molecules that had never been detected on a comet before.

The Rosetta orbiter continued to orbit Comet 67P until September 2016, and it was in that month -- just weeks before Rosetta itself landed on the comet on Sept. 30, 2016 -- that the spacecraft rediscovered the Philae lander lying on its side in a rocky crevice.

  • The rule was introduced in the 1960s to encourage fans to attend lower league games and prevents matches from being shown on UK television between 2:45pm and 5:15pm on Saturdays.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The blackout originated in the 1960s when Burnley chairman Bob Lord encouraged the EFL to oppose television coverage of 15:00 Saturday matches.

Andy Burnham has urged caution on lifting the Saturday 3pm TV blackout in the UK, saying the health of the football pyramid should come first.

The rule was introduced in the 1960s to encourage fans to attend lower league games and prevents matches from being shown on UK television between 2:45pm and 5:15pm on Saturdays.

The blackout, which is enforced by Article 48 of the Uefa Statutes and is imposed by the English and Scottish football associations, comes into effect when 50% of fixtures in the top two divisions are scheduled to kick off at 3pm.

The Premier League is in the middle of a record Â£6.7bn domestic TV deal for Sky and TNT to show up to 270 live games a season.

But there could be room for change with the 3pm rule in the upcoming broadcast cycle, as the rights deals for the Premier League, EFL and SPFL all end in 2028-29.

The prime minister mentioned any decision to remove the ban would require careful thought about the consequences.

"I would urge a bit of caution [on the blackout], because it does protect the income of lower-league clubs," Burnham mentioned.

Scottish football could pave way for 3pm TV blackout to end.

Why does football have Saturday 3pm TV blackout in UK?

"If you have effectively wall-to-wall Premier League football at any time, it takes away perhaps the incentive to go and watch the football league or non-league.

In a recent development, "So I think it has to be considered carefully. I'm not going to take the pure consumer view here. I'll take the health-of-football approach to this particular matter.".

Only the FA Cup final, which traditionally kicks off at 3pm, is allowed to be broadcast during the blackout window.

In October, the SPFL remarked it is "flexible about the number of games" that will form part of the TV newly introduced deal, which BBC Sport understands includes matches shown on a Saturday afternoon.

Premier League chief executive Richard Masters has previously said a decision about whether the blackout stays in place would need to be made in the future.

But Burnham added: "I would first of all want to protect the football pyramid before I agree to saying 'let's have even more live football'".

"I think it's about protecting the experience with the paying supporter, protecting the football pyramid. Those problems matter to me, first of all.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Columbia Records emerged Monday (Nov.
  • Recent findings suggest that ella Langley led the way for Columbia, with nominations in each of the Substantial Four — making her the fifth artist since the expansion of the categories to land nominations in each of the major general field areas, joining Sabrina Carpenter (2025), Chappell Roan (2025), Olivia Rodrigo (2022) and Billie Eilish (2020).
  • Recent findings suggest that behind Columbia is a trio of labels, including Republic, represented in album (Taylor Swift, The Life of a Showgirl), record (Swift, “The Fate of Ophelia”) and song of the year (Swift, “I Knew It, I Knew You” and Ariana Grande, “Hate That I Made You Love Me”); Atlantic, with a trio of Bruno Mars noms (album, The Romantic; record, “I Just Might”; and song, “Risk It All”) as well as a best latest artist nod for Don Toliver; and Island, which saw a trio of nods for last year’s best new artist winner Olivia Dean (album, The Art of Loving; and record and song for “Man I Need”) as well as another best new artist nominee in Remi Wolf.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Columbia Records emerged Monday (Nov. 16) with nine nominations among the traditional Big Four Grammy categories of album, record and song of the year and best newly introduced artist for the 2027 ceremony, easily leading all record labels among those areas of the general field. That’s the most nominations in the Big Four since Interscope had 13 for the 2024 ceremony.

Recent findings suggest that ella Langley led the way for Columbia, with nominations in each of the Substantial Four — making her the fifth artist since the expansion of the categories to land nominations in each of the major general field areas, joining Sabrina Carpenter (2025), Chappell Roan (2025), Olivia Rodrigo (2022) and Billie Eilish (2020). (Eilish famously swept them all, only the second time that has ever happened, after Christopher Cross in 1981.) Langley’s “Choosin Texas” shattered the record for most weeks at No. 1 on the Hot 100 this year, at 28 weeks and counting, while her album Dandelion reached No. 1 on the Billboard 200 in April. Joining Langley among Columbia’s nominees is Rosalía, whose LUX album and single “Berghain” were nominated for album, record and song (she got a BNA nom herself in 2020), while Tame Impala and JENNIE’s “Dracula” (record) and Slayyyter, signed to RECORDS/Columbia (BNA) rounded out the label’s Big Four nominees.

Recent findings suggest that behind Columbia is a trio of labels, including Republic, represented in album (Taylor Swift, The Life of a Showgirl), record (Swift, “The Fate of Ophelia”) and song of the year (Swift, “I Knew It, I Knew You” and Ariana Grande, “Hate That I Made You Love Me”); Atlantic, with a trio of Bruno Mars noms (album, The Romantic; record, “I Just Might”; and song, “Risk It All”) as well as a best latest artist nod for Don Toliver; and Island, which saw a trio of nods for last year’s best new artist winner Olivia Dean (album, The Art of Loving; and record and song for “Man I Need”) as well as another best new artist nominee in Remi Wolf. Notably, that’s the third straight year with a BNA for Island Records, and its fifth in three years, extending the longest-running active streak for a label and highlighting its recent dominance, particularly among young and rising female pop artists — Carpenter, Roan, Dean and Wolf join Lola Young on that list since the 2025 awards. The last label with that many BNA nods in that period was Columbia, which had five in three years between 2020 and 2022, and actually had six across four years when including 2019. Prior to 2019, that feat got a lot more difficult, given that the category was limited to five entries per year through 2018.

It has been revealed that RAYE’s success — landing album (This Music May Contain Hope), record and song (“Where Is My Husband!”) recognition — earned her label Human Re-Sources three nominations among the Substantial Four categories, tying with Interscope, which also saw one of its superstars, Olivia Rodrigo, nab three nods (album, You Seem Pretty Sad For a Girl So In Love; and record and song, “The Cure”). RAYE, who got a BNA nom in 2025, helped lead the charge among the indie label community, which racked up seven nominations in addition to her trio: Phoebe Bridgers (dead oceans) was nominated for album of the year; while Angine de Poitrine (ATO), Geese (Partisan) and The Womack Sisters (Daptone) all received nods for best newly introduced artist. That adds up to the most indie nominees for the Big Four since six in 2021, when Megan Thee Stallion (300 Entertainment, prior to its acquisition by WMG) won best new artist; Black Pumas (ATO) was up for album and record; Jacob Collier (Hajanga) got a nod for album; and Bridgers (dead oceans) and D Smoke (EMPIRE) also got BNA nods.

Overall, Universal Music Group led the way in the Big Four, with 12 nominations (in addition to those above, Capitol landed a BNA nod for Sienna Spiro), followed by Sony with Columbia’s nine and WMG with its four from Atlantic; while, as mentioned, the indies picked up seven. By distribution ownership, Human Re-Sources, distributed by The Orchard, would give Sony 12 noms, while the distribution deals for ATO and Partisan go through Virgin Music Group, which would push UMG’s total to 14.

Latest Update: Eli Lilly’s Foundayo obesity pill eases sleep apnea in late-stage trial, paving way for approval

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Eli Lilly on Monday noted its obesity pill Foundayo significantly reduced the severity of obstructive sleep apnea, the most common sleep-related breathing disorder, in patients with obesity, in a late-stage trial.
  • Sources indicate that the drugmaker looks to file by the end of the year for U.S.
  • OSA refers to interrupted breathing during sleep due to narrowed or blocked airways, which can cause drops in oxygen and increases in blood pressure that are associated with serious complications, such as hypertension, heart failure and stroke.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eli Lilly on Monday noted its obesity pill Foundayo significantly reduced the severity of obstructive sleep apnea, the most common sleep-related breathing disorder, in patients with obesity, in a late-stage trial.

Sources indicate that the drugmaker looks to file by the end of the year for U.S. approval of the daily pill for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea, or OSA, in adults with obesity or who are overweight. The results make the pill — which rolled out in the U.S. in April — one of several GLP-1 treatments to show promise in treating the condition.

OSA refers to interrupted breathing during sleep due to narrowed or blocked airways, which can cause drops in oxygen and increases in blood pressure that are associated with serious complications, such as hypertension, heart failure and stroke. The condition affects nearly 1 billion adults globally, including 80 million people ages 20 and over in the U.S., according to the National Council on Aging. Most have never been diagnosed, Lilly remarked in a release.

Lilly's blockbuster weight loss injection Zepbound became the first medication to win U.S. approval for OSA in December 2024. Patients have limited treatment options outside of that drug and many use cumbersome machines that provide positive airway pressure, or PAP, to allow for normal breathing.

"Foundayo is already making a difference for people living with obesity, and with looks to submit these results to the FDA by the end of the year, we could have the opportunity to help people living with OSA," Dr. Thomas Seck, senior vice president of product development of Lilly Cardiometabolic Health, noted in a release.

It has been revealed that the trial tested Foundayo in two independent studies, the first of which included 363 patients who were unable or unwilling to use PAP therapy. The second study included 349 people who were on PAP therapy for at least three months at the time of screening and continued that treatment during the trial.

Patients in both studies who took Foundayo started at a low dose and increased it gradually at four-week intervals to different maximum dosages.

Industry observers note that researchers specifically examined how much the pill reduced the so-called apnea-hypopnea index, or AHI, which records the number of times per hour a person's breathing highlights a restricted or completely blocked airway. The index is used to evaluate the severity of obstructive sleep apnea and the effectiveness of treatments for the condition.

People who took Foundayo and were not using PAP therapy had an average of 21.1 fewer AHI events per hour at 52 weeks, compared with an average reduction of 4.8 per hour for the placebo, according to the results.

Foundayo also met the trial's second goal in that group, leading to an overall AHI reduction of 43.8% compared with a decrease of 6.3% for the placebo. Lilly said 31.5% of the participants in the Foundayo group met the criteria for remission or improvement to mild OSA.

Meanwhile, patients who were on both Foundayo and PAP therapy had an average of 18.3 fewer AHI events per hour at 52 weeks, compared with an average reduction of 5.5 per hour for the placebo.

Foundayo led to an overall AHI reduction of around 27.5% in that group, compared with a decrease of 3% for the placebo. The company stated 19.6% of the participants on Foundayo and PAP therapy also met the criteria for remission or mild OSA.

Foundayo also reduced what's known as the sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden — a measure of how deeply and for how long oxygen levels fall during sleep. That metric fell by 55.9% in people not using PAP therapy and 45.8% in those using it.

Lilly remarked the pill also helped patients lose roughly 11% of their weight across groups at 52 weeks and helped to lower a marker of inflammation.

The firm said the safety data and how well patients tolerated Foundayo were generally consistent with previous trials on the pill.

Around 12% of people on Foundayo who were not using PAP therapy discontinued due to side effects, compared to 3.8% with the placebo. Meanwhile, 6.8% of those on both Lilly's pill and PAP discontinued the drug due to side effects, compared with 0.6% in the placebo group.

The most common side effects were gastrointestinal, including nausea, diarrhea, constipation and vomiting, and were generally mild to moderate in severity. That's consistent with other GLP-1 medications.

FAA Grounds All US Flights Until Further Notice

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (546 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Enhancement, 8:45 pm EST Friday: The FAA’s ground stop is now over.
  • The Federal Aviation Administration grounded all US flights Friday afternoon, due to “extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety,” the agency mentioned in a statement.
  • In a post on X, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy stated that the ground stop was related to a communication concern affecting Air Traffic Control Centers and agency technicians are investigating.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Enhancement, 8:45 pm EST Friday: The FAA’s ground stop is now over.

The Federal Aviation Administration grounded all US flights Friday afternoon, due to “extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety,” the agency mentioned in a statement. Flights already in the air will be allowed to land, the agency said, but no newly introduced ones are permitted to take off.

In a post on X, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy stated that the ground stop was related to a communication concern affecting Air Traffic Control Centers and agency technicians are investigating.

Sources indicate that the ground stop came after widespread reports of radio frequency outages among several of the nation’s most critical Air Traffic Control Centers, including in Boston, Chicago, and New York. Air traffic controllers use designated radio frequencies to communicate with pilots and manage and monitor airspace safety. In the past, controllers have used voice communications relayed over these radio frequencies to direct traffic; in recent years, the FAA has also rolled out a text-based communication system.

Reached for comment, an FAA spokesperson did not provide any additional details.

Nationwide ground stops are rare. The FAA halted all air traffic on September 11, 2001. In January of 2023, a ground stop was issued after an outage to a critical system that the FAA used to distribute real-time data and warnings to pilots, known as NOTAM (Notice to Air Mission).

In a recent development, “This really points to how much we need to modernize our air traffic control system,” claims Susan Hotle, a professor of transportation engineering at Virginia Tech who worked at the FAA. “Right now all it takes is for one system to go out, and it affects a wide region at once.”.

Earlier Friday, Duffy wrote congressional leaders to ask lawmakers to “act swiftly” on the Transportation Department’s request for $30.1 billion funding updates to the nation’s air traffic control system.

Industry observers note that if the outage lasts more than a couple hours, it will take airlines—and the flyers that depend on them—days to recover, notes Michael McCormick, a professor at Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University and a former air traffic controller. An extended stop would mean “airline systems are going to be complete in chaos, with aircraft and air crews in the wrong places. It would take days to get up and back running normally,” he says.

The FAA noted this week that it was rolling out a latest AI tool to help advise air traffic controllers. The tool, now available nationwide, had been tested in the busy Washington, DC, region. Air Space Intelligence, the FAA contractor responsible for the tool, posted on X that the groundstop “is not based on or a result of the SMART system, any product of ASI or our integration with FAA and [Air Traffic Control].”.

At San Francisco International Airport on Friday, hoards of confused travelers lined up to speak with airline staff. A number flights at the airport had already been delayed because of high winds, and the FAA ground stop was now compounding the matter.

“The FAA has issued a nationwide ground stop,” a United Airlines employee said over the intercom at Terminal 3 near the E departure gates. “This is a nationwide event.”.

Louise Matsakis contributed reporting from SFO.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Romelu Lukaku scored three goals for Belgium at the World Cup this summer.

Romelu Lukaku has retired from international football, saying he has "enjoyed every single moment" of playing for Belgium.

Fenerbahce striker Lukaku, 33, made his international debut in 2010 and is Belgium's all-time leading men's goalscorer with 94 goals in 135 appearances.

He is the fifth highest men's international goalscorer of all time, behind Sunil Chhetri, Ali Daei, Lionel Messi and leader Cristiano Ronaldo, who has scored 146.

Lukaku scored eight goals across four World Cups, including in the run to the quarter-finals at this summer's tournament, and a total of six goals at three European Championships.

Writing on Instagram,, external the former Everton, Chelsea and Manchester United forward thanked his team-mates and coaches "for pushing and trusting me to help the team" during his 16 years with the national side.

He missed Belgium's Nations League win over Turkey last week with a hip injury and was an unused substitute on Sunday as they qualified for the last eight of the competition by beating Italy 4-1.

Sources indicate that "These 16 years I gave all I had for the national team... I went through every emotion possible," Lukaku wrote.

"To the Belgium fans thank you for the support you gave our team. I am proud to have represented my country in four World Cups and three European Championships.

"I will never forget those moments. I'm at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing. It was enjoyable. I'm grateful.".

In 2023, Lukaku scored 14 times in eight Euro 2024 qualifying appearances, breaking the record for goals scored by a player in a European Championship qualifying campaign.

His Belgium team-mate Kevin de Bruyne posted an image of himself with Lukaku, external on Instagram adding: "There are no words to describe what you've meant to me and our country!".

Beginning with Debby Boone’s “You Light Up My Life” in 1977, a relatively select few smashes have led the Billboard Hot 100 for at least 10 weeks. How few? Just a mere 4% of all Hot 100 No. 1s dating to the chart’s launch on Aug. 4, 1958, have earned the achievement.

Recent findings suggest that olivia Newton-John’s “Physical” flexed 10 weeks at No. 1 in 1981-82, and that smash and Boone’s shared the mark for the longest Hot 100 reign for more than a decade, until Boyz II Men’s “End of the Road” dominated for 13 weeks in 1992. That best lasted briefly, as Whitney Houston’s “I Will Always Love You” led for 14 weeks in late 1992/early 1993. In 1995-96, Mariah Carey and Boyz II Men’s “One Sweet Day” ran up 16 weeks at No. 1, a milestone that held for more than 23 years. #741. This supernova impostor baffled astronomers for 15 years — until they found a hidden black hole feeding on an unstable star

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1055 w)
📖 Baca

This supernova impostor baffled astronomers for 15 years — until they found a hidden black hole feeding on an unstable star

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1055 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A cosmic imposter that has faked being a supernova 27 times and counting is actually a hot, luminous, and decidedly unstable star that is being fed on by a vampiric black hole or neutron star, NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory has discovered.
  • When a massive star reaches the end of the road and runs out of nuclear fuel to power fusion reactions in its core, the star is destroyed in a supernova explosion.
  • Yet when the light of the 'supernova' faded, the star was still there, only to continue bursting into light every 113 days.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A cosmic imposter that has faked being a supernova 27 times and counting is actually a hot, luminous, and decidedly unstable star that is being fed on by a vampiric black hole or neutron star, NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory has discovered.

When a massive star reaches the end of the road and runs out of nuclear fuel to power fusion reactions in its core, the star is destroyed in a supernova explosion. That’s what astronomers thought they had found on 11 January 2012, when they observed what appeared to be a supernova on the outskirts of the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, which is about 25 million light-years away in the constellation Coma Berenices.

Yet when the light of the 'supernova' faded, the star was still there, only to continue bursting into light every 113 days.

"For 15 years, astronomers have been watching this star get really bright and then dim again on a regular basis," Mojgan Aghakhanloo of the University of Virginia in Charlottesville remarked in a statement.

Several other supernova imposters have been observed over the past decade or two. Until now, no one knew what causes these stars to repeatedly cry wolf. Thanks to Chandra’s X-ray vision, Aghakhanloo has led a team of astronomers who think they have now uncovered an explanation.

The supernova imposter is named AT 2016blu, and is a type of star that we call a 'luminous blue variable,' or LBV. These are the most massive and luminous stars in the universe and their extreme characteristics result in them being highly unstable, undergoing intermittent bouts of mass loss as they eject material from their outer layers into the surrounding space.

However, faking a supernova is not part of their typical behavior, so a new way of looking at AT 2016blu was needed.

"To understand the cause of these eruptions, we realized that we needed X-ray data that was timed so that we’d observe the star when it was in an outburst," team member Núria Torres-Albà, also from the University of Virginia in Charlottesville, remarked.

Recent findings suggest that aghakhanloo’s team were granted the opportunity to commandeer Chandra to target an outburst of AT 2016blu at the earliest opportunity. That opportunity arose in March 2026.

Sources indicate that chandra had previously and coincidentally looked in the direction of NGC 4559 back in 2001 and 2002 and did not notice anything unusual back then. This time around, however, it captured a powerful blast of X-rays coinciding with yet another false supernova outburst.

The X-ray detection allowed Aghakhanloo’s team to assemble a picture of what is happening. "Until we were able to get Chandra data at the right time, we couldn’t figure out what was making this happen," he stated.

Chandra’s X-ray observations indicate that AT 2016blu has an unseen companion, a compact, high-gravity object that is either a neutron star or a stellar-mass black hole on an elliptical 113-day orbit around the luminous blue variable.

Neutron stars and stellar-mass black holes are the core remnants of massive stars that have gone supernova for real, meaning that at one time AT 2016blu was a binary star system.

Each time the compact object reaches the point in its orbit that is closest to the luminous blue variable, its powerful gravity is able to pull material from the unstable star. This sets in motion a chain of events that results in the brilliant outbursts.

As the stolen starstuff is dragged away from the wounded star and towards the compact object, it forms an accretion disk swirling around the neutron star or black hole so fast and growing so hot that it emits X-rays. These are the X-rays that Chandra saw.

Sources indicate that the X-rays are immense, energizing the surrounding cloud of material that had been ejected by the luminous blue variable years before. The cloud is heated and glows extremely brightly in visible light, creating the impression of a supernova.

"We suspected that the bright repeating flashes at optical wavelengths might actually be powered by periodic blasts of high-energy X-rays," noted team member Nathan Smith of the University of Arizona in Tucson. "The dense gas surrounding the system is heated by the X-rays and then glows in the optical.".

Calculations suggest that each year a 440 billion trillion pounds of material at minimum is stolen by the compact object, and possibly two orders of magnitude more than that. This is a huge amount, yet it is only 800 millionths of the mass of the sun, and AT 2016blu’s luminous blue variable is at least 33 times the mass of the sun.

Nevertheless, it is far greater than the maximum rate of material that a neutron star can safely accrete, referred to as the Eddington limit. It’s little wonder that the accretion onto the compact object unleashes such extreme energies.

According to recent reports, AT 2016blu is also connected with another mysterious and rare astrophysical phenomenon, that of ultra-luminous X-ray (ULX) sources. The identity of whatever it is that is powering ULXs remains unclear, but the involvement of compact objects such as black holes and neutron stars is high on the list.

AT 2016blu is bright enough to be considered a ULX, so could it act as a Rosetta stone connecting supernova imposters with ULXs? It’s too early to say that; only one other supernova impostor has so far been found to have X-ray emission typical of material being stolen from one star and accreting onto a compact body, and that is SN 2010da, but in that case it is known that the companion is another massive star, a red supergiant, rather than a compact object.

In a recent development, the X-ray detection of AT 2016blu is described in a paper published on Monday (Nov. 9) in The Astrophysical Journal.

Industry observers note that keith Cooper is a freelance science journalist and editor in the United Kingdom, and has a degree in physics and astrophysics from the University of Manchester. He's the author of "The Contact Paradox: Challenging Our Assumptions in the Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence" (Bloomsbury Sigma, 2020) and has written articles on astronomy, space, physics and astrobiology for a multitude of magazines and websites.

Jurgen Klopp took over as Germany head coach in July.

Germany head coach Jurgen Klopp says he "didn't think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that" as he called for Fifa president Gianni Infantino to be replaced.

Blatter resigned as Fifa boss in 2015 amid a corruption scandal and was succeeded by Infantino in February 2016.

Infantino plans to stand for re-election in March but has been under pressure since scrapping his Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, which included selling off stakes in the World Cup and other Fifa competitions to private investors.

Infantino apologised to the Fifa Council for the initiative but was told he was not fit to lead world football's governing body unless he released all the documents and answered key questions.

"I've been following football for many years. There are people who are much more knowledgeable about this than I am. But I think most people now agree a change would make a lot of sense," stated former Liverpool boss Klopp.

"I didn't think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that.".

Klopp added: "Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job.".

French Football Federation (FFF) president Philippe Diallo has been named as Uefa's candidate to challenge Infantino.

Diallo received the unanimous support of Uefa's executive committee and formal ratification from the FFF is expected on Tuesday.

Uefa, which is European football's governing body, mentioned it has "full confidence" Diallo would "uphold the highest standards of governance" amid its calls for "renewed unity and trust within the global football community".

Wenger decides not to challenge Fifa chief Infantino.

Infantino apologises to Fifa Council - but told he is still not fit to lead.

Uefa has been one of Infantino's fiercest critics and has repeatedly called on him to stand down.

It has prepared criminal legal proceedings against Infantino and lodged a claim in three US courts for all documents related to FFE to be released.

The deadline for candidates to officially confirm they are standing against Infantino in Fifa's presidential election is Wednesday.

Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, who is Fifa's head of global development, had been considering running for the job but sources have told BBC Sport he has ruled himself out.

Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega was the first person to put his name forward in October.

Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima has also unveiled his intention to stand.

"There are people who truly care about the future of football - people who aren't driven by financial interests," noted Klopp.

"If someone like that were to step up - if someone like that were to become president - I think that would be a significant improvement.

"There are surely people who care deeply about the future of football and have no financial interests in it.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • James Trafford has made five appearances for England, all of them in 2026.
  • As he was mobbed by his England team-mates for a late double save that secured a memorable 3-2 win against world champions Spain, the debate that followed about who the country's number one is was inevitable.
  • The Leeds keeper was given his chance to show England boss Thomas Tuchel what he could do again - and he absolutely took it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

James Trafford has made five appearances for England, all of them in 2026.

It was some night for James Trafford.

As he was mobbed by his England team-mates for a late double save that secured a memorable 3-2 win against world champions Spain, the debate that followed about who the country's number one is was inevitable.

The Leeds keeper was given his chance to show England boss Thomas Tuchel what he could do again - and he absolutely took it.

On his fifth England cap the 24-year-old enjoyed a magnificent performance in Madrid as his side handed the hosts their first loss in 43 matches.

Trafford made four key saves in the final 12 minutes of the game, including an incredible double stop to first deny a Lamine Yamal curler and then dive again to his right to keep out Fermin Lopez from close range.

Last week Tuchel had made it clear that Everton goalkeeper Jordan Pickford was his number one.

But after full-time in Spain Tuchel told ITV Sport "there's no number one" and Trafford had "a brilliant match".

So, following his performance on Sunday night, is Trafford now likely to oust Pickford as England's go-to goalkeeper?

Is Trafford 'closing the gap' on Pickford?

Despite being just 24 years old Trafford has already been England's most expensive goalkeeper by transfer fee... twice.

Trafford returned to his boyhood Manchester City from Burnley for a Â£31m fee in 2025 and then left the Etihad for Leeds for Â£45m this summer - having been limited to being Pep Guardiola's 'cup goalkeeper'.

Given the downturn in form of their current goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, many City fans may well be wishing Trafford had stayed. Their loss is Leeds' - and maybe England's - gain.

At Leeds he has found his form and this season ranks first among the 52 goalkeepers who have played at least 10 games in Europe's significant five leagues by save percentage (81.4%).

He has made five appearances for England, all of them in 2026, and has rotated with Pickford across the Three Lions' five matches since the World Cup.

Pickford has started against Czech Republic and Croatia twice whereas Trafford has played against Czech Republic and started both England's matches with Spain, home and away.

After England's win in Madrid, which was the first time Spain had lost in the city in 39 years, Trafford's double-save was praised by his Three Lions team-mate Declan Rice.

"Everything happened so quick so for him to make two in the space of two seconds is massive," he told ITV. "A massive night for him.".

Industry observers note that spain manager Luis de la Fuente agreed. He said: "We did generate some chances but England's goalkeeper has produced a fantastic performance and stopped two or three potential goals in the last 10 or 15 minutes.".

After the double-save several England players ran over to celebrate with Trafford.

And on Tuchel's decision to rotate between his two keepers former Manchester United captain Roy Keane told ITV: "I think it's smart management.

"This is the perfect time for Trafford to come in, against top players, and show what he's capable of doing.".

Social media has been full of the 'England number one' debate since, with many suggesting this was a moment that marked the changing of the guard.

Could Tuchel really now not start with Trafford for England's Nations League quarter-finals? Only time will tell.

Pickford - "You've got to respect it".

What about Pickford though? England's undisputed first choice for almost 10 years has rarely let his country down.

The 32-year-old has won 94 caps for England since making his debut in a 0-0 draw with Germany in 2017 and during his time as number one England have reached two World Cup semi-finals and two Euros finals.

According to Opta stats, Pickford has only made two errors leading to goals across his England career, with 46 clean sheets and a 74.3% save ratio.

And since the start of the 2024-25 season, only Arsenal's title-winning keeper David Raya has more clean sheets in the league than Pickford at Everton.

Industry observers note that "We saw the last selections and all thought Jordan Pickford's place is under threat and James Trafford is going to be the next number one. I don't think Thomas Tuchel saw it as starkly or simply as that," noted former England number one goalkeeper Paul Robinson to BBC Sport before England's win against Spain,.

"It's a conversation that will definitely take place down the road, but not now. Jordan is England's first choice, in my opinion, rightfully so given his consistency and performances over such a long period.

"This is a debate and conversation for the future definitely because Father Time catches up with everyone eventually and the manager needs to have a contingency strategy, but Jordan Pickford very much remains number one and Thomas Tuchel has noted as much.

"I don't think Jordan Pickford is under threat for his jersey on a permanent basis any time soon, irrespective of the next selection.".

This isn't a debate that is going away any time soon. But having two goalkeepers genuinely competing for that number one shirt can only be to England's benefit.

60 minutes of perfection, 30 minutes of chaos - an England win for the ages.

How did England cling on against Spain and what did Tuchel do differently?

Shania Twain is standing up for others in country music.

The legendary star in the genre used her acceptance speech for the Equal Play Award at Sunday’s CMT Awards to call for more equity and diversity in the country music industry.

According to recent reports, “When I wrote the phrase ‘Man I feel like a woman’ I honestly had no idea at the time it would become an undercurrent of a decades-long career,” she stated, referring to one of her biggest hits. “It’s amazing how one statement can empower so many.”.

The phrase, Twain stated, “has been adopted by an array of fantastic communities all around the world and become a genuine path of power…which brings me so much joy.”.

“I believe in an all-inclusive country music. We’re family,” Twain said. “This is a genre of music with a rich history that raised and nurtured my own songwriting and performance and recording career from childhood. Currently, the industry standard does a real disservice to this.”.

Twain, who was presented the award by rapper Megan Thee Stallion, shouted out some of the diverse acts she is spotlighting on her “Queen of Me” tour this year, including Lily Rose, Lindsay Ell, Hailey Whitters, Mickey Guyton and others.

In a recent development, “I will continue to do my best as a trailblazer,” Twain mentioned. “Together, let’s ensure all our fellow artists get equal play regardless of gender, age or race.”.

Recent findings suggest that she also performed acappella with the African American singing group, The BoykinZ, while presenting an award onstage. Twain connected with the group, who are sisters and rising country stars, after Kelly Clarkson surprised them recently by bringing Twain out to meet them during an episode of Clarkson’s daytime talk show.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it feels like yesterday when we were discussing Superman, the first massive-screen entry in James Gunn's rebooted DCU. Now Gunn is out, and Skydance (the tech giant formed by the merger of Warner and Paramount) is already dismantling his grand intends for the DCU.

That means that Man of Tomorrow, which arrives next summer, will be the final entry in Gunn's ambitious, and occasionally divisive, DC experiment. The DCU's first chapter — officially titled 'Gods and Monsters' — gave us Supergirl and Clayface (as well as TV demonstrates like Peacemaker S2 and Lanterns) in the run-up to Clark Kent and Lex Luthor's return.

Man of Tomorrow looks to be upping the stakes from Earthly villains to intergalactic baddies with the introduction of Brainiac, and it may well have been the herald of the first Justice League movie in the rebooted DCU.

Gunn has yet to prove audiences actually care about more than Batman and Supes, which might explain why this follow-up is also an ensemble of sorts. As the Marvel Cinematic Universe prepares to unleash Avengers: Doomsday, Secret Wars, and even a fresh X-Men reboot, their DC counterparts have always struggled to get their dream team off the ground.

Recent findings suggest that we'll never know what might have been, but we can still enjoy Gunn's DC swansong when it lands in 2027. Here's everything we know about James Gunn's Man of Tomorrow.

Man of Tomorrow will be released theatrically in the United States on July 9, 2027. Most international territories are expected to get it around the same time.

In a recent development, only a few months after Superman's release and successful box office run, DC Studios and Warner Bros. Pictures confirmed the sequel would be coming two years after Clark Kent's return to the big screen.

Man of Tomorrow isn't out yet, but you can watch the rest of the DCU so far (it's pretty good for the most part) in preparation first.

When the movie hits theaters on July 9, 2027, it'll likely remain exclusive to significant screens for at least two or three months, depending on how successful it is.

In a recent development, with that stated, we know Warner Bros. (now part of Skydance) isn't the most patient when it comes to theatrical runs based on its track record, so the chances are Man of Tomorrow will hit HBO Max sooner rather than later, probably by early autumn 2027.

It has been revealed that no, we're still waiting for the first Man of Tomorrow trailer. Looking at the timeline of Superman's fantastic marketing campaign, however, we can guess the sequel will get a first trailer before 2026 ends, probably in time for Christmas.

It has been revealed that yes, James Gunn has officially confirmed Brainiac is the main threat Earth is facing in Man of Tomorrow. This explains why other heroes will be joining Superman in a fight against the alien mastermind, but the plot is looking a bit more complex.

In typical comic book fashion (and somewhat reminiscent of Thor: The Dark World), the main hook in Man of Tomorrow appears to be a reluctant alliance between the first movie's villain, Lex Luthor, and Kal-El (aka Clark Kent). "Enemies to allies" is always a fun dynamic to have in a sequel, especially when stars David Corenswet (Superman) and Nicholas Hoult (Lex Luthor) delivered strong and memorable performances the first time around.

The actual plot remains under wraps, but we can guess Brainiac — one of DC's biggest and most iconic alien villains — will be a tough nut to crack, thus requiring some sort of unofficial team-up that will include returning heroes like Mister Terrific, Guy Gardner, Hawkgirl, John Stewart, Blue Beetle, and even Kara Zor-El (Supergirl). There are other names circling the project that could lead to even bigger appearances, but don't expect to learn much about them before the movie's marketing kicks off.

Why should you care about Brainiac? Well, he's a super-intelligent techno-organic alien from the planet Colu with an obsession with knowledge and self-improvement. A perfect foe for Luthor, Earth's greatest mind, but also a breath of fresh air for Superman, who's been stuck battling either Kryptonian menaces or just Luthor too long on the substantial screen.

As a direct continuation of Superman, Man of Tomorrow is bringing back plenty of actors in both main and supporting roles, including:.

New cast members with publicly announced (or previously established) characters include:.

Last but not least, we also know Adria Arjona, Andre Royo, Matthew Lillard, and Sinqua Walls are part of the cast, but their parts remain a secret for now.

Recent findings suggest that much of the current Man of Tomorrow speculation centers on Adria Arjona's role in the story. While many have theorized she could be playing Wonder Woman — something that neither Gunn nor Arjona has straight-up denied — the earlier reports and rumors suggested she could be Maxima.

According to recent reports, such a role would fit Gunn's penchant for throwing lesser-known comic book heroes and villains into his movies wherever possible. If you're not an avid reader or longtime DC fan, all you need to know is that Maxima is an alien conqueror from the planet Almerac obsessed with Superman as her perfect mate and king. She's also morally ambiguous, at least when she first appeared, so that makes her a particularly interesting character to bring in for a more complex and nuanced sequel.

With Brainiac spearheading the roster of fresh DC icons joining Man of Tomorrow, it also isn't hard to imagine another alien figure factoring into the plot, though the flick is getting extremely crowded as it is.

Yes, James Gunn is the sole writer and director of Man of Tomorrow.

Despite his previous role as co-chairman and co-CEO of DC Studios, Gunn is extremely hands-on when it comes to most DCU projects. In fact, it seems he had already begun working on his next movie after Man of Tomorrow, though his unceremonious exit will almost certainly mean the end of those prepares.

He's also co-producing alongside Peter Safran, who was also ousted in November 2026's DC Studios shakeup.

The rest of the crew includes Sam McCurdy (Peacemaker, Shogun) as cinematographer, Fred Raskin (Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3, Supergirl) as editor, and David Fleming (Superman, Anaconda) as the main composer, among others.

Industry News: Robertson eclipses Dalglish to become Scotland's most capped man

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (975 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You've done Liverpool and Scotland proud - Kenny Dalglish on Andy Robertson's career.
  • Andy Robertson has become Scotland's most capped men's international after starting in Monday's Nations League game in Switzerland to reach 103 appearances for his country.
  • Twelve years on from his debut - off the bench in a Poland friendly - he surpassed his friend and fellow Liverpool legend, Kenny Dalglish, whose record haul had stood for 40 years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You've done Liverpool and Scotland proud - Kenny Dalglish on Andy Robertson's career.

Andy Robertson has become Scotland's most capped men's international after starting in Monday's Nations League game in Switzerland to reach 103 appearances for his country.

Twelve years on from his debut - off the bench in a Poland friendly - he surpassed his friend and fellow Liverpool legend, Kenny Dalglish, whose record haul had stood for 40 years.

After moving level with the man they - and he - will always call King, the Tottenham Hotspur left-back shifted chat towards the former forward, his commendable humility laid bare.

But, in St Gallen, the spotlight shone on one of Scotland's favourite sons as he moves solo at the summit.

Robertson set to make history, but hero Dalglish will always be King.

Inside the fairytale journey of Scotland captain Robertson.

Andy Robertson on his hero, Kenny Dalglish.

For much of this year, Dalglish was the only man to have pulled on the navy blue of Scotland more times than Robertson.

'King Kenny' topped the list on 102 caps - earning his last in November 1986 against Luxembourg when in a player-manager role at Liverpool.

Few since have even come close to toppling him - and Robertson is keen to stress the throne is still reserved for Dalglish - but it is perhaps fitting it is the current captain, given their great friendship.

Which allows Dalglish to say he's not having any of it.

It has been revealed that "He always says: 'You've got millions more games. Nations League, what's that? They didn't have that in my day!'" Robertson joked on the Stick to Football podcast recently.

"I think he might bring up a ratio for years-to-games-played so he's still on top.

"It's obviously something that's been on my radar for a while now. When you get to 80-odd caps, you start to look up.".

Dalglish can console himself that his record of 30 goals - held jointly with Denis Law - is safely out of Robertson's reach.

But not out of John McGinn's - the midfielder's double against North Macedonia on Friday took him to within six of the legendary duo.

The Aston Villa captain is lurking only eight caps behind Robertson on the all-time caps list, too, so the Scotland men's centurion club could have three members soon.

Since being given the armband by Alex McLeish after Scott Brown retired in 2018, Robertson has captained Scotland 33 times more than any other player.

At the time, he had earned just 22 caps and was just 24 but had established himself as Liverpool's left-back as they reached the Champions League final.

Now he is the only man to have led Scotland out at three major finals, reaching the milestone at the World Cup this summer.

Scotland and Napoli midfielder Scott McTominay enthused: "He's such a great captain and he's got that good balance between being one of the senior players and saying you need to wake up if you're not playing well.

Recent findings suggest that "Then he's also got the personable side, organising things with the manager, helping young players and stuff. He's brilliant with that, brilliant.".

One of those young players is 20-year-old Findlay Curtis, who told the media the night before Robertson's historic night that his captain has "probably been the biggest role model" he's looked up to since joining the international set-up earlier this year.

According to recent reports, perhaps that was because Robertson did him a turn back in the day. Unbeknownst to the skipper.

Rangers winger Curtis was only 14 during the Covid pandemic and was partial to playing a bit of Fifa, and Robertson was a star in his team.

In a recent development, "I was just thinking, I had him in my Fifa team," he explained. "[For] defending and he was just fast as well.

"What a servant he has been for the country.".

'I had him in my Fifa team!' - Findlay Curtis on going from fan to team-mate of Robertson.

Robertson has played under four permanent Scotland team bosses in his 12-year international career.

It was Strachan who plucked him from the under-21s to hand him his debut as a 19-year-old in a win over Poland in March 2014.

McLeish made him captain in 2018, calling Robertson the "outstanding candidate" and an "inspirational figure" - and now he has played five times for latest boss Sebastien Pocognoli.

He even played one game under interim manager Malky Mackay in a friendly against the Netherlands at Pittodrie in 2017 as the Scottish FA searched for Strachan's replacement.

However, it is Steve Clarke's seven-year stint that Robertson will be mainly associated with, as the pair led Scotland to three major tournaments.

Robertson played 68 times for Clarke, all of them as captain, and the recently departed head coach consistently praised his figurehead.

"He's been a fantastic captain for Scotland," Clarke said at the World Cup.

"He's worked ever so hard for the country and he leads the group like the leader he is - and he's very, very important to me and the squad.".

Over the piece, Robertson's caps are spread fairly evenly among friendlies and qualification games.

It has been revealed that crucially, though, he has also played nine times in major tournaments. What will rankle with him is there is only one win among those nine - June's victory over Haiti in Boston at the World Cup.

Overall, though, Robertson's Scotland career can be characterised by consistency.

He has started 101 of his 103 caps, rarely ever being substituted. He has not missed a camp in three years.

The only question seems to be how many Scotland caps will Robertson end up with?

At 32 and still playing in the Premier League, it appears there will be plenty more to come.
