Tech Report: The New James Bond Has Been Cast. Who Will Do the Next Theme Song?

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1658 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Billboard

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that it’s over.
  • The announcement came after a five-year search which reportedly included potentials such as Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Nicholas Hoult.
  • Recent findings suggest that pattison will be joined by Denis Villeneuve, director of the Dune trilogy (the upcoming Dune 3 flick will star Pattison) and Arrival.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that it’s over. The psychodrama that has enveloped the casting of the next James Bond reached its conclusion on Monday (Nov. 16) when Robert Pattinson assumed the role of 007.

The announcement came after a five-year search which reportedly included potentials such as Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Nicholas Hoult. Go back even further, and Idris Elba and Henry Cavill have been linked with the role since Daniel Craig declared that No Time to Die (2021) would be his final outing in the role. If you were a British actor and 6’0 or above you were bound to be given some consideration for this role. (Tough luck, Tom Holland.).

Recent findings suggest that pattison will be joined by Denis Villeneuve, director of the Dune trilogy (the upcoming Dune 3 flick will star Pattison) and Arrival. He joins as the Bond franchise enters a new era, with Amazon MGM taking control of the beloved series for its 26th official outing, after decades under the stewardship of the Broccoli family and producer Michael Wilson.

It has been revealed that now comes the fun part: the Bond song. Nearly all of the movies has been soundtracked with a signature, original song for its opening credit sequence, a tradition that began with Shirley Bassey’s iconic “Goldfinger” from 1964.

Recent findings suggest that music’s finest has since tackled the mission with chart success, to boot. Duran Duran’s “A View to Kill” is the only Bond song to hit No. 1 on Billboard’s Hot 100, with Carly Simon (1977’s “Nobody Does it Better,” No. 2), Paul McCartney (1973’s “Live and Let Die,” No. 2) and Sheena Easton (1981’s “For Your Eyes Only,” No. 4) also scoring significant hits with their own themes. In the 21st century, Adele (2012’s “Skyfall,” No. 8), Madonna (“Die Another Day,” No. 8), and Billie Eilish (“No Time to Die,” No. 16) have all also seen similar success.

It has been revealed that for many it’s a dream gig, and the ultimate collaboration between music and a film series that prides itself on being the coolest and suavest of them all. These are our frontrunner predictions for who will record the title track to the upcoming 26th James Bond film, presented in no particular order.

Callum Turner, Dua’s husband, was reportedly part of the final five actors that were in consideration for the role, making it a distinct possibility that the pair could pull off a remarkable double-act. Ultimately Turner was passed over, but Dua’s name has still been floated as a potential future Bond performer. She has an international profile, and her 2024 live album recorded at the Royal Albert Hall showed her ability to perform with a string section, undoubtedly a prerequisite for cutting a track for the franchise. – THOMAS SMITH.

According to recent reports, perhaps, then, Pattinson might like to keep it in the family. The fresh lead actor is married to Suki Waterhouse, who has embarked on a successful solo music career in recent years — with three LPs released on Sub Pop, most recently 2026’s Loveland. Her songwriting has a classic feel and she’s collaborated with accomplished songwriters such as Amy Allen, the Dessner brothers and Blue May. It’s hard to imagine this not working. – T.S.

Recent findings suggest that dean is one of British music’s biggest exports in the 2020s with sold-out arena reveals internationally and, as of this week, six Grammy nominations. As Pattison’s casting shows, there is appetite for headline-grabbing moves, and Dean would certainly be another. “Loud” from The Art of Loving features the kind of dramatic build and – yes – a swelling string section that you can totally picture over the opening credits. – T.S.

It has been revealed that this Music May Contain Hope, RAYE’s sophomore album, could be read as a perfect audition piece for the role. It is an ambitious and classy collection that utilizes a full orchestra, and also saw RAYE work closely with composer Hans Zimmer, who scored the 2021 film No Time to Die, and contributed to Billie Eilish’s title track of the same name. It’s a connection that could potentially be too good to overlook. – T.S.

Could Adele, author and singer of 2012’s towering “Skyfall,” one of the Bond franchise’s most celebrated tracks, also be in the running? If British press reports are to be believed, the icon is presently gearing up to release newly introduced material, and such was the success of “Skyfall” – which scooped a Grammy (best song written for visual media) BRIT Award (British single of the year) and an Academy Award (best original song), among dozens of other trophies – that it would be foolish to rule her out for seconds, particularly if she ends up kicking off another blockbuster album campaign. – S.W.

In a recent development, with Villeneuve at the helm of the next Bond film, the Dune director could fulfill a long-standing wish among fans: to evolve the franchise by looking to the past with a period piece. And who better to soundtrack a potential shift towards the swinging ’60s than the retro soul-obsessed Sienna Spiro, whose raspy, distinct vocals would sit comfortably alongside previous Bond theme performers like Sam Smith and Adele? “I think it is my biggest dream,” the 20-year-old singer told Capital FM in an interview last year, when asked about the prospect of recording for the soundtrack. Consider it a wish worth granting, Genie. – SOPHIE WILLIAMS.

Recent findings suggest that one of the greatest “what-if”s in Bond history was Radiohead’s pitch to soundtrack 2015’s Spectre. When approached by director Sam Mendes, the band suggested “Man of War,” an unreleased recording from the OK Computer sessions which Yorke said was inspired by the Bond themes of the past. When a upcoming original composition was required, the band pulled together the haunting “Spectre,” but was told that it had arrived too late, and that the creation of the credit sequence had begun with Smith’s “Writing’s on the Wall.” Mendes later called it “an utter nightmare… We had this beautiful song and we weren’t able to use it.”.

The band felt strongly enough about it, however, to release it as a free download on Christmas Day in 2015, their first release as a group in four years. Villeneuve has incorporated Radiohead tracks into a number of his previous films (Incendies, 2010; Prisoners, 2013), so perhaps he could convince the lads to give it another shot. – T.S.

Sources indicate that 007 could perhaps be the only way to get Noel and Liam Gallagher back in the studio together. Upcoming Oasis material has not been forthcoming – despite Liam’s playful teasing – but when asked about stepping up for His Majesty’s Secret Service, Noel highlighted a surprising amount of enthusiasm. Speaking on TalkSport radio, the elder brother (and chief songwriter) noted he would do “in a heartbeat”, and said “it’d be an absolute honour.” Clearly some kind of national pride had kicked in: “I think those kinds of things should be done by Brits, not Yanks.” – T.S.

Industry observers note that lana Del Rey has long been on wishlists to tackle a Bond song. In 2015, she unsuccessfully pitched “24” for the film Spectre (which was won by Sam Smith), and the song eventually surfaced on her LP Honeymoon. In 2026, she provided the song “First Light” for the video game 007 First Light working alongside David Arnold, who co-wrote songs with Garbage and Chris Cornell for the franchise. Is this a make-up for the previous snub? Or perhaps an audition for the real deal? – T.S.

The Catalan-born singer is surely a front-runner for this for a number of reasons. She’s one of the most critically acclaimed artists on the planet right now, with LUX already triumphant at the 2026 Latin Grammys and nominated for multiple awards at the 2027 Grammys. That album proved her range as a singer, and that she understood the opportunities of working closely alongside a full orchestra. No Latin artist has ever tackled the assignment, and given Bond’s established stature around the world, this could resonate on a global scale. – T.S.

Recent findings suggest that it’s been a hot minute since a rock band got the call, with Scottish-American rockers Garbage being the last when they tackled 1999’s The World is Not Enough. Rock frontmen-gone-solo Chris Cornell (“You’ll Know My Name,” Casino Royale, 2006) and Jack White (“Another Way to Die,” Quantum of Solace, 2008) both provided their talents, but each act since has come from the pop world, not rock.

On their fresh LP Dopamine Chamber, however, there’s hints that they could be well-suited for the spot: “You Miss Me” integrates a striking string section but retains their edge; “Where Is Gone?” is a gorgeous collaboration with Rosalía that has real emotional heft. That said, an Irish band contributing to a franchise that is – for better or worse – so intrinsically tied up with British identity does feel fanciful. – T.S.

It has been revealed that off the back of the North Shields singer-songwriter’s most prolific year to date, which has seen him announce a mega U.K. and Ireland stadium tour for 2027 (plus his biggest North American headline dates yet), scoop multiple BRIT Awards and score the longest-running U.K. No. 1 single of all time with Olivia Dean team-up “Rein Me In,” Sam Fender is, to put it mildly, teeming with clout. Could the next major step in his sky-rocketing career see Bond producers come a-calling? For starters, Fender has a deeply emotive tone and can belt to the nines (see People Watching standout “Remember My Name”); a big swing like this would only do wonders for the stature and star power of U.K. indie’s favorite son. – S.W.

#729. Jane Lynch Reveals Whether She’ll Return for Glee Reboot

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 22m • 📚 Deep Dive (4393 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Eonline ↗ Open Full Page

Jane Lynch Reveals Whether She’ll Return for Glee Reboot

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 22 min read (4393 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eonline

⏱️ ~22 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sue Sylvester may be picking up the whistle once again.
  • Glee fans have been curious about whether Jane Lynch will reprise her role as the cheerleading coach on the musical series' upcoming reboot, and she's now finally weighing in.
  • According to recent reports, "If I am asked to partake, the answer will be yes," she said on the Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sue Sylvester may be picking up the whistle once again.

Glee fans have been curious about whether Jane Lynch will reprise her role as the cheerleading coach on the musical series' upcoming reboot, and she's now finally weighing in.

According to recent reports, "If I am asked to partake, the answer will be yes," she said on the Nov. 16 episode of The Jennifer Hudson Show. "I would love to do Sue Sylvester for the rest of my life.".

The 66-year-old went on to share what it would feel like to play the iconic villain again over a decade after Glee originally came to an end in 2015.

"You know, I wonder though how far we can take her now, because if you look out in the world, there are a lot of Sue Sylvesters out there,” Lynch mused. “I think I kind of made the mold for everybody, but I can’t wait. I think it would be really, really fun to do it again and to get to wear tracksuits every day. And my that was my most favorite wardrobe.".

Though it remains to be seen which of the cast—which also included Matthew Morrison, Harry Shum Jr., Lea Michele, Chris Colfer, Amber Riley and more—will appear in the reboot, creator Ryan Murphy previously hinted that some William McKinley High School alums will be returning.

"I've been in touch with around 10 of the original cast members," he told Entertainment Tonight in September. "It's very sweet, and they all had a lot of questions, but they all were very enthusiastic about the idea.".

Michele had also expressed interest in playing Rachel Berry again in a potential Glee revival—if it felt right.

"I love Glee," she told E! News in September. "I will always love Glee. I love Ryan Murphy. It just holds such a special place in my heart for me. So, I will follow Ryan wherever he goes.".

In the meantime, keep reading for an encore on everything Glee...

A few years after Glee ended, Ryan Murphy reflected on the pop culture phenomenon and revealed how chaotic things were behind the scenes.

"It was the best time in my life and the worst time in my life," he told Entertainment Weekly, going on to admit, "There was a lot of infighting. There was a lot of people sleeping together and breaking up. It was good training for being a parent, I'll tell you that much.".

He also reflected on his time on the show, looking back with some regret on how he handled things as the showrunner.

Sources indicate that "I was there with them all day long, and then we'd finish work and we'd go out and have fun all night, and I guess in a weird, twisted way, I was trying to relive the childhood I never had," he told THR. "I thought they wanted a parent, and they didn't. They didn't want me to tell them what to f—king do. They didn't want me to tell them how to treat each other or what the world was like at the end of the day. I wish I could go back and do that differently with a lot of those actors. Some of them I'm still very close to: Lea Michele, Chord Overstreet, Darren Criss — but there were some that didn't work out well, and I regret that. I guess I just wish I had been able to let them figure it out for themselves.".

Going on to create Scream Queens, American Horror Story, Pose and other hit series, Murphy remarked Glee "was a great lesson in what not to do moving forward.".

It has been revealed that fun fact: Ryan Murphy wrote the role of Rachel Berry with Lea Michele, a Broadway standout thanks to Spring Awakening, in mind. But not every cast member's journey to becoming a Gleek was so easy.

Before he was cast as Blaine, Criss auditioned for the role of Finn, the lead quarterback.

It has been revealed that "It was the first audition I ever had. I auditioned for the pilot," he revealed at the Paleyfest panel. "And then I remember watching the pilot to see who got the part [I went out for] and seeing Cory [Monteith got it] and thinking, oh, obviously, right.".

Another star who also auditioned for a different part was Colfer, who read for Artie originally. Producers were so impressed by the teen that they created the role of Kurt specifically for him.

In fact, Murphy revealed Colfer's audition was the inspiration behind creating The Glee Project, the show's reality competitions series that gave aspiring actors the chance to be cast on Glee.

"It's such a huge honor and I mean that's really special because I feel like if I inspired something that is giving kids a platform that is incredible," Colfer remarked.

The final cast member to join the show? Dianna Agron, who played head cheerleader Quinn Fabray, landing the role the day before they filmed the pilot.

Initially, Quinn was supposed to be the stereotypical mean girl, but Agron's nature ended up changing the role for the writers.

Recent findings suggest that "When we cast Dianna as Quinn, she ruined the part for me," Murphy told Rolling Stone. "She was supposed to be the Cybill Shepherd, Last Picture Show c—, so to speak, but she humanized it. She can cry at the drop of a hat. So now her character has a conscience, a soul and great vulnerability.".

Agron would leave the show after season three, returning only for the 100th episode.

Just like in the hallways of McKinley High, the Glee set featured a lot of flirtation and relationships between its young stars. (And even before the show, as Lea Michele revealed in her 2014 memoir Brunette Ambition that she and Matthew Morrison "actually dated back in for the day for a Broadway beat.").

Michele and Cory Monteith, whose characters were one of the show's most iconic couples," dated for several years before Monteith's tragic death in 2013, while Blake Jenner and Melissa Benoist, who now stars on Supergirl, married in 2015 after meeting on the set in 2012 when they also played love interests; they split in 2016 and their divorce was finalized the following year.

In a recent development, naya Rivera and Mark Salling briefly dated in the show's earlier days and it wasn't an amicable split, as Rivera would write in her 2016 memoir, "I think everyone should have that one relationship where you look back and ask yourself, 'What the hell was I thinking?' You'll learn something and you won't regret it. Unless, of course, that relationship was with someone who had a sizable stash of child porn on his computer. Then, by all means, regret everything." Rivera was referring to Salling's child pornography indictment in 2017. In January 2018, Salling committed suicide at the age of 35.

While they first met when she guest-starred on Glee, Gwyneth Paltrow didn't begin dating future husband Brad Falchuk, one of Glee's co-creators, until she returned to the show in 2014, over a year after her split from Coldplay frontman Chris Martin.

Industry observers note that "When you're going through a divorce and you think about going out with somebody, it's a weird thing," she told Howard Stern of taking it slowly with Falchuk, a recently-divorced father of two. "So I don't think it's the same as being 23 and running into someone at a coffee shop. It's just different. You have kids, you have divorce—it's just a lot of stuff.".

They got married in October 2018.

While there were whispers of a romance between Kevin McHale (Artie) and Jenna Ushkowitz (Tina) during the show's run, it turns out they were just in a showmance, which became the latest of their hit podcast.

Industry observers note that given its popularity and millions of downloads (including huge bumps for the original versions of the songs covered by the cast), you would think any band or artist would give Glee the rights to their songs. But there were several major bands that wouldn't let the glee club put their take on their tunes: Kings of Leon, with Murphy calling the band members "self-centered assholes" because they "missed the significant picture" aka how the show could inspire kids to join arts education through their songs, namely their hit "Use Somebody." A mini-Twitter feud followed.

According to recent reports, guns N' Roses guitarist Slash also rejected Glee's request, saying he wasn't a fan of the show. "Usually I find people who make those comments, their careers are over' they're uneducated and stupid," Murphy remarked.

The Foo Fighters didn't approve the show's request either, with Dave Grohl calling out Murphy in an interview with THR.

According to recent reports, "You shouldn't have to do f--king Glee," he said. "And then the guy who created Glee is so offended that we're not, like, begging to be on his f--king show...I watched 10 minutes...it's not my thing.".

Colfer and Ushkowitz lived together during the show's run and often had cast parties at their apartment.

"Those of us who were obviously over-age would drink themselves into the oblivion," McHale remarked on Showmance, his podcast with Ushkowitz, before Colfer chimed in, "Oh, I drank too." (During a 2013 Paleyfest panel, Colfer revealed he actually had his first drink at their apartment.).

Amber Riley (Mercedes) smoked her first and last cigarette during one of their many late nights there, with the foursome being so close they called themselves JACK (the first initial of all of their names).

Sources indicate that they also reminisced on their wild nights out while on their concert tour, with Riley revealing she got into a fight with a random girl while in London with the cast. After realizing she had punched the girl, she told their security team who then paid the girl off to stay quiet. Colfer, still not 21 at the time, admitted to sneaking into a lot of bars.

Because they were a young, close-knit cast, many things the stars were going through ended up on-screen, especially early on.

Industry observers note that "There have been a couple of times when I have gone to Ryan Murphy and told him a couple of things that have happened to me, and then he writes it into the show," Colfer mentioned in an interview with PR.com. "Or he'll ask me what song I would want to sing, in this situation or in that situation. I don't think any of us directly try to give input on the character or on the storyline, but they definitely steal things from us. I remember I was talking to Ryan about when I was in high school and I really wanted to sing 'Defying Gravity.' The other students in my drama class and the teachers, when we were putting on this talent show, they wouldn't let me sing it because I was a boy and it was a girl's song. And then that was made [into] an episode.".

And star Chord Overstreet's (Sam) plump lips even worked their way into a storyline...and song, called "Trouty Mouth.".

Recent findings suggest that during a Paleyfest panel, Overstreet said, "I never even realized my lips were anything until the jokes started coming. And they wrote that freakin' song!".

While he ultimately didn't snag the role of Finn (his first audition ever!), Darren Criss ended up becoming one of the biggest breakout stars of the series when he made his debut as Head Warbler Blaine Anderson in season two. His first scene, which featured his performance of Katy Perry's "Teenage Dream," set up one of the show's most popular couples, Klaine (Kurt and Blaine), but also delivered one of Glee's most successful singles of all-time, debuting at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100.

Criss, one of the stars and creators of the popular YouTube "A Very Potter Musical" pre-Glee (He played Harry Potter, of course!), was promptly promoted to series regular and became one of the central characters.

And when Murphy was looking to cast the role of serial killer Andrew Cunanan for The Assassination of Gianni Versace: American Crime Story, he surprised many when he chose Criss, crediting his turn on Broadway in Hedwig and the Angry Inch.

"I just knew he could do it," Murphy revealed to EW. "More than that, I knew that he was super hungry and ambitious. I think people thought of Darren as a musical comedy star first. But, when I saw Hedwig, I knew he was capable of great darkness.".

Criss' performance on the FX hit series earned him a Golden Globe, Emmy and SAG Award.

While she would go on to become one of the show's most beloved stars, Heather Morris was actually brought in by the show's choreographer just to teach Colfer how to do the "Single Ladies" dance because she was one of Beyoncé's back-up dancers. Producers then decided to cast her as a background player when they needed a third cheerleader, but they quickly realized they had a secret weapon in Morris, who had a knack for tossing out one-liners "(Did you know dolphins are just gay sharks?") and became a fan-favorite. She was promoted to series regular in season two, becoming the focus of the  Britney Spears tribute episode and one-half of one of the show's most popular couples with Naya Rivera's Santana.

For the fifth season, Morris became a recurring guest star after getting pregnant in real-life, with the actress choosing not to return as a full-time cast member.

At the height of its fame, it seemed like everyone appeared on Glee or wanted to appear on Glee. Some of the show's biggest guest star gets included Gwyneth Paltrow, John Stamos, Helen Mirren (via voiceover), Carol Burnett, Kate Hudson, Lindsay Lohan, Ricky Martin, Sarah Jessica Parker and Whoopi Goldberg, among many, many more.

Still, there were some unveiled guest stars who never ended up Gleeking out: Javier Bardem was supposed to play a rock star who befriends Artie, which never came to fruition. Anne Hathaway was set to play Kurt's lesbian aunt, but never popped up.

Jennifer Lopez also met with producers, but it never ended up materializing.

After tributes to Madonna and Lady Gaga, Glee staged its most successful tribute episode: in season two: "Britney/Brittany," an homage to Britney Spears. (They did a second Brit tribute episode in season four.).

According to recent reports, it was [Britney's] idea," Murphy said of the pop icon's response to the honor. "I think she loves what the show's about, paying tribute to pop culture in a very loving, respectful, kind way. She responded to that.".

Unlike Madonna and Gaga though, Spears actually appeared as herself in the episode.

In a recent development, "I loved it! Thank you guys SO much for making this happen!" the "I'm A Slave 4 U" singer tweeted.

And Spears was particularly taken with Morris, writing, "Awww Heather Morris is sooo cute! Brittany S Pearce. Ha! She was so fun to work with and was really sweet in person.".

It was a major moment for Morris, who idolized Spears growing up.

Recent findings suggest that "She was my idol from, like, age 12 to 16," Morris told TV Week. "I sang to her [songs] in my living room and danced to her—I learned all her moves. And I had my talent shows and I lip-synced to her. I just kept flashing back to growing up and being obsessed with her.".

According to recent reports, glee was so popular that the main cast went on a national tour from 2010-11, selling out almost all of their 40 dates. (Eventually it went overseas as well, visiting European cities.).

It has been revealed that "The response of the fans to our little show has been so immediate and so gratifying, we wanted to get out and thank them live and in person," Murphy said when the tour was announced. "And what show lends itself more to a concert than Glee?".

The tour would go on to gross $40 million, and resulted in the two-week theatrical release of Glee: The 3D Concert Movie, using footage from the cast's concert in Fresh Jersey.

As for their music sales, the show's 16 soundtrack albums and six compilation albums had sold over 7.9 million copies by 2015, while their songs had been downloaded over 45 million times and sold 53 million copies.

It has been revealed that you can't stay in high school, even when you're attending TV high school. Still, fans were shocked when hen Murphy told THR that the series' main trio Michele, Monteith and Colfer would not be returning for season four after their class graduated from McKinley. Rumors of a potential New York-set spinoff being explored by the producers surfaced, which would find Rachel and Kurt trying to make their Broadway dreams come true in the Significant Apple.

"You can keep them on the show for six years and people will criticize you for not being realistic," Murphy remarked at the time, "or you can be really true to life and say when they started the show they were very clearly sophomores and they should graduate at the end of their senior year.".

But the trio ended up staying on Glee, which focused on their post-college prepares while also introducing upcoming students into the mix at McKinley, with the network's then president telling reporters ahead of season four, "There will not be a Glee spinoff.".

Industry observers note that still, season four presented a shake-up for the show, with Murphy telling Vulture he gave the original cast members the choice to exit the series if they wanted after their characters graduated. "I mentioned to them, 'Anybody who wants to stay on the show will stay on the show,'" he explained. Almost everyone stayed but many dropped down to recurring or guest star status.

During Glee's third season, The Glee Project kicked off on Oxygen, which found the contestants competing for a role on the main show.

In a recent development, from its two season-run, Glee brought four contestants over, including season one's winners Samuel Larsen and Damian McGinty Jr., as well as runner-ups Lindsay Pearce and Alex Newell. Blake Jenner, the winner of season two, became a series regular in season five, while the runner-up Ali Stroker made an unexpected guest appearance in season four.

One of the show's breakout stars, winning a Golden Globe for his turn as Kurt, Colfer went on to write an episode of Glee in season five, later admitting he was terrified to take on the challenge despite writing several novels, as well as the film adaptation of his book Struck By Lighting.

"When they first approached me I said, absolutely not," he said during a Paleyfest panel. "I'm not putting words into my costars' mouths. There was a lot of pressure.".

His onscreen paramour Darren Criss also penned something for Glee during the show's run, writing an original song for the series finale called "This Time.".

Industry observers note that "I basically wrote a love note to the entire experience," Criss explained of the song, which Michele sang in the episode. "Having Lea sing it to me is one of the most special moments of my career.".

It was just as special for Michele, who remarked, "Darren gave me the greatest gift. Honestly. That was the day I fell to my knees and cried. I literally had to call my mother to come [get me]. It's so special, it was the most amazing memory.".

The song would go on to be nominated for an Emmy.

Recent findings suggest that in 2011, a Glee extra/fan found herself in hot water when she shared major spoilers on Twitter, revealing most of the major happenings at the prom. Co-creator Brad Falchuk put her on blast, responding, "Who are you to spoil something talented people have spent months to create?".

He then added, "hope you're qualified to do something besides work in entertainment.".

The leaker Nicole Crowther, then 2, received "very, very hateful messages" from fans and said she was "black-balled" by every agency in town.

"I had no idea it would even come close to anything it's been," she told E! News. "I regret it and I can totally understand, not only where the fans are coming from, but why Brad and other people from Fox are furious with me. I can understand their point of view.".

Industry observers note that A few years later, the show had another Twitter scandal when someone hacked Colfer's account and tweeted he was leaving the show. "Due to personal issues, I have been let go from the cast of GLEE. Explanations will come shortly..." the message read.

After the mass hysteria from Klaine fans subsided when the show's rep denied Colfer was leaving the show, the actor appeared on Good Morning America, calling the hack "very upsetting.".

It has been revealed that "Some jerk hacked me," he remarked. "It was a pain, it really was.".

In her 2016 memoir, Sorry Not Sorry: Dreams, Mistakes and Growing Up, Rivera revealed she got an abortion during the show's run.

In late 2010, Naya discovered she was pregnant just weeks after breaking up with actor Ryan Dorsey, whom she later wed in 2014 and is the father of her son, Josey Dorsey (they divorced in 2018).

She chose not share the news with Dorsey at the time, instead choosing to focus on her career; she terminated the pregnancy during a day off from filming an episode of Glee.

"I think every woman should have the right to choose, and it scares me to think of a world where the decision of whether to have a child is not her choice to make," she wrote.

After Monteith's sudden and tragic death from combined drug intoxication in 2013 at the age of 31, questions arose about how Glee would handle his passing and Finn's absence on the show (with Murphy telling E! News they even considered ending  the series).

After taking an extended hiatus, Glee addressed Monteith's death in "The Quarterback," a beautiful tribute episode that revealed Finn had died. It was an emotional and somber hour of television, both on-screen and off as each cast member was given a change to honor Monteith in the episode.

"Almost everything in that episode is from the first take of every performance because the actors and the crew had a really hard time shooting it,' Murphy stated at the time. "I've never seen a crew that you can't continue shooting because they've left the room sobbing. It was very hard. I struggled even working on it because what they felt, not just about Finn but Cory.".

The episode ended with Michele, Monteith's girlfriend, singing Bob Dylan's "Make You Feel My Love," and Rachel returning to McKinley to hang a plaque in the choir room featuring a picture of Finn and a quote from him that reads: "The show must go...all over the place...or something.".

Industry observers note that matthew Morrison said of the filming, "[Lea] had one of the first songs we filmed for the episode and she did it so beautifully and after, she said something like, 'It can't be harder for anyone else than it was for me.' So, we knew we had to show up because our leader stepped forward and kind of gave permission to all of us to do it. I don't think we could have done it without her.".

In an In Memoriam piece penned for Entertainment Weekly in 2013, Murphy revealed the ending he and the writers originally envisioned for Finchel's journey on the show.

Sources indicate that "Rachel comes back to Ohio, fulfilled and yet not, and walks into Finn's glee club," he explained. "'What are you doing here?' he would ask. 'I'm home,' she would reply. Fade out. The End.".

Three of Michele's 16 tattoos are Glee-related: Michele showed off her "Finn" tattoo when she posed naked for the cover of Women's Health U.K., a tattoo Rachel had gotten on the show as a tribute to Finn after his death. Michele also has the No. 5 in honor of Monteith, which was Finn's football jersey number.

"And one more...for my Quarterback...#5," she captioned the Instagram post debuting her new body ink.

In a recent development, she also has a tiny gold star on her left wrist as a nod to her character Rachel and one of her lines from the pilot episode: "You may laugh because every time I sign my name I put a gold star after it, but it's a metaphor, and metaphors are important. My gold stars are a metaphor for ME being a star.".

In an interview with Rolling Stone, Michele revealed she and co-stars Ushkowitz and McHale got matching "Imagine" tattoos on their feet, a nod to The Beatles, during a night out and a few glasses of wine.

"I'm known to be the instigator to do some more risky stuff. So we have little tattoos on our feet now," she said. "It made a lot of sense that night.".

Many of the cast members have remained since the series ended in 2015, proving once a Gleek always a Gleek.

Michele and Criss have gone on co-headlining tours together, and Michele performed at Criss' nuptials to longtime girlfriend Mia Swier in February 2019. Criss was also present Michele married Zandy Reich a month later in a ceremony officiated by Murphy. Becca Tobin, who joined Glee in season four and ow stars in E!'s Ladygang, was also present as she and Michele have continued to be best friends in the years since Glee.

When Tobin got married in 2016 Jane Lynch officiated the ceremony, which was a mini-Glee reunion with Michele, McHale, Ushkowitz, Meg Doyle, Michael Hitchcock, Matt Hodgson and Dante Russo all in attendance.

Sources indicate that in 2018, Morrison reunited many of the member of New Directions to meet his newborn son, Revel James Makai Morrison. "It's a GLEE-Union!!" Morrison captioned the photo of the gang, including Michele, Rivera, Riley, Morris, Colfer, Criss and more. "What a beautiful night hangin with my old kids & new kid! Ohana...".

In March, some of the Gleeks, including Crazy Rich Asians' Harry Shum Jr., reunited on-screen, competing against each other on Drop the Mic.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crystal Palace are Thomas Frank's third London club after previous spells with Brentford and Tottenham.

"When the time is right I will look forward to my return as a manager, ready to embrace the job with great energy and dedication," said Thomas Frank in June.

That time is now after the Dane was confirmed as the new manager of Crystal Palace, who are two points and a goal difference deficit away from safety at the bottom of the Premier League.

Former boss Pierre Sage was sacked last week after just 16 league and cup games.

The role offers Frank an opportunity to rebuild his reputation after he was sacked by Tottenham in February after eight months.

Frank described it as "an honour" to be "in charge of this fantastic football club" as Palace revealed his arrival on a deal running to June 2029.

"Crystal Palace is an iconic club in England and in the Premier League," Frank told Palace's website.

"I will do everything I possibly can to help and support the players and everyone around the place, and I'm really looking forward to meeting them.".

Palace chairman Steve Parish remarked Frank was the "perfect fit for our club".

But how significant is the challenge at Selhurst Park that awaits the man who made his name at Brentford?

"It's going to be a bit of a shock for Thomas Frank," former West Ham and England goalkeeper Rob Green tells BBC Sport.

"He had his success at Brentford - a very well-run club where players are brought in with a lot of thinking and planning to take over the players they sell for profit.

"That doesn't happen at Crystal Palace.

"They lose players and then have a mad scramble to get players in. They have a team that has been decimated by sales and not replaced by the same quality.

"Thomas Frank needs to find something within that team that builds and garners the belief that means that they can compete in the Premier League, because it feels a long way short of that right now.".

Will Frank prove the right fit for Palace and haul the Eagles out of the relegation zone?

Frank 'the perfect man' for Palace job.

Since getting the sack at Tottenham after 26 league games last season, Frank has been out of management longer than he was in charge of Spurs.

In the summer he released a statement in which he said "there have been conversations and opportunities" to return to management, but that he had "decided not to rush into the next role".

Frank's name was heavily linked with Palace before they went for a head coach with no Premier League experience to replace Oliver Glasner - the man who delivered an FA Cup, a Conference League title and the Community Shield before moving to Nottingham Forest.

According to recent reports, "Palace had one of the best managers they have had, if not forever, silverware coming across the doorstep. Look at what they achieved last season and instead of building on that, they dismantled a team," remarked former Tottenham and England goalkeeper Paul Robinson.

Frank once described managing as being on a "hamster wheel" and a "crazy circus"., external.

Palace confirmed his coaching staff will include current assistant manager Paddy McCarthy and goalkeeping coach Andy Quy, who previously worked with him at Brentford.

Justin Cochrane, who is part of Thomas Tuchel's England staff, is set to join.

Palace are also in the process of approaching Chelsea set-piece coach Bernardo Cueva, who would join as assistant first-team coach.

It is understood Frank would like to take Andreas Georgson from Tottenham, though the north London club are determined to keep the Swede.

Denmark fitness coach Chris Haslam, who worked with Frank at Tottenham, is another potential member of Palace's new coaching set-up.

A trip to Coventry City awaits Palace on Saturday.

So why does Frank feel now is the right moment to return to management at a club propping up the table?

Frank, who was part of BBC Sport's World Cup punditry team during the summer, will be coming into the job refreshed and with renewed energy and enthusiasm following several months out of the game.

Between his appointment as Brentford boss in October 2018 and the sack at Tottenham earlier this year, he managed without a break for seven years and four months.

Spending the past few months away from Premier League pressure has allowed Frank, in his own words, to "study, observe and learn from other leaders both within sport and beyond".

Will his positivity and passion rub off on a Palace team who have lost seven times in 10 top-flight matches?

Would Thomas Frank be a good fit for Crystal Palace?

Frank, who places a major emphasis on set-piece organisation, will have to hit the ground running at Palace, who have lost their past four league games.

They have conceded more goals than anyone else in the Premier League (24) and have scored only 10 themselves.

"If you want someone to go in and restore some stability and defensive solidity while improving the set-piece element of the team, then Thomas Frank is the perfect man for the job," Times football writer Tom Allnutt told BBC Radio 5 Live's Football Daily podcast.

With the Premier League season just 10 games old, Frank certainly has time to turn it around and will have targets in mind when the transfer window opens in January.

Palace sold France centre-back Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea for Â£52m and Colombia right-back Daniel Munoz to Nottingham Forest for Â£22m during the summer transfer window.

Allnutt added: "We know they have sold so many good players and so far I don't think they have really replaced them adequately.".

Another challenge for Frank is getting midfielder Adam Wharton, who has not played for England since March, back to something like his best form.

These are all challenges the new manager will relish.

After his bruising experience at Tottenham - having established Brentford in the Premier League - Frank has decided to climb back on the hamster wheel with Palace.

"Crystal Palace and Thomas Frank feels like a very good fit," added Robinson.

Crystal Palace fan calls Thomas Frank 'the perfect hire'.

Thomas Frank has a lot of work to do as Crystal Palace have undoubtedly been the worst team in the Premier League so far this season, ranking bottom not just in points (seven) but also goal difference (-14) and expected goal difference (-8.1).

It's the defence where Frank will have to focus most of his attention. Not only have Palace conceded the most goals (24) but they've also faced the most shots (189) and have the worst expected goals against (xGA) figure in the league (21.9).

In a recent development, their attack has actually not been too bad. While only Hull have taken fewer shots, the Eagles have created really good chances and have perhaps been unlucky not to score a few more goals given the opportunities they've had.

Recent findings suggest that there is also one significant factor in Frank's favour. Although Palace may be bottom of the Premier League, they are certainly not cut adrift as they sit just two points from safety.

The side propping up the table at this stage have had an average of just three points in the past 10 seasons, but for as bad as they've been, Palace have seven - the most the bottom side have had after 10 games for 24 years.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co. unveiled Monday that CEO Mark Stewart would be stepping down from his role effective immediately.

Board member Roger Wood is taking over as interim CEO and president, Goodyear mentioned.

The leadership change comes as the tire manufacturer is in the midst of a multiyear transformation plan.

Stewart was hired in January 2024 to lead the tech giant, with the goal of revitalizing the legacy American business to make it more efficient and profitable.

Recent findings suggest that the firm has faced disappointing results thus far, reporting last week third-quarter results that saw net sales down 2.3% year over year and an adjusted net loss of $31 million. Goodyear failed to reach a 10% operating margin by the end of last year, which was a major goal of the turnaround proposal.

Goodyear remarked it formed a special committee of the board earlier this year to conduct a "strategic review of the manufacturer's businesses and operations focused on identifying opportunities to strengthen performance and drive shareholder value.".

It said Monday it will continue that work by evaluating strategic and operational initiatives that include further optimizing the company's business mix and footprint, improving efficiency and investing in upcoming products and capabilities that support long-term growth.

"Goodyear has made meaningful progress in becoming a more efficient and focused firm, and the board believes this is the right moment to transition leadership to accelerate that progress and capture additional opportunity," Goodyear Chair Joe Hinrichs noted in a press release.

The company has faced headwinds from tariffs, higher raw material costs and increased competition from China.

Wood has been a member of the company's board of directors since July 2023 and was previously the co-CEO of Tenneco as well as CEO of Dana Holding Corporation.

The company will start a search for a permanent replacement as part of its strategic review.

Shares of Goodyear were down roughly 4% in early trading Monday.

Watch SpaceX attempt a historic Starship launch and double-catch landing today (Nov. 13)

💡 Key Takeaways
  • ET: SpaceX has launched the Starship Flight 15 mission, but did skip the first stage Super Heavy booster landing.
  • It has been revealed that spaceX plans to launch its Starship megarocket on an unprecedented mission today (Nov.
  • Starship is scheduled to launch on its 15th test flight today from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas, during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Patch for 6:25 p.m. ET: SpaceX has launched the Starship Flight 15 mission, but did skip the first stage Super Heavy booster landing. See launch video and our full Starship Flight 15 liftoff wrap.

It has been revealed that spaceX plans to launch its Starship megarocket on an unprecedented mission today (Nov. 13), and you can watch the action live.

Starship is scheduled to launch on its 15th test flight today from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas, during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT; 4:45 p.m. local Texas time). SpaceX intends to bring both of Starship's stages back to Starbase for a catch by the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — something it has never done before.

In a recent development, you can watch it all live here at Space.com. And there should be a lot to see: Starship Flight 15 will last more than 22 hours, if all goes according to initiative.

Starship consists of two elements: a huge booster known as Super Heavy and an upper-stage spacecraft called Starship, or Ship for short. Both are designed to be fully and rapidly reusable — a first in the world of orbital spaceflight.

The rapidity of Starship's reuse hinges heavily on SpaceX's recovery strategy: Returning both vehicles directly to the launch mount will enable much faster inspection, refurbishment and reflight, the organization has said.

SpaceX has already caught Super Heavy, pulling the feat off on three previous Starship test flights. But it has never tried to do so with Ship, which flies farther and faster than the booster and is therefore a more challenging vehicle to recover.

So today's flight is a pretty big deal for SpaceX.

"If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket," the firm wrote in a Flight 15 mission description.

The action will unspool over two days, if all goes to initiative. Super Heavy will return to Starbase for a touchdown just 6.5 minutes after launch, but Ship will continue on to low Earth orbit.

The upper stage will deploy 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites, during a 42-minute stretch beginning about 35 minutes after liftoff. This will be just the second batch of V3 spacecraft to reach orbit, after the 26 that went up on Flight 14 on Sept. 28.

Sources indicate that ship will then stay aloft for nearly a full day. The mission plan calls for the upper stage to return to Starbase for its chopsticks catch on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), about 22.5 hours after liftoff.

There's no guarantee things will go according to blueprint, however. SpaceX will call off a Ship catch if the vehicle experiences any complications during Flight 15. If something crops up, the company will steer Ship to a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean, either near Hawaii or off the coast of Chile.

Sources indicate that so it'll be a busy weekend for SpaceX, and for space fans who want to keep tabs on the mission. And we can help you out there, with our Flight 15 updates page.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that instability in a system that allows communications between the Federal Aviation Administration, air traffic controllers, and pilots was responsible for the country’s most disastrous nationwide ground stop in air traffic since September 11.
  • It has been revealed that several outlets reported that a failure in the FAA Telecommunications Infrastructure (FTI) network was linked to the FAA’s decision to declare a ground stop.
  • Industry observers note that at the time the ground stop was lifted on Friday evening, over 6,300 flights within, into, or out of the US had been canceled, according to the aviation tech company FlightAware; 9,500 had been delayed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that instability in a system that allows communications between the Federal Aviation Administration, air traffic controllers, and pilots was responsible for the country’s most disastrous nationwide ground stop in air traffic since September 11. The ground stop lasted five hours.

It has been revealed that several outlets reported that a failure in the FAA Telecommunications Infrastructure (FTI) network was linked to the FAA’s decision to declare a ground stop. The FTI is the private communications backbone for the air traffic control system. The system is in the midst of a major, multiyear modernization project, which involves replacing a decades-old network of copper wire with high-speed fiber-optic cables. The FAA has noted the upgrade will reduce outages and outage-related delays, and make the system safer. It will also be equipped to more easily handle newer aircraft, including drones, electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft (eVTOLs), and other “air taxis.”.

Industry observers note that at the time the ground stop was lifted on Friday evening, over 6,300 flights within, into, or out of the US had been canceled, according to the aviation tech company FlightAware; 9,500 had been delayed. Freight and mail flights have also been affected. It will likely take days, if not weeks, for airlines to reposition aircraft and crew and get their schedules back on track.

“It will take us some time to unwind what has happened,” US transportation secretary Sean Duffy said in a Friday evening briefing at the White House. He blamed “old switches, old routers,” and a “data overload” for the communications system failure. He said a “legacy system”—likely referring to FTI—was involved.

In a recent development, the issue was caused by “putting patches into the system” as new equipment was being installed, US Department of Homeland Security secretary Markwayne Mullin said at the White House briefing. “The new technology was overwhelming the older system,” he said.

Mullin noted there were no indications that the outage was related to a cyberattack, but “there’s not complete certainty right now.”.

Recent findings suggest that the system is managed by the government contractor L3Harris Technologies. On its website, L3Harris notes that its “team’s deep knowledge of the US national airspace allows us to upgrade systems without disrupting air traffic operations.” A spokesperson for the firm did not respond to a request for comment.

Industry observers note that in May, L3Harris said it had completed 50 percent of its modernization project. Seventy percent of FAA sites have been upgraded to fiber, the manufacturer said earlier this month. The Trump administration has said it aims to overhaul the nation’s air traffic control system by the end of 2028.

Recent findings suggest that in August, the FAA tapped AT&T to upgrade the FTI, the private FAA communication network, to an entirely latest system. That contract is worth $73 million, though its worth is likely to climb into the billions over the years. Previously, Verizon had been selected to build and operate this new system. L3Harris is meant to operate the legacy system until the upgrades are in place.

Earlier Friday, before the ground stop, US transportation secretary Sean Duffy sent a letter to congressional leaders asking them to approve his department’s request for $30.1 billion in funding to further upgrade the air traffic control system and to improve airports. On Friday, he upped the ask: “I want $50 billion,” he said during a briefing at the White House.

A September report published by the US Government Accountability Office raised concerns that the FAA’s attempt to accelerate long-delayed modernization prepares “could be prioritizing speed over costs and air traffic disruption.” It found that the FAA does not have a “well-documented” life-cycle cost estimate for its programs, and that, rather than a master schedule guiding the sprawling project, has 11,389 schedules that are not integrated.

#721. Astronomers watched a planet vanish in space. Now they know why.

📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (964 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Mashable ↗ Open Full Page

Astronomers watched a planet vanish in space. Now they know why.

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (964 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For seven years, a NASA telescope watched a planet the size of Jupiter cross in front of its star again and again — until one day it didn't.
  • Recent findings suggest that the planet, TOI-2535 b, had been acting a little weird for a while.
  • Then, earlier this year, the planet just stopped showing up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For seven years, a NASA telescope watched a planet the size of Jupiter cross in front of its star again and again — until one day it didn't.

Recent findings suggest that the planet, TOI-2535 b, had been acting a little weird for a while. Each time it passed, which astronomers call a transit, it arrived as much as six hours early or late. The crossings also grew shorter and fainter.

Then, earlier this year, the planet just stopped showing up.

Astronomers knew an exoplanet could drift out of view like this, but they figured it would take decades or even centuries to happen. Imagine their surprise.

"The planet's orbit is tilting so quickly that its transit disappeared while we were watching," remarked Samuel Yee, a UCLA postdoctoral fellow and the study's corresponding author, in a statement.

It has been revealed that the findings reveal the most extreme case yet of two worlds yanking on each other's orbits. The research also offers a rare clue to how giant planets could end up sidling so close to their stars. Scientists think most of these snuggly planets got there in some violent way. Perhaps a close encounter with another object, for example, knocked them onto a stretched-out orbit, and then their star reeled them in. But this pair likely took a gentler route and spiraled in slowly together, according to the upcoming paper, published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

Recent findings suggest that planet TOI-2535 b sits about 1,000 light-years from Earth. It's what's known as a "hot Jupiter," a gas giant that orbits so close to its star that it finishes a lap in about eight days. By contrast, Mercury, our solar system's closest world to the sun, needs 88 days to make a revolution.

To be clear, NASA's TESS, short for Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite, never saw the planet directly. It infers the presence of a planet by catching the tiny decrease in starlight when one passes in front of its star. One day, TESS could no longer track those fluctuations.

But planets don't normally just disappear into thin space. Astronomers knew something else was going on.

In a recent development, those fading crossings told the team that the planet's path was sliding from the middle of the star toward its edge until it was no longer traceable. The planet still circles its star, but from Earth it now passes above or below it.

UCLA astrophysicist and co-author Erik Petigura compares it to eclipses.

"If the moon's orbit around the Earth was perfectly aligned with the Earth's orbit around the sun, we would see an eclipse every month," he remarked. "But because the moon's orbit is tilted, eclipses are less common. The tilt of the moon's orbit is a relic of its violent formation history, which resulted from a collision with the early Earth.".

In a recent development, that raised a bigger question. What tipped TOI-2535 b's orbit?

Timing (or the lack of it) gave it away. A planet on its own crosses its star on a steady schedule. TOI-2535 b's early and late arrivals told the team that something unseen was tugging on it.

Recent findings suggest that the researchers combined those timing clues with measurements of how the star wobbles as its planets pull on it. Everything pointed to a second planet, likely at least as massive as Saturn, circling nearby and also on a tilted orbit.

Sources indicate that nobody has seen that world, and for the same reason TOI-2535 b has gone AWOL. Its tilted path carries it above or below the star from our space telescope's vantage point, so the mystery planet never blocks any starlight that TESS can detect. But astronomers know it's there because of how hard it pulls on TOI-2535 b.

Recent findings suggest that the two planets continue to pull on each other, so their orbits wobble slowly like spinning tops. The researchers expect TOI-2535 b to swing back into view in 30 to 50 years. But its hidden neighbor may show up sooner.

According to recent reports, the pair also tells a story about the past. Astronomers have found hundreds of hot Jupiters, but these planets rarely have a massive neighbor close enough to tug on them. A violent fling couldn't have left two giant planets this close together, according to the research, so this pair likely took the scenic route.

It has been revealed that but a gentler journey should have left the two orbits lying flat. Something had to have later tipped them, though the team doesn't yet know what. This star system may reveal a rare way of forming planets.

Industry observers note that the discovery took patience. TESS's first four years of data wouldn't have been enough to reliably catch the change. As the telescope keeps watching, the researchers expect to find more planets slipping in and out of sight.

"We think of the universe as resembling clockwork, where everything is regular," Yee mentioned, "but that's not true.".

#719. Genetic variant that reshaped the human brain was inherited from Neanderthals

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (740 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

Genetic variant that reshaped the human brain was inherited from Neanderthals

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (740 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The skulls of a human (left) and a Neanderthal (right).Credit: Philippe Psaila/Science Photo Library.
  • A genetic variant that seems to reduce the size of brain areas involved in visual processing comes from an unexpected source — Neanderthals.
  • Sources indicate that geneticists have previously found fragments of Neanderthal DNA in the genomes of many modern humans, suggesting that the two species interbred in the millennia before Neanderthals died out about 40,000 years ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The skulls of a human (left) and a Neanderthal (right).Credit: Philippe Psaila/Science Photo Library.

A genetic variant that seems to reduce the size of brain areas involved in visual processing comes from an unexpected source — Neanderthals. People who carry the variant also have a reduced risk of schizophrenia.

Sources indicate that geneticists have previously found fragments of Neanderthal DNA in the genomes of many modern humans, suggesting that the two species interbred in the millennia before Neanderthals died out about 40,000 years ago. But this variant, described in a study published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA today1, has an unusually powerful effect on brain anatomy.

It has been revealed that “This is a very vital variant,” notes computational biologist Davide Marnetto at the University of Turin, Italy. “Its effect is really one of the most beautiful and strong that I’ve ever seen.”.

It has been revealed that when it comes to their brains, humans and Neanderthals have many subtle anatomical differences. Neanderthal brains were more oblong and elongated front to back, whereas modern human brains are rounder. Neanderthals also tended to have slightly larger occipital lobes — the region at the back of the brain that processes visual information.

Neanderthal-like ‘mini-brains’ created in lab with CRISPR.

Neanderthal-like ‘mini-brains’ created in lab with CRISPR.

It has been revealed that in their study, evolutionary geneticists Hugo Zeberg and Svante Pääbo at the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology in Leipzig, Germany, compared ancient DNA to data from the 1000 Genomes Project and UK BioBank, among other sources. They found evidence that a genetic variant that influences the volume of modern humans’ occipital lobes was inherited from Neanderthals.

Zeberg and Pääbo identified the variant in all five detailed Neanderthal genomes that are available to scientists, but found that it is not present in genomes of Denisovans, another extinct hominin group. In modern humans, the variant only occurs in people with non-African ancestry. It is unlikely to have been inherited from an older species that is ancestral to both humans and Neanderthals because it is found in a chunk of DNA that is 59.7 kilobases long — too massive to have survived for hundreds of thousands of years.

“This is a piece of DNA that looks like it comes from Neanderthals,” notes Zeberg.

The variant itself is a deletion of four nucleotides on chromosome 14 and was originally identified in 20192. Its effect on people’s brains is the opposite of what might be expected, say Zeberg and Pääbo. Even though Neanderthals had larger occipital lobes than humans do, this Neanderthal-derived variant is associated with a decrease in the volume of a part of the occipital lobe called the cuneus. Each copy of the variant was associated with 0.85 cubic centimetres less volume — an effect on the cuneus larger than any other known variant.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03762-0.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The University of Connecticut won its fifth men’s basketball national title with a 76-59 victory over San Diego State University on Monday night at NRG Stadium in Houston.

Senior guard Tristen Newton led UConn (31-8) with 19 points and 10 rebounds while Final Four Most Outstanding Player Adama Sanogo, a junior forward, chipped in with 17 points and 10 rebounds.

“We weren’t ranked going into the year so we had the chip on our shoulder,” UConn head coach Dan Hurley told game broadcaster CBS. “We knew the level that we could play at, even through those dark times,” he added, referencing the team’s six losses in eight games during the regular season.

He remarked going into the tournament his group had confidence garnered during the season.

“And when you have the type of leaders like Andre Jackson (game-high six assists Monday) and Adama Sanogo, they kept this team together, got us back on track and we knew we were the best team in the tournament going in and we just had to play to our level,” he added.

San Diego State (32-7) was topped by Keshad Johnson who had 14 points.

According to recent reports, UConn trailed very early but San Diego State was undone by an 11-minute, eight-second stretch in which they scored just five free throws and missed 12 consecutive shots from the field. The Huskies went from down 10-6 to up 36-24 at halftime.

The Aztecs made a run midway through the second half and narrowed the deficit to five at 60-55 with 5:19 to play but the Huskies scored the next nine to take a comfortable lead into the final two minutes.

“We battled. Battled back to five in the second half, but gave them too much separation,” San Diego State coach Brian Dutcher stated. “We had to be at our best. We weren’t at our best. A lot had to do with UConn.”.

Senior guard Adam Seiko told reporters they gave themselves a chance with their second half comeback but UConn “just made a little bit more plays” at the end.

“They have a lot of weapons. They were pretty good,” mentioned Matt Bradley, also a senior guard. “To beat them, we had to make shots. I shot poorly. And you had to have a really good game to beat those dudes on the offensive end.”.

UConn won each of its six tournament games by at least 10 points, with its closest game being a 13-point win over the University of Miami in the national semifinals.

Sources indicate that “I just want to thank my teammates, my coaches who believed in me. If it were not for them I would not be here right now,” Sanogo told CBS.

Jordan Hawkins, who scored 16 points for UConn, talked about winning the crown one day after his cousin, Angel Reese of Louisiana State University, won the women’s title.

“I mean it’s absolutely amazing that we both get this opportunity and I mean the family reunion is going to be great so that’s all I know,” he stated.

In a recent development, UConn enters rarefied air as only the sixth team to win five NCAA men’s basketball championships, joining UCLA (11), Kentucky (eight), North Carolina (six), Duke (five) and Indiana (five). All of UConn’s titles have come since 1999 with the most recent before Monday occurring in 2014.

UConn’s women’s teams have won 11 basketball national titles.

CNN’s Steve Almasy and Issy Ronald contributed to this report.

'Don't panic': SpaceX pens familiar message on Starship ahead of historic double-catch test flight

💡 Key Takeaways
  • SpaceX has a message for itself, and for the spacecraft set to make history today (Nov.
  • The tech giant's Starship megarocket will conduct its 15th test flight this afternoon, a landmark liftoff that will feature the first-ever attempt to catch both of its stages with its launch tower's "chopstick" arms.
  • Industry observers note that on Thursday (Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SpaceX has a message for itself, and for the spacecraft set to make history today (Nov. 13): Don't panic.

The tech giant's Starship megarocket will conduct its 15th test flight this afternoon, a landmark liftoff that will feature the first-ever attempt to catch both of its stages with its launch tower's "chopstick" arms.

Industry observers note that on Thursday (Nov. 12), SpaceX rolled the Flight 15 upper stage, a vehicle known as Ship 42, out to the launch pad at its Starbase site in South Texas to prep. The company shared photos of the move on X, and in two of those shots we can see some intriguing words inked on the spacecraft: "Don't panic.".

The phrase is familiar to fans of Douglas Adams' sci-fi classic "The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy": In the novel, the electronic guidebook that helps travelers find their way across the cosmos has "Don't panic!" on its cover.

Sources indicate that and Ship 42 itself is connected to the beloved book, by virtue of its serial number. In "The Hitchhiker's Guide," a supercomputer named Deep Mind is asked to come up with "the answer to the ultimate question of life, the universe, and everything." It thinks for 7.5 million years and comes up with "42.".

SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk has voiced his affection for "The Hitchhiker's Guide" in the past — and he has already paid tribute to it with a well-placed "Don't panic.".

The debut launch of SpaceX's Falcon Heavy rocket back in February 2018 sent Musk's red Tesla Roadster into orbit around the sun, with a spacesuit-clad mannequin named Starman at the wheel and its entertainment display programmed to read "Don't panic!".

Starship Flight 15 is scheduled to launch today during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT; 4:45 p.m. local Texas time). You can watch it here at Space.com.

If all goes according to proposal, Starship's Super Heavy first stage will come back to Starbase for a chopsticks catch about 6.5 minutes after liftoff.

It has been revealed that ship 42, meanwhile, will head to orbit, a destination that Starship reached for the first time on Flight 14, which took place on Sept. 28. Ship 42 will deploy 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites today — the second batch of the spacecraft to reach orbit. (The first set of 26 were delivered on Flight 14).

Industry observers note that ship 42 will stay up for a while after that, circling Earth 14 times before coming back for its own chopsticks catch on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), 22.5 hours after launch.

According to recent reports, that's the plan, anyway; SpaceX will only go through with a Ship catch attempt if all systems on the vehicle look good. If there are any problems, the company will divert to a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean, near either Hawaii or Chile.

Both of Starship's stages — Super Heavy and the Ship — are designed to be rapidly reusable. And "rapidly" is a bit of understatement: SpaceX wants to launch 10,000 Starship missions per year by 2030, Musk has said.

Recent findings suggest that the chopsticks-catch strategy is a massive part of that vision. Bringing both Starship stages directly back to the launch mount will greatly reduce the time needed for inspection, refurbishment and reflight, according to SpaceX.

The company has already caught Super Heavy on three previous Starship test flights. It has never tried to do so with Ship, instead targeting ocean splashdowns with the upper stage.

The double catch attempt may be unprecedented, but SpaceX seems to be taking its own advice: There's no panic around Flight 15 or its bold goals.

"I'd say it's more likely than not that this succeeds next flight," Musk remarked last month, during SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call.

In a recent development, in the first quarter of the game, which was played in Germany, Hutchinson sacked Patriots quarterback Drake Maye. The play, however, would prove disastrous for both players.

After the collision, Hutchinson leapt into the air in celebration. As he landed, however, the 26-year-old’s right knee buckled beneath him, and he collapsed to the ground. Though he was able to walk off the field with the assistance of the Lions’ training staff, Hutchinson didn’t return to the game. The NFL Network Insider’s Ian Rapoport later confirmed on Nov. 16 that the player had torn his ACL, cutting his season short.

As for Maye, Rapoport also shared an enhancement on the Patriots’ star, confirming the 24-year-old suffered a “significant lower leg injury,” believed to be a fractured ankle, during the sack. According to Rapoport, the injury could mean the 2025 NFL MVP runner-up is also out for the rest of the Patriots’ season.

“He is good spirits,” the coach shared following the match up against the Patriots. “And he continues to get better every day.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • MARYSVILLE, Ohio — Honda Motor plans to invest $3 billion to build a new vehicle assembly plant in Ohio, the automaker confirmed Monday.
  • Honda said the fresh plant, which will be near its other facilities in Marysville, Ohio, is expected to begin production in 2029, have a capacity for 240,000 vehicles annually and create more than 2,000 jobs.
  • The facility is expected to be capable of producing traditional vehicles with internal combustion engines, all-electric vehicles and hybrid models, which have been growing in popularity in the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

MARYSVILLE, Ohio — Honda Motor plans to invest $3 billion to build a new vehicle assembly plant in Ohio, the automaker confirmed Monday.

Honda said the fresh plant, which will be near its other facilities in Marysville, Ohio, is expected to begin production in 2029, have a capacity for 240,000 vehicles annually and create more than 2,000 jobs.

The facility is expected to be capable of producing traditional vehicles with internal combustion engines, all-electric vehicles and hybrid models, which have been growing in popularity in the U.S.

Honda declined to disclose what vehicles the firm looks to produce at the new facility.

The plant is expected to increase Honda's light-duty vehicle capacity to 1.3 million units annually in the U.S. It right now has 12 manufacturing plants in United States, eight of which produce engines or light-duty vehicles for the auto industry.

Industry observers note that "This is not simply an investment in another plant. It is an investment in the future of Honda manufacturing in America," Bob Nelson, executive vice president of American Honda Motor, remarked during the announcement at the tech giant's U.S. heritage center in Ohio.

The auto industry has been trying to localize more production amid President Donald Trump's tariffs and inflated logistics costs that have cut into profits.

Nelson told CNBC after the event that tariffs are affecting the manufacturer's business but the new plant is more about Honda's ambitions to grow in the U.S.

According to recent reports, "Tariffs are an impact to us, even with the high localization rate that we have," he said. "But the real impact is that we have customers out there wanting Honda product and we can't give it to them. That's the real area.".

Nelson stated Honda did not work with the Trump administration ahead of Monday's announcement.

Honda's plans for a newly introduced plant come roughly two weeks after Volkswagen-owned luxury brand Audi unveiled it would invest more than $4 billion in a new plant at a rally with President Donald Trump, which Audi CEO Gernot Dollner faced criticism for attending.

Honda's fresh plant is the tech giant's first new mass production U.S. vehicle assembly plant since it opened a facility in Indiana in 2008. It also opened a $70 million performance vehicle facility in 2016 and a multibillion-dollar joint venture battery plant earlier this year, both in Ohio.

According to recent reports, the announcement comes after the automaker in May indefinitely suspended an $11 billion investment plan to produce all-electric vehicles and batteries in Canada. It also canceled three planned EVs for the U.S. market.

American Honda Motor Co. executive Jennifer Thomas recently emphasized the Japanese automaker's commitment to the U.S. and need for additional capacity.

"In order to be competitive in this market, you're going to need to build products here," Thomas, senior vice president of corporate affairs, mentioned Oct. 27 in Detroit. "We are focused on trying to maximize the existing capacity that we have, but we are at capacity, and so we're exploring all options.".

It has been revealed that thomas also warned the automotive industry faces a "catastrophic" scenario if the U.S. and Canada cannot reach a latest trade deal by the end of this year, when Trump has threatened to double tariffs on Canadian vehicles and parts from 25% to 50% on Jan. 1 if the two countries don't reach a deal.

According to recent reports, honda stated it has built more than 33 million vehicles and more than 39 million engines in the U.S. since it started auto production in the U.S. in 1982.

The Japanese automaker presently has more than 30,000 employees in the U.S.
